body.translated_text: <s>Bodhasāra</s> (The Essence of Knowledge)

children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. With some curiosity, and out of a desire to please the learned,
having performed the auspicious invocation, the <s>Bodhasāra</s> is set forth. [NBs 1.1]
We worship <s>Gaṇarāja</s> [<s>Gaṇeśa</s>], the power that destroys obstacles,
of the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) who is replete with infinite powers. [NBs 1.2]
She who abides in her own nature through illumination (<s>prakāśa</s>) and reflection (<s>vimarśa</s>) —

children.text: smarāmi tāmahaṃ bhaktyā jñānaśaktiṃ sarasvatīm // NBs_1.3 //
children.translated_text: I remember with devotion that power of knowledge, <s>Sarasvatī</s>. [NBs 1.3]
I salute the revered teachers (<s>guru</s>s), whose nature is supreme bliss,
whose grace removes the threefold suffering and is a fountain of the nectar of <s>Brahman</s>. [NBs 1.4]
Now the praise of the <s>Guru</s>.
Salutation to the revered <s>Guru-Viṣṇu</s>, who conquers the cruel [demons] <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s> named intoxication and delusion,
and who is the abode of the <s>Lakṣmī</s> of liberation. [NBs 1.5]
<s>Hari</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Hara</s> — these three have attained eminence through qualities;
but our teachers have attained the state of weightiness by transcending qualities. [NBs 1.6]
<s>Rudra</s> destroys the demon of the [three] cities; <s>Hari</s> destroys <s>Kaṃsa</s> and <s>Keśi</s>;
<s>Caṇḍī</s> destroys <s>Caṇḍa</s> and <s>Muṇḍa</s>; but the <s>Guru</s> destroys all dualities. [NBs 1.7]
When pleased, the deities grant wealth, longevity, sons, and fame;

children.text: jñānaṃ ke nāma dāsyanti vinā śrīgurupādukām // NBs_1.8 //
children.translated_text: who indeed will grant knowledge without the sandals of the revered <s>Guru</s>? [NBs 1.8]
Victorious is the quality of the dust of the lotus-feet of the revered <s>Guru</s>s —
by that single [dust], the three <s>guṇa</s>s — <s>rajas</s>, <s>sattva</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — are destroyed. [NBs 1.9]
We are to be ferried across; knowledge is the ferry; the ocean of worldly existence is to be crossed —
I worship the revered <s>Guru</s>, the deliverer, in the form of the helmsman. [NBs 1.10]
By the instruction of the <s>Tāraka</s> [mantra], the <s>Guru</s>, having become [the means], grants liberation;
even in <s>Kāśī</s>, it is <s>Īśvara</s> [who teaches]; therefore the <s>Guru</s> is greater than <s>Īśvara</s>. [NBs 1.11]
By the grace of the <s>Guru</s>, [one sees] <s>Īśvara</s>; by the grace of <s>Īśvara</s>, [one finds] a <s>Guru</s>;
the vision of the revered <s>Guru</s> is the cause; but in [attaining] the vision of <s>Īśvara</s>, it is supreme. [NBs 1.12]
<s>Īśvara</s>, being the cause of all, is the cause of both <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly bondage) and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation);

children.text: mokṣasyaiva gurustasmānnāsti tatvaṃ guroḥ param // NBs_1.13 //
children.translated_text: but the <s>Guru</s> is [the cause] of liberation alone; therefore there is no truth higher than the <s>Guru</s>. [NBs 1.13]
Even without the greatness of a [sacred] place, through the greatness of the <s>Guru</s> indeed,

children.text: vimuktiryatra kutrāpi na kāśyāṃ guruṇā vinā // NBs_1.14 //
children.translated_text: liberation [is possible] anywhere whatsoever; but not in <s>Kāśī</s> without a <s>Guru</s>. [NBs 1.14]
Why should one say 'forgive me'? Why should one say 'be gracious'?
My <s>Guru</s> is full of forgiveness and grace by his very nature. [NBs 1.15]
Now the discrimination regarding the disciple.
The <s>Guru</s>'s instruction is indeed the seed; the seeker (<s>jijñāsu</s>) is called the field;
the tree of knowledge, born from the sprout of discrimination — <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) is its fruit. [NBs 2.1]
Although without the field and the seed, there is no arising of a tree,

children.text: kiṃ tu bījamupādānaṃ nimittaṃ kṣetramucyate // NBs_2.2 //
children.translated_text: yet the seed is the material cause, while the field is called the efficient cause. [NBs 2.2]
The tree is a transformation of the seed, not a transformation of the field;
knowledge is a transformation of the <s>Guru</s>, not a transformation of the disciple. [NBs 2.3]

children.text: drumo hi bījajātīyaḥ kṣetrajātīyako na hi /
children.translated_text: The tree is of the same species as the seed, not of the same species as the field;

children.text: bodho hi gurujātīyaḥ śiṣyajātīyako na hi // NBs_2.4 //
children.translated_text: knowledge is of the same species as the <s>Guru</s>, not of the same species as the disciple. [NBs 2.4]
By the seed, a tree of the same species as the seed is placed in the field;

children.text: guruṇā svātmajātīyo bodhaḥ śiṣye samarpitaḥ // NBs_2.5 //
children.translated_text: by the <s>Guru</s>, knowledge of his own nature is placed in the disciple. [NBs 2.5]

children.text: vahniprabhā hi varttisthā tamo hanti prakāśate /
children.translated_text: The radiance of fire, situated in the wick, destroys darkness and illuminates;

children.text: tamohantrī prakāśātmā prabhaiva na tu varttikā // NBs_2.6 //
children.translated_text: the destroyer of darkness, whose nature is illumination, is the radiance itself, not the wick. [NBs 2.6]

children.text: guruprabhā hi śiṣyasthā tamo hanti prakāśate /
children.translated_text: The radiance of the <s>Guru</s>, situated in the disciple, destroys darkness and illuminates;

children.text: tamohantā prakāśātmā gurureva na śiṣyakaḥ // NBs_2.7 //
children.translated_text: the destroyer of darkness, whose nature is illumination, is the <s>Guru</s> alone, not the disciple. [NBs 2.7]
When fire, having mounted wood, reduces a city to ashes,

children.text: bhasmāsātkāraṇaṃ tatra guṇo vahnerna kāṣṭhagaḥ // NBs_2.8 //
children.translated_text: the cause of that incineration is a quality of the fire, not [a quality] belonging to the wood. [NBs 2.8]
The <s>Guru</s>, in the form of knowledge, enters the disciple and instantly burns

children.text: yaddvaitaṃ sā guroḥ śaktirna śiṣyasyeti nirṇayaḥ // NBs_2.9 //
children.translated_text: whatever duality [remains] — that is the power of the <s>Guru</s>, not of the disciple: this is the conclusion. [NBs 2.9]
Although at sunrise a lotus blooms,

children.text: na kāśante tathā padmāḥ kāṣṭhapāṣāṇamṛṇmayāḥ // NBs_2.10 //
children.translated_text: lotuses made of wood, stone, or clay do not likewise shine. [NBs 2.10]
Just as the illuminating sun would cause only the [real] lotus to bloom,
so the <s>Guru</s>, the awakener, would awaken only the [true] disciple. [NBs 2.11]
The greatness of the illuminator is indeed greater than that of the illuminated;

children.text: sūkṣmaṃ viśeṣaṃ vakṣyāmi gurusūryasya taṃ śṛṇu // NBs_2.12 //
children.translated_text: I shall state the subtle distinction — listen to this [comparison] of the <s>Guru</s> and the sun. [NBs 2.12]
Through discrimination, dispassion, and Vedāntic reasoning on the respective [topics],

children.text: śiṣyaṃ nayati gurvarkaḥ svaikyaṃ svādbhinnamapyaho // NBs_2.13 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Guru</s>-sun leads the disciple — who is different from himself — to unity with himself: how wondrous! [NBs 2.13]

children.text: vikāsako'pi tapano na padmaṃ svaikatāṃ nayet /
children.translated_text: Though the sun causes blooming, it does not lead the lotus to unity with itself;
therefore the sandals of the revered <s>Guru</s> should be served with the attitude of complete identification. [NBs 2.14]

children.text: tatsatyaṃ dātṛpātrābhyāṃ vinā dānaṃ na siddhyati /
children.translated_text: It is true that without both giver and recipient, a gift is not accomplished;

children.text: tathāpi pātraṃ pātraṃ syāddātā paramakāraṇam // NBs_2.15 //
children.translated_text: yet the recipient is [merely] a recipient, while the giver is the supreme cause. [NBs 2.15]
By the touch of the philosopher's stone, iron becomes gold, but not [the reverse —] the stone;
by the touch of the <s>Guru</s>-philosopher's-stone, [the disciple] becomes that [<s>Brahman</s>] in an instant. [NBs 2.16]
Thus, through discrimination, O wise one, both are useful;
but the disciple is merely an instrumental cause — the sandals of the <s>Guru</s> are supreme. [NBs 2.17]
'O <s>Rāma</s>, the sequence of instruction is merely a maintenance of convention' —
such statements are for the purpose of increasing the enthusiasm of the disciple. [NBs 2.18]
The established conclusion of all systems, which produces immediate conviction,
should always be contemplated — this determination regarding <s>Guru</s> and disciple. [NBs 2.19]
The inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>.
Now therefore the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>: <s>Brahman</s> alone is to be inquired into,
by its accidental definition (<s>taṭasthalakṣaṇa</s>) and by the definition of its essential nature (<s>svarūpalakṣaṇa</s>). [NBs 3.1]
<s>Īśvara</s> is the root cause of creation, sustenance, and destruction;
omniscient, of true resolve — and so forth: this is the accidental definition. [NBs 3.2]
Its nature is <s>Sat-Cit-Ānanda</s> (existence-consciousness-bliss), self-luminous, the supreme beyond the supreme,
neither minute nor [gross] — and so forth as stated in the <s>Veda</s>s: this is the definition of its essential nature. [NBs 3.3]
Whatever is required in the relation of attribute and principal —
all of that is expounded under the pretext of various topics. [NBs 3.4]
The sequence of external and internal means [of knowledge] —
that which is more internal is set forth later. [NBs 3.5]
The section on the foundation of dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>).
First hear the section on the foundation of dispassion, O wise one;

children.text: na nemireva yatrāsti sthitiścakrasya kīdṛśī // NBs_4,1.1 //
children.translated_text: where there is not even the rim, what stability can the wheel have? [NBs 4.1.1]
A <s>śūdra</s> has no Vedic initiation; there is no oil in sand;

children.text: na syātkaratale roma tathā muktirna rāgiṇi // NBs_4,1.2 //
children.translated_text: there is no hair on the palm — so too there is no liberation for one with attachment. [NBs 4.1.2]
Dispassion is twofold — understand its subtle division:
one is primarily characterized by the desire to inquire (<s>jijñāsā</s>), and the other by the desire to abandon (<s>jihāsā</s>). [NBs 4.1.3]
The desire to abandon <s>saṃsāra</s> and the desire to inquire into <s>Brahman</s> — these two, O sage,

children.text: ekameva tathāpyasti viśeṣaḥ kaścidatra hi // NBs_4,1.4 //
children.translated_text: are indeed one; yet there is some distinction here. [NBs 4.1.4]
Those fallen from royal power, those with long illness, those dependent on others, those whose fortune is destroyed —
those who become dispassionate and practice austerity — that is indeed dispassion primarily of the abandoning type. [NBs 4.1.5]
Those free from mental affliction, physical disease, fear, anxiety, and dependence —

children.text: ye dhīrā muktimicchanti śṛṇu teṣāmayaṃ kramaḥ // NBs_4,1.6 //
children.translated_text: those steadfast ones who desire liberation — hear this sequence for them. [NBs 4.1.6]
Those in whose home is the wish-fulfilling cow, who dwell in the <s>Nandana</s> garden,
<s>Kaśyapa</s> and others practice austerity — that is indeed dispassion primarily of the inquiry type. [NBs 4.1.7]
Those afflicted by mental anguish, physical disease, fear, anxiety, dependence, and the like —

children.text: ye jīvā mokṣamicchanti jihāsāmukhyatā tu sā // NBs_4,1.8 //
children.translated_text: those beings who desire liberation — that is [dispassion] primarily of the abandoning type. [NBs 4.1.8]

children.text: mānuṣyaṃ durlabhaṃ prāptaṃ sacchāstraiḥ saṃskṛtā matiḥ /
children.translated_text: Human birth, difficult to obtain, has been obtained; the intellect has been refined by true scriptures;
if there is no resting in <s>Brahman</s>, then what have we achieved? [NBs 4.1.9]
With such determination, like the [unexpected] falling of fruit from the sky,

children.text: jijñāsayanti ye dhīrā jijñāsāmukhyatā tu sā // NBs_4,1.10 //
children.translated_text: those steadfast ones who inquire — that is indeed dispassion primarily of the inquiry type. [NBs 4.1.10]
<s>Virocana</s>, <s>Kārttavīrya</s>, <s>Bali</s>, <s>Śrī Rāghava</s> [<s>Rāma</s>], and others,

children.text: viraktā rājalīlāyāṃ te hi tatra nidarśanam // NBs_4,1.11 //
children.translated_text: who became dispassionate toward the sport of kingship — they are the examples of this. [NBs 4.1.11]
If from intense dispassion toward <s>saṃsāra</s>, inquiry into <s>Brahman</s> [arises],
that dispassion of meritorious beings is indeed primarily of the abandoning type. [NBs 4.1.12]
O dear one, the detachment from visible objects that is effected
by intense desire to inquire into <s>Brahman</s> — that is indeed primarily of the inquiry type. [NBs 4.1.13]

children.text: sahajaṃ yasya vairāgyaṃ kā vācyā tasya mukhyatā /
children.translated_text: For one whose dispassion is innate, what need to speak of its primacy?

children.text: atha doṣāḥ pradarśyante vairāgyaṃ doṣadarśanāt // NBs_4,1.14 //
children.translated_text: Now faults are displayed; dispassion [comes] from seeing faults. [NBs 4.1.14]
I shall state briefly — listen with attentive mind,
O virtuous one, beginning with the absurdity of the body. [NBs 4.1.15]
The mockery of the body.
This body, which they adorn with gold, garments, and sandalwood —
only through lack of examination has it come to be considered beautiful. [NBs 4.2.1]
This body — food for the corpse-eater, fuel for fire,
emaciated by [its own] transformations — wherein lies its beauty? [NBs 4.2.2]
This is the very abode of <s>Kali</s> (the age of strife); this embodied form is conflict incarnate;

children.text: pañcabhūtanivāso'yaṃ kathaṃ tatra sukhī bhavet // NBs_4,2.3 //
children.translated_text: this is the dwelling-place of the five elements — how can one be happy therein? [NBs 4.2.3]
The prison is the womb; infancy is sheer stupidity;
and even there, existence is utterly unbearable because of dependence on others. [NBs 4.2.4]
Where there is torment by the arrows of desire, the fever of separation from the beloved,
an abundance of sinful tendencies — youth is a forest of calamities. [NBs 4.2.5]
Formerly erect, now brought low; gray with the alkaline [wash] of old age;
resembling an old pumpkin — the body of the aged is contemptible. [NBs 4.2.6]

children.text: maraṇasya tu kiṃ vācyaṃ mṛtyudūtabhayaṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: As for death, what need be said? Thereafter comes the fear of <s>Yama</s>'s messengers;

children.text: narake tu mahadduḥkhaṃ svarge patanajaṃ bhayam // NBs_4,2.7 //
children.translated_text: in hell, great suffering; in heaven, the fear born of [eventual] falling. [NBs 4.2.7]
Even there, through the distinction of high and low, there is mockery;

children.text: yadi paśvādiyoniḥ syāttadā duḥkhasya kā kathā // NBs_4,2.8 //
children.translated_text: and if one should obtain birth as an animal or the like, then what words can describe the suffering? [NBs 4.2.8]
Birth again, death again, suffering again, fear again —

children.text: na jānāti gatiṃ janturnimagno mohasāgare // NBs_4,2.9 //
children.translated_text: the creature, submerged in the ocean of delusion, does not know its course. [NBs 4.2.9]
The mockery of livelihood.

children.text: kṣatradharme parā hiṃsā yācñāyāṃ lāghavaṃ mahat /
children.translated_text: In the warrior's duty, the highest sin is violence; in begging, the greatest degradation;
in commerce, nothing but falsehood — there is no sin greater than untruth. [NBs 4.3.1]
In service, the utmost hardship; the farmer is a worm of the earth;

children.text: dyūte sarvasvanāśaḥ syāccaurye rājabhayaṃ mahat // NBs_4,3.2 //
children.translated_text: in gambling, the loss of everything; in thievery, great fear of the king. [NBs 4.3.2]

body.translated_text: Wealth does not fall from the sky — how then can livelihood be a source of happiness?

children.translated_text: The mockery of desire.
When the life-breath departs, goblins chew the great flesh;
while alive, men and women, the four-faced ones, chew each other's flesh. [NBs 4.4.1]
At night, goblins dance with human bodies in cremation grounds;
householders [dance] in their homes with various postures of the limbs. [NBs 4.4.2]
Deluded, one licks, touches, repeatedly smells, and devours —
this practice of sensual conduct is fitting for a village-lion [a lustful person]. [NBs 4.4.3]
Is the pleasure of scratching an itch truly pleasure?

children.text: paścādyatra mahāpīḍā tathā vaiṣayikaṃ sukham // NBs_4,4.4 //
children.translated_text: Where great pain follows — such is the pleasure of sense-objects. [NBs 4.4.4]
A hunter pierces with sharp arrows the deer attached to sound;
a woman [pierces] repeatedly with the dagger of sexual union the man attached to form. [NBs 4.4.5]
The mockery of anger.

children.text: rudhiraṃ pibati svīyaṃ divā tamasi nṛtyati /
children.translated_text: He drinks his own blood, dances in darkness by day;

children.text: bhīṣayatyātmanātmānaṃ krūraḥ krodhī na rākṣasaḥ // NBs_4,5.1 //
children.translated_text: the cruel angry person frightens himself by himself — he is not a demon. [NBs 4.5.1]
The mockery of greed.

children.text: na piśācā na ḍākinyo na bhujaṅgā na vṛścikāḥ /
children.translated_text: Neither goblins, nor <s>ḍākinī</s>s, nor serpents, nor scorpions

children.text: saṃbhrāntayanti manujaṃ yathā lobho dhiyaṃ ripuḥ // NBs_4,6.1 //
children.translated_text: throw a man into confusion as does greed, the enemy of wisdom. [NBs 4.6.1]
The <s>Meru</s> mountains appear like drops of ghee in the wildfire of insatiable desire;
how then can the greedy person be satisfied by thousands and millions? [NBs 4.6.2]
Sleepless, from early morning he keeps awake even in dreams;

children.text: bhramanno labhate śāntiṃ sa lobhasya parākramaḥ // NBs_4,6.3 //
children.translated_text: wandering, he finds no peace — such is the prowess of greed. [NBs 4.6.3]
Treasures that <s>Yakṣa</s>s, serpents, and others guard with great effort —

children.text: na pibanti na khādanti teṣāṃ hi guravaḥ śaṭhāḥ // NBs_4,6.4 //
children.translated_text: they neither drink nor eat them; their teachers in this are the miserly. [NBs 4.6.4]
The wealth of a wealthy person that is devoid of giving and enjoyment —

children.text: na tu tasya mukhe dhūlirdīyate bhūmigopanaiḥ // NBs_4,6.5 //
children.translated_text: the earth-hiders [who guard it] do not even give dust to his mouth. [NBs 4.6.5]
The fool — does he store his wealth in a copper vessel?

children.text: pātre sthitaṃ dhanaṃ bhadraṃ kintu pātraṃ parīkṣaya // NBs_4,6.6 //
children.translated_text: It is good that wealth is placed in a vessel — but examine the vessel! [NBs 4.6.6]
For the sake of wealth [worthless as] crow-droppings, with great bodily toil,

children.text: madāndhā dhaninaḥ sevyā mahatīyaṃ viḍambanā // NBs_4,6.7 //
children.translated_text: the intoxicated wealthy are served — what a great mockery this is! [NBs 4.6.7]
Gems, mantras, herbs, and the like are no remedy for greed;
even the one who praises gems, mantras, and herbs is himself devoted to greed. [NBs 4.6.8]
Meditating upon some tiny morsel of wealth, you look at the face of the rich man

children.text: karoṣi śveva cāṭūni lobhenāpakṛtaṃ smara // NBs_4,6.9 //
children.translated_text: and fawn like a dog — remember the harm done by greed! [NBs 4.6.9]
With an iron bolt, it steals what is good; with the mark of fickleness, it gives fear;

children.text: lunātyubhau ca yallokau tena lobhaḥ prakīrttitaḥ // NBs_4,6.10 //
children.translated_text: because it ruins both worlds, it is called <s>lobha</s> (greed). [NBs 4.6.10]
Those with desires are greedy for women; the desireless are greedy for liberation;
the Lord is greedy for devotion — one truly without greed is extremely rare. [NBs 4.6.11]
Though the bed shines white with milk-foam, and a young wife attends his feet,

children.text: nidrāṃ na labhate bhūpaḥ pararāṣṭrajigīṣayā // NBs_4,6.12 //
children.translated_text: the king does not obtain sleep — out of desire to conquer another's kingdom. [NBs 4.6.12]

children.text: mārgeṣu militāścaurāḥ sakhyaṃ taiḥ saha vardhitam /
children.translated_text: Thieves are encountered on the roads; friendship with them is cultivated;

children.text: te gatā dhanamādāya paścācchocati mandadhīḥ // NBs_4,6.13 //
children.translated_text: they depart taking the wealth — afterward the dull-witted one grieves. [NBs 4.6.13]
The master guards his property here and there like a thief;
wife, sons, and others, like thieves, enjoy [it] as if they were the master. [NBs 4.6.14]
The wealth that people hide from sons, friends, and wives —

children.text: tena manye'vanaṃ pāpaṃ sukṛtyā gopyate nahi // NBs_4,6.15 //
children.translated_text: by that, I think, only sin is guarded, for merit is not hidden. [NBs 4.6.15]

children.text: rāgiṇī gaṇikā vittaṃ yadvāñchati varā hi sā /
children.translated_text: The courtesan who is passionate and desires wealth — she is indeed excellent;
shame on the one who preaches dispassion yet is garrulous and lusting after wealth! [NBs 4.6.16]
Taking wealth from the rich, the scripture-reciter boasts —

children.text: bahubhyo mithunībhūya dhanibhyo gaṇikā yathā // NBs_4,6.17 //
children.translated_text: like a courtesan who pairs with many wealthy [patrons]. [NBs 4.6.17]
This greedy expounder of <s>Vedānta</s> does not shine

children.text: cauryeṇa nigaḍe datto jaṭābhasmadharo yathā // NBs_4,6.18 //
children.translated_text: any more than one wearing matted hair and ashes who is put in fetters for theft. [NBs 4.6.18]
If the learned gain respect only by earning wealth,
then tell me — what is the difference between a courtesan and a scholar? [NBs 4.6.19]

children.text: anityamiti yo vakti sevate nityameva tat /
children.translated_text: He who says 'it is impermanent' yet constantly serves that very [impermanent thing] —

children.text: bahirmukhasya tasyāsyaṃ mā darśaya maheśvara // NBs_4,6.20 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Maheśvara</s>, do not show the face of that outward-facing one! [NBs 4.6.20]
Having become servants of desire, the desirous are servants of all;

children.text: kāmenaiva parityakto niṣkāmaḥ kasya kiṃkaraḥ // NBs_4,6.21 //
children.translated_text: one who is abandoned even by desire and is desireless — whose servant is he? [NBs 4.6.21]
The Mockery of Action
Like a bamboo vessel that is never filled even by hundreds of pots,

children.text: kriyājālaṃ kathaṃ sādho virāgāya na jāyate // NBs_4,7.1 //
children.translated_text: how is it, O good one, that the net of rituals does not give rise to dispassion? [NBs 4.7.1]
From the beginning of <s>Brahmā</s>'s day until now, rituals have been performed,

children.text: muhūrttaṃ hanta saṃsārī naiva niścintatāṅgataḥ // NBs_4,7.2 //
children.translated_text: yet alas, the one bound in <s>saṃsāra</s> has not been free from anxiety for even a moment! [NBs 4.7.2]
The supreme misfortune of men is living off another's food-offering;
how then is living off a son's food-offering considered good fortune? [NBs 4.7.3]
Addressing with the word 'dead,' offering a ball of food for the dead on the death-day
to the dead — will a son give [this]? How much better than immortality is that? [NBs 4.7.4]

children.text: aśanāyāṃ pipāsāṃ ca śokaṃ mohaṃ jarāṃ mṛtim /
children.translated_text: Experiencing hunger, thirst, sorrow, delusion, old age, and death —
do not, through scripture and <s>śāstra</s>, become an eater of funeral offerings! [NBs 4.7.5]
Long life is for the experience of old age; abundant wealth is for anxiety;
sons are for the suffering of quarrels — astonishing is the suffering in <s>saṃsāra</s>! [NBs 4.7.6]

children.text: chāyāṃ paśyati kāyasya rāyo garveṇa muhyati /
children.translated_text: He sees the shadow of the body, is deluded by pride of wealth,

children.text: jāyāṃ bhajati bhāvena māyāṃ no veda vaiṣṇavīm // NBs_4,7.7 //
children.translated_text: devotes himself to his wife with passion — and does not know the <s>māyā</s> (illusion) of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. [NBs 4.7.7]
Regarding cattle, sons, and wives — who come and go without being planned, like a meeting on a journey —

children.text: paśuputrakalatrādau mamatā na matā samā // NBs_4,7.8 //
children.translated_text: possessiveness (<s>mamatā</s>) is not considered equal [to wisdom]. [NBs 4.7.8]
Our teachers, the best of grammarians, are truly excellent —

children.text: ādiśya mamatāsthāne samatāṃ sādhayanti ye // NBs_4,7.9 //
children.translated_text: they who, prescribing in the place of 'mine-ness' (<s>mamatā</s>), teach 'sameness' (<s>samatā</s>). [NBs 4.7.9]

children.text: tyakṣyaṃtyavaśyaṃ ca tvāntvaṃ ca tyakṣyasi yānapi /
children.translated_text: They will certainly leave you, and you too will leave those [things];

children.text: yeṣāṃ tyāge mahatsaukhyaṃ teṣāṃ tyāge'pi kaḥ śramaḥ // NBs_4,7.10 //
children.translated_text: when there is great happiness in their renunciation, what effort is there in giving them up? [NBs 4.7.10]
For those deluded by worldly dealings, the course consists of praise and blame;
and that too lasts only as long as the body — and the body, how many days does it last? [NBs 4.7.11]
On one hand, all the people pull according to their strength;
on the other, powerful Time alone swallows the entire chain of objects. [NBs 4.7.12]
Fickle is <s>Lakṣmī</s> (wealth), fickle are we, fickle are the activities of the senses;

children.text: kiṃ sukhaṃ tatra yatrāṅga jīvanasyaiva saṃśayaḥ // NBs_4,7.13 //
children.translated_text: where, O friend, is happiness when even life itself is in doubt? [NBs 4.7.13]
Grief, delusion, fear, wretchedness, mental affliction, bodily disease, hunger, thirst —
thus is the varied suffering described in brief. [NBs 4.7.14]
The Inquiry into <s>Dharma</s>
Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>dharma</s>. <s>Dharma</s> is declared to be fourfold:

children.text: nityo naimittikaḥ kāmyaḥ prāyaścittamiti kramāt // NBs_5,1.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>nitya</s> (daily obligatory), <s>naimittika</s> (occasional), <s>kāmya</s> (desire-prompted), and <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiatory) — in order. [NBs 5.1.1]
The observances of one's <s>varṇa</s> (class) and <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life) — purity, bathing, and the rest —

children.text: āvaśyakāste nityāḥ syurakṛtya pratyavaiti yān // NBs_5,1.2 //
children.translated_text: those that are obligatory are <s>nitya</s>; one who fails to perform them incurs fault. [NBs 5.1.2]

children.text: deśakālanimittā ye te tu naimittikāḥ smṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those that are occasioned by place, time, and cause are called <s>naimittika</s> —
bathing, giving, funeral rites, and recitation on occasions such as <s>saṃkrānti</s> (solstice) and eclipses. [NBs 5.1.3]
Expiatory <s>dharmas</s> are <s>kṛcchra</s>, <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>, and the like;
<s>kāmya</s> (desire-prompted) duties are preceded by desire and are not enjoined for the one seeking liberation. [NBs 5.1.4]
The desire for the grace of <s>Hari</s>, the desire for purification of the mind,

children.text: mokṣasya kāmanā ceti kāmaneyaṃ na kāmanā // NBs_5,1.5 //
children.translated_text: and the desire for <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) — this kind of desire is not [really] desire. [NBs 5.1.5]
Therefore, with that desire, bathing, giving, recitation, and the like,
commitment to holy places, vows, and austerity should be performed by those seeking liberation. [NBs 5.1.6]
The determination regarding actions is stated thus by <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) in the <s>Gītā</s>:

children.text: sarvathā na parityājyaṃ nityaṃ karma mumukṣuṇā // NBs_5,1.7 //
children.translated_text: the <s>nitya</s> (obligatory) <s>karma</s> should by no means be abandoned by the seeker of liberation. [NBs 5.1.7]
Even after knowledge has arisen, it should not be abandoned — for the sake of benefiting the world;

children.text: yo vāsanāparityāgaḥ karmatyāgaḥ sa evahi // NBs_5,1.8 //
children.translated_text: the abandonment of mental tendencies (<s>vāsanā</s>) is indeed the true abandonment of action. [NBs 5.1.8]
There is no [true] abandonment of actions — the abandonment of action is mental;

children.text: yajño dānaṃ tapaśceti pāvanāni manīṣiṇām // NBs_5,1.9 //
children.translated_text: sacrifice, giving, and austerity are purifiers for the wise. [NBs 5.1.9]
Through action comes purification of the mind; from that, intense desire for liberation;

children.text: tato vivekānmuktiḥ syātkarma tyājyaṃ kathaṃ tu tat // NBs_5,1.10 //
children.translated_text: then, through discrimination, liberation arises — how then should that action be abandoned? [NBs 5.1.10]

children.text: ye tu bodhena saṃprāptāstāta karmātigāṃ daśām /
children.translated_text: But those who, through awakening, O dear one, have attained the state beyond action —

children.text: na vidheḥ kiṃkarāstasmātsvacchandaṃ vicarantu te // NBs_5,1.11 //
children.translated_text: they are not servants of injunction; therefore, let them wander freely. [NBs 5.1.11]
The Purport of Austerity
Austerity performed with pretense, by those devoted to hypocrisy and greed,

children.text: haṭṭe nagaramadhye vā sā tapasyā'dhamā smṛtā // NBs_5,2.1 //
children.translated_text: in a market or in the middle of a city — that austerity is considered the lowest. [NBs 5.2.1]
That which is performed according to the rules laid down in the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>śāstras</s>, by one enduring cold, heat, and the rest,

children.text: yā kṛtā kāmanāpūrvaṃ sā tapasyā tu madhyamā // NBs_5,2.2 //
children.translated_text: preceded by desire — that austerity is middling. [NBs 5.2.2]
For the purpose of restraining the mind, devoted to the supreme reality,

children.text: akāmā tatvajijñāsoḥ sā tapasyottamā matā // NBs_5,2.3 //
children.translated_text: desireless, for one who inquires into truth — that austerity is considered the highest. [NBs 5.2.3]
One should welcome whoever comes and not prevent whoever goes;
one should endure everything as it comes — that austerity is the supreme of the supreme. [NBs 5.2.4]
The Determination of Vows
Abstaining from another's wife, another's property, and harm to another —
the renunciation of passion and aversion — this is the highest of all vows. [NBs 5.3.1]
Thus it is said in the <s>Kāśīkhaṇḍa</s>:
One who turns away from another's wife, another's property, and harm to another —
even the <s>Gaṅgā</s> says: 'When will this one come and purify me?' [NBs 5.3.2]
Examination of External Appearance

children.text: muktirnāsti jaṭājūṭe na kāṣāye na muṇḍane /
children.translated_text: Liberation is not in matted hair, nor in saffron robes, nor in a shaved head,

children.text: na bhasmani na kanthāyāṃ tilake vā kamaṇḍalau // NBs_5,4.1 //
children.translated_text: nor in ashes, nor in a patched garment, nor in a <s>tilaka</s>-mark, nor in a water-pot. [NBs 5.4.1]
The snake is struck out of hatred — the striking of the anthill is useless;

children.text: manaso nigraho nāsti vṛthā kāyasya muṇḍanam // NBs_5,4.2 //
children.translated_text: if there is no restraint of the mind, the shaving of the body is useless. [NBs 5.4.2]
The wearing of matted hair, a patched garment, and the like for the purpose of calming the distraction of the mind —
if done by one free from passion, that is indeed the supreme of the supreme. [NBs 5.4.3]
Investigation of Silence
Silence is declared to be fourfold: <s>vāgmauna</s> (silence of speech) is the restraint of speech;
the restraint of the sense-organs of knowledge is called <s>akṣamauna</s> (silence of the senses). [NBs 5.5.1]
The restraint of the organs of action is <s>kāṣṭhamauna</s> (stillness like wood);

children.text: gauṇaṃ tu trividhaṃ maunamuttamaṃ tu manolayaḥ // NBs_5,5.2 //
children.translated_text: but the threefold [external] silence is secondary; the highest is the dissolution of the mind. [NBs 5.5.2]

children.text: na maunī mūkatāṃ yāto na maunī dugdhabālakaḥ /
children.translated_text: The silent one is not one who has become mute; the silent one is not a suckling child;

children.text: na maunī vrataniṣṭhopi maunī saṃlīnamānasaḥ // NBs_5,5.3 //
children.translated_text: the silent one is not even one who is devoted to a vow [of silence] — the truly silent one is one whose mind is dissolved. [NBs 5.5.3]
The state of a <s>muni</s> (sage) constitutes <s>mauna</s> (silence), according to the science of words;

children.text: munibhāvo yarhi nāsti tarhi maunaṃ nirarthakam // NBs_5,5.4 //
children.translated_text: when the state of a sage is absent, then silence is meaningless. [NBs 5.5.4]
Knowledge of Giving
Giving for fame, giving out of desire, and giving out of compassion — thus [giving is] threefold;

children.text: uttarāduttaraṃ śreṣṭhaṃ tebhyaḥ kṛṣṇārpaṇaṃ param // NBs_5,6.1 //
children.translated_text: each successive one is superior; but offering to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is the highest of all. [NBs 5.6.1]
The Truth of Pilgrimage
'This is a holy place, that is a holy place, this pilgrimage is better than that one,

children.text: ito dūrataraṃ tīrthaṃ mayā dṛṣṭaṃ na tu tvayā // NBs_5,7.1 //
children.translated_text: a holier pilgrimage is farther away — I have seen it but you have not.' [NBs 5.7.1]

children.text: tava tīrthaphalaṃ svalpaṃ mama tīrthaphalaṃ mahat /
children.translated_text: 'The fruit of your pilgrimage is small, the fruit of mine is great' —

children.text: iti bhramanti ye tīrthaṃ te bhrāntā na tu tairthikāḥ // NBs_5,7.2 //
children.translated_text: those who thus roam to holy places are deluded, not true pilgrims. [NBs 5.7.2]
At a holy place, sins are destroyed by bathing; a holy place is the company of the good;
at a holy place there should be discussion of dispassion; a holy place is the worship of God. [NBs 5.7.3]
A holy place is the endurance of cold and heat; a holy place is wandering without attachment;

children.text: iti jānanti ye tīrthaṃ tīrthatattvavido hi te // NBs_5,7.4 //
children.translated_text: those who know the holy place thus are indeed knowers of the truth of pilgrimage. [NBs 5.7.4]
The Skill of Conduct
Lack of conduct is impurity; excessive observance is foolishness;
the combination of discernment and conduct is the mark of right conduct. [NBs 5.8.1]
The Determination of Attachment and Renunciation

children.text: na viraktā dhanaistyaktā na viraktā digambarāḥ /
children.translated_text: The dispassionate are not those who have abandoned wealth; the dispassionate are not those who go naked;

children.text: viśeṣaraktāḥ svapade te viraktā matā mama // NBs_6.1 //
children.translated_text: those who are especially attached to their own [true] station — they, in my view, are the dispassionate. [NBs 6.1]

children.text: caurastyajanti gehaṃ svaṃ bhayenaiva na bodhataḥ /
children.translated_text: Thieves abandon their homes out of fear, not from awakening;

children.text: jārāstyajanti gehaṃ svaṃ kāmenaiva na bodhataḥ // NBs_6.2 //
children.translated_text: paramours abandon their homes out of lust, not from awakening. [NBs 6.2]
The angry one abandons his home due to conflict with an adversary;

children.text: ruddhastyajati gehaṃ svaṃ rodhenaiva na bodhataḥ // NBs_6.3 //
children.translated_text: the imprisoned one abandons his home due to confinement, not from awakening. [NBs 6.3]
Sages who have attained the joy of non-attachment, through some playful awakening,

children.text: gṛhaṃ tyajanti munayo gṛhasthā vāvane sthitāḥ // NBs_6.4 //
children.translated_text: leave their homes — or, remaining as householders, abide in the forest [of detachment]. [NBs 6.4]

children.text: mūḍhaḥ kiṃ tyajatu pramattamanasastyāgena vā kiṃ phalaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'What should a fool renounce? What is the fruit of renunciation for one with a distracted mind?

children.text: vijñaḥ karma karotu vā na kurutāṃ tyāge'valipto na yat /
children.translated_text: Let the wise man perform actions or not — for he is not smeared by renunciation.',
Thus, having formed his conviction through the teachings of those learned in <s>Advaita</s> (non-dual) wisdom,

children.text: rāgatyāganirādaro munijanaḥ pāre girāṃ khelati // NBs_6.5 //
children.translated_text: the sage, indifferent to attachment and renunciation, plays beyond the reach of words. [NBs 6.5]

body.translated_text: Thus it is said:

children.translated_text: This, then, is the determination of attachment and renunciation for those united with <s>yoga</s>;
one should know that [which is to be known] by renunciation alone — such is the conclusion of <s>Vedānta</s>. [NBs 6.6]
Examination of Qualification
Many kinds of <s>dharma</s> are declared in <s>śāstra</s> for those qualified for <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: tatra tībrā mumukṣaiva mokṣe mukhyādhikāritā // NBs_7.1 //
children.translated_text: among them, intense desire for liberation is the chief qualification for <s>mokṣa</s>. [NBs 7.1]
For the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> [sacrifice], one desiring heaven [is qualified]; for marriage, one desiring a son;
for commerce, one who is greedy; for <s>mokṣa</s>, one who desires liberation is qualified. [NBs 7.2]

children.text: tīvrā mumukṣā yadyasti prajñāmāndyaṃ ca varttate /
children.translated_text: If intense desire for liberation exists but intellectual dullness also persists,
one should first remove that through discussion with learned teachers of true <s>śāstra</s>. [NBs 7.3]
If one has no qualification for the <s>Veda</s> but the desire for liberation exists,
inquiry should be conducted by him through listening to <s>Purāṇas</s> and the like. [NBs 7.4]

children.text: yadeva vede kathitaṃ purāṇe'pi tadeva hi /
children.translated_text: What is said in the <s>Veda</s> is also said in the <s>Purāṇa</s>;

children.text: na tu vedākṣaraṃ śrāvyamiti bhāṣye vinirṇayaḥ // NBs_7.5 //
children.translated_text: but the letters of the <s>Veda</s> are not to be recited [by the unqualified] — such is the determination of the commentary. [NBs 7.5]
The <s>karma</s> (action) that is enjoined according to one's qualification succeeds; otherwise,
the accomplishment of the task would not occur, and a great adverse consequence would arise. [NBs 7.6]
[Chapter:] The Nectar of Holy Company (<s>Satsaṃgasudhā</s>)
O dear one, when the mind is delighted by the nectar of holy company (<s>satsaṃga</s>),
then one should ascertain: through [the dispelling of] delusion, my liberation will come about. [NBs 8.1]
Of all spiritual means (<s>sādhanas</s>), the association with the holy (<s>sādhusaṅgati</s>) is the best.

children.text: etayā siddhayā siddhaṃ sarvameva hi sādhanam // NBs_8.2 //
children.translated_text: When this [association] is perfected, every [other] means is perfected. [NBs 8.2]
Those who are ever devoted to the Lord, dispassionate, and equal-visioned,
those holy ones, expert in the scripture of liberation, should be served. [NBs 8.3]
Those by whose mere sight faith in liberation increases,

children.text: yeṣāṃ ca vāgvilāsena saṃśayo vinivarttate // NBs_8.4 //
children.translated_text: and by the play of whose speech doubt is removed — [NBs 8.4]
The ascertainment of the purport [of scripture] through the indicators beginning with the opening (<s>upakrama</s>) and the conclusion (<s>tātparya</s>),
and the arrangement of scriptural meanings through the particular and the general — [NBs 8.5]
Entry into the path of liberation without contradicting the <s>Vedas</s> and śāstras,
the knowledge of tradition (<s>saṃpradāya</s>), and the determination of differences among doctrines — [NBs 8.6]
Those from whose words both the prior and later positions [of a debate] are obtained,

children.text: jñāninaḥ karṇadhārāste sevitavyā hi sādhavaḥ // NBs_8.7 //
children.translated_text: those knowers are the helmsmen — such holy ones should indeed be served. [NBs 8.7]
And thus in the <s>Gītā</s>:
Know that through prostration, inquiry, and service,
the knowers who have seen the truth will teach you knowledge. [NBs 8.8]
[Chapter:] The River of Harmonization (<s>Samanvayasarasvatī</s>)
The river of harmonization (<s>samanvaya</s>) should be plunged into especially,
by which the washing away of the mud called doctrinal differences would arise. [NBs 9.1]
The word, the meaning of words, the meaning of sentences, the categories (<s>tattvas</s>), the discipline of the mind,
and the knowledge of the meaning of the <s>mahāvākyas</s> (great sentences) — these are the means, in order. [NBs 9.2]
The utility of all the systems of philosophy (<s>tantras</s>) therein, each according to its scope,
I shall state in brief, all exactly as it is. [NBs 9.3]
Through the science of grammar (<s>śabdaśāstra</s>), the excellent derivation of words arises;
and the derivation of word-meanings through the statements of <s>Nyāya</s> and <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>. [NBs 9.4]
Through <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>, the derivation of sentence-meaning is established;

children.text: vyaktiḥ sāṃkhyena tattvānāṃ yogena manaso yamaḥ // NBs_9.5 //
children.translated_text: through <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, the discrimination of categories; through <s>Yoga</s>, the discipline of the mind. [NBs 9.5]
The knowledge of the meaning of the <s>mahāvākyas</s> is through <s>Vedānta</s>, with firm establishment in <s>Brahman</s>.
Thus, the harmonization (<s>samanvaya</s>) of all systems culminates in <s>Brahman</s> alone. [NBs 9.6]
[Chapter:] The Understanding of Non-Contradiction (<s>Avirodhabodha</s>)
In this context, the understanding of non-contradiction is also examined.
In practical life (<s>vyavahāra</s>), the reality of duality is the same in both the dualist and the non-dualist views. [NBs 10.1]
And the superimposed nature [of duality] in <s>Advaita</s> — thus there is no contradiction in the two views.
Let those who relish debate repeatedly debate about it. [NBs 10.2]
The <s>yamas</s> (restraints) are non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), truthfulness (<s>satya</s>), and the rest; the <s>niyamas</s> (observances) are purity (<s>śauca</s>) and the rest;

children.text: sukhāsane ca saṃsthānaṃ pratyāhārastu sarvataḥ // NBs_10.3 //
children.translated_text: and steady abiding in a comfortable posture (<s>āsana</s>), and <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal) from all [sense-objects]. [NBs 10.3]

children.text: dhāraṇā ca tathā dhyānaṃ samādhānaṃ ca cetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>samādhāna</s> (absorption) of the mind —
these seven limbs of <s>yoga</s> are accepted by all. [NBs 10.4]

children.text: laye mantre haṭhe rājñi bhaktau sāṃkhye harermate /
children.translated_text: In <s>laya</s> (absorption), <s>mantra</s>, <s>haṭha</s>, <s>rāja</s> [yoga], <s>bhakti</s> (devotion), <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, and the doctrine of <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: mataikyamasti sarveṣāṃ ye budhā mokṣamārgagāḥ // NBs_10.5 //
children.translated_text: there is unity of view among all those wise ones who tread the path of liberation. [NBs 10.5]
For the practitioners of <s>haṭha</s> [yoga], there is one additional exertion — <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control).

children.text: prāṇāyāme manaḥsthairyaṃ sa tu kasya na saṃmataḥ // NBs_10.6 //
children.translated_text: That <s>prāṇāyāma</s> produces steadiness of mind — who does not accept this? [NBs 10.6]
Therefore, among the proponents of liberation, there is no doctrinal difference whatsoever.
Some slight difference exists even among the <s>Vedāntins</s> themselves. [NBs 10.7]
[Chapter:] The Collyrium Stick of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> (<s>Sāṃkhyāñjanaśalākā</s>)
The eyes should be anointed with the collyrium stick of <s>Sāṃkhya</s>;
then, by the destruction of the cataract [of ignorance], the subtle reality is perceived. [NBs 11.1]
<s>Devahūtī</s> was enlightened by <s>Kapila</s>, [who is] <s>Mukunda</s> himself,
through the discrimination of all categories — that is called <s>Sāṃkhya</s>. [NBs 11.2]
She from whom all modifications arise — gross and subtle, moving and unmoving —
there exists a certain indescribable <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), consisting of three <s>guṇas</s>. [NBs 11.3]
<s>Mahat-tattva</s> (the great principle), <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), and the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) —
these seven are both <s>prakṛti</s> (cause) and <s>vikṛti</s> (effect). [NBs 11.4]
A <s>vikṛti</s> (modification) of its own cause, and a <s>prakṛti</s> (cause) of its own product —
thus there are eight <s>prakṛtis</s>, and from them arise the sixteen <s>vikṛtis</s>. [NBs 11.5]
The five gross elements beginning with space, the five organs of knowledge (<s>jñānendriyas</s>),

children.text: karmendriyāṇi pañcaiva manasā saha ṣoḍaśa // NBs_11.6 //
children.translated_text: and the five organs of action (<s>karmendriyas</s>) together with the mind — these are sixteen. [NBs 11.6]
Space, wind, fire, water, and earth — these are called the five elements.

children.text: śabdasparśau rūparasau gandhasteṣāṃ guṇāḥ kramāt // NBs_11.7 //
children.translated_text: Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell are their qualities, in order. [NBs 11.7]

children.text: śrotraṃ tvakcakṣu rasanaṃ ghrāṇaṃ jñānendriyāṇi ca /
children.translated_text: Ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose are the organs of knowledge;
speech, hands, feet, the organ of excretion, and so on — these are the five organs of action. [NBs 11.8]
The mind, which is of both natures [knowledge and action] — with it, twenty-four [categories] are stated.

children.text: tattvānāṃ tadvikārastu sarvaṃ caiva jagattrayam // NBs_11.9 //
children.translated_text: These categories and their modifications constitute the entire three worlds. [NBs 11.9]
Because <s>Prakṛti</s> consists of three <s>guṇas</s>, everything is of the nature of three <s>guṇas</s>.
The <s>guṇas</s> of <s>rajas</s>, <s>sattva</s>, and <s>tamas</s> have the forms of red, white, and dark respectively. [NBs 11.10]
<s>Rajas</s> is restless, <s>tamas</s> is inert, and <s>sattva</s> is regarded as luminous.

children.text: tamo'dhamaṃ rajo madhyaṃ sattvamuttamameva hi // NBs_11.11 //
children.translated_text: <s>Tamas</s> is the lowest, <s>rajas</s> is the middle, and <s>sattva</s> is indeed the highest. [NBs 11.11]
Greed and the like are states of <s>rajas</s>; dullness and the like are of <s>tamas</s>.
Happiness, clarity, knowledge, and the like are declared to be the states of <s>sattva</s>. [NBs 11.12]
Gods and the like are <s>sāttvika</s>; humans and the like are said to be <s>rājasa</s>.

children.text: tāmasāḥ paśubhūtādyā evaṃ sarvaṃ vivicyatām // NBs_11.13 //
children.translated_text: Animals, ghosts, and the like are <s>tāmasa</s> — thus let everything be discriminated. [NBs 11.13]
Antagonistic, cooperative, mutually cause and effect —
the <s>guṇas</s>, of unequal activity, combine to produce effects. [NBs 11.14]

children.text: viśvaṃ guṇātmakaṃ sarvamātmā nirguṇa eva hi /
children.translated_text: The entire universe is of the nature of the <s>guṇas</s>; the <s>ātman</s> (self) is indeed devoid of <s>guṇas</s>.

children.text: prakāśakatayā tatra praviṣṭa iva bhāsate // NBs_11.15 //
children.translated_text: By virtue of being the illuminator, it appears as if entered there. [NBs 11.15]
Just as the tongue, situated among the thirty-two teeth, knows tastes and discriminates flavors,
so the knower of the self, within the twenty-four categories, knows the truth. [NBs 11.16]
<s>Māyā</s> (illusion), lustful for sense-objects, taking her one true lord

children.text: bahurūpadharaṃ kṛtvā veśyeva khalu khelati // NBs_11.17 //
children.translated_text: and making him assume many forms, plays like a courtesan indeed. [NBs 11.17]
Having merged with <s>Puruṣa</s> (the conscious being) in the form of non-separation,
that dancer (<s>Prakṛti</s>) makes him dance through her manifold forms and shapes. [NBs 11.18]

children.text: nirdoṣo niścalo nāthaḥ sadoṣā cañcalā vadhūḥ /
children.translated_text: The lord is faultless and motionless; the bride (<s>Prakṛti</s>) is faulty and restless.
Surely, between this couple, a rupture of rasa (aesthetic sentiment/relationship) will occur. [NBs 11.19]
When recognized as separate and as being of corrupt nature,

children.text: na mukhaṃ darśayatyeṣā salajjā mriyate'pi ca // NBs_11.20 //
children.translated_text: she does not show her face; ashamed, she even dies away. [NBs 11.20]
<s>Prakṛti</s> is neither cause nor effect [ultimately]; <s>Puruṣa</s> is of motionless nature,
of the form of pure consciousness — this is the determination of <s>Sāṃkhya</s>. [NBs 11.21]
[Chapter:] The Wish-Fulfilling Jewel of <s>Yoga</s> Initiation — <s>Pātañjala Yoga</s>
Now, henceforth, the wish-fulfilling jewel of <s>yoga</s> initiation is expounded.
By its attainment, all the poverty of ignorance is destroyed. [NBs 12.1.1]
<s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) is the great lord of <s>yoga</s>; <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) is the great lord of <s>yoga</s>;
<s>Brahmā</s> is the great lord of <s>yoga</s>; <s>Bhavānī</s> is the perfected <s>yoginī</s>. [NBs 12.1.2]
<s>Sanaka</s> and the others, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and the others, <s>Kaca</s>, <s>Datta</s>, <s>Śuka</s>, and the rest,
<s>Arundhatī</s> and the others — all attained perfection through <s>yoga</s>. [NBs 12.1.3]
The <s>yoga</s> that is the union of the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>) and the supreme self (<s>paramātman</s>) through self-knowledge —

children.text: sa yogastasya hetutvādyogā bahuvidhā matāḥ // NBs_12,1.4 //
children.translated_text: that is <s>yoga</s>; and because it is the means to that, many types of <s>yoga</s> are recognized. [NBs 12.1.4]
Just as, by an apparent contradiction, what is inauspicious [becomes] auspicious —
<s>Keśava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) says that <s>yoga</s> is the complete separation from all suffering. [NBs 12.1.5]
Even for the extremely restless mind, through the power of <s>yoga</s>,
steadiness would arise, like that of the great mountain <s>Vindhya</s>. [NBs 12.1.6]
And thus <s>Bhuśuṇḍa</s> [says]:
"Having established the ethereal <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), I remain free from fever,
as long as the lotus-born one (<s>Brahmā</s>) continues in the work of creation." [NBs 12.1.7]
The cessation of the modifications of the mind (<s>cittavṛttinirodha</s>) is the primary [yoga], regarded as <s>Pātañjala</s> [yoga].
The cessation of the modifications of <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) is secondary, because it is the means to that. [NBs 12.1.8]
<s>pratyāhāra</s>, <s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, and <s>samādhi</s> — these are the eight limbs.
<s>Yama</s> consists of non-stealing (<s>asteya</s>), truthfulness (<s>ṛta</s>), non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), and non-possessiveness (<s>aparigraha</s>).

<s>Niyama</s> consists of purity (<s>śauca</s>), contentment (<s>santoṣa</s>), austerity (<s>tapas</s>), study of scripture (<s>pāṭha</s>), and surrender to the Lord (<s>īśvarārpaṇa</s>). [NBs 12.1.9]

body.translated_text: The sūtra thereon: <s>yama</s>, <s>niyama</s>, <s>āsana</s>, <s>prāṇāyāma</s>,

children.translated_text: <s>Āsana</s> is regarded as steadiness of the body in a comfortable posture.
<s>Prāṇāyāma</s> is the discipline of <s>prāṇa</s>, through <s>kumbhaka</s> (retention), <s>pūraka</s> (inhalation), and <s>recaka</s> (exhalation). [NBs 12.1.10]
<s>Pratyāhāra</s> is the restraining of the restless sense-organs.

children.text: kvacitpradeśe cittasya sthāpanaṃ dhāraṇā matā // NBs_12,1.11 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dhāraṇā</s> is regarded as the fixing of the mind on some particular locus. [NBs 12.1.11]
An uninterrupted flow of consciousness toward the object of meditation is declared to be <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation).
<s>Samādhi</s>, the eighth [limb], is to be known as abiding in identity with that [object]. [NBs 12.1.12]
<s>Saṃprajñāta</s> [samādhi] and the other — <s>samādhi</s> is indeed of two kinds.
The first five [limbs] beginning with <s>yama</s> are external limbs; the remaining are internal. [NBs 12.1.13]
Accompanied by <s>vitarka</s> (deliberation), <s>vicāra</s> (reflection), <s>ānanda</s> (bliss), and <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness),
<s>saṃprajñāta samādhi</s> is of four kinds. [NBs 12.1.14]
Where nothing is cognized, that is called <s>asaṃprajñāta</s> [samādhi].
It is of two kinds: <s>bhavapratyaya</s> (arising from worldly tendency) and <s>upāyapratyaya</s> (arising from the means). [NBs 12.1.15]
Even for the deluded, absorption of the mind may arise through the intensity of austerity.

children.text: prakṛtau vā mahatattve bhavapratyaya eva saḥ // NBs_12,1.16 //
children.translated_text: In <s>Prakṛti</s> or in <s>Mahat-tattva</s> — that is indeed <s>bhavapratyaya</s>. [NBs 12.1.16]
As in the case of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, who desired sovereignty over the three worlds,
whose body was consumed by worms and even covered by an anthill. [NBs 12.1.17]
Preceded by faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), memory (<s>smṛti</s>), wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), and the abandonment of desire —
the absorption of the mind of the greatest sages is <s>upāyapratyaya</s>. [NBs 12.1.18]
For those whose minds are distracted and who desire absorption, it is stated:
austerity, recitation of the <s>Vedas</s>, and the offering of all actions to <s>Hari</s>. [NBs 12.1.19]
Untouched by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), <s>karma</s>, and their ripening of various forms and their residual impressions,
there is one unique <s>Puruṣa</s> — <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord). [NBs 12.1.20]
He is omniscient by nature; <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ) is his designator.
The repetition of that, preceded by contemplation, is the means to liberation. [NBs 12.1.21]
Just as disease, its cause, medicine, and health —
with their fourfold distinction to be analyzed — so is medical treatment fourfold. [NBs 12.1.22]

children.text: janmaduḥkhaṃ tathā moho vijñānaṃ ca vimuktatā /
children.translated_text: Birth-suffering, delusion, knowledge, and liberation —
with their fourfold distinction to be analyzed — so is the <s>yoga</s> śāstra fourfold. [NBs 12.1.23]
Non-discrimination between <s>Puruṣa</s> and <s>Prakṛti</s> — that is delusion, the cause of suffering.
It is destroyed by the knowledge of discrimination — the otherness of the self from the equilibrium [of the guṇas]. [NBs 12.1.24]
For one engaged in the practice of <s>yoga</s>, <s>siddhis</s> (supernatural powers) that bestow enjoyment

children.text: āyānti nādaraḥ kāryo hyantarāyā matā yataḥ // NBs_12,1.25 //
children.translated_text: come; but no regard should be given to them, since they are considered obstacles. [NBs 12.1.25]
The differentiation of <s>siddhis</s> that is stated through the variety of <s>dhāraṇā</s> and <s>dhyāna</s>,
being entirely unprofitable, is not examined here. [NBs 12.1.26]
[Chapter:] <s>Śaiva Yoga</s>
<s>Śaiva Yoga</s> is now examined.

children.text: mantro layo haṭho rājayogo yogaścaturvidhaḥ // NBs_12,2.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mantra</s>, <s>laya</s>, <s>haṭha</s>, and <s>rāja</s> <s>yoga</s> — <s>yoga</s> is of four kinds. [NBs 12.2.1]
[Section:] <s>Mantra Yoga</s>
The eight-syllabled <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> [mantra], the twelve-syllabled <s>Vāsudeva</s> [mantra],
the <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, and <s>Gopāla</s> mantras — these are praised in the <s>Tāpinī</s> [Upaniṣads]. [NBs 12.2.2]
The five-syllabled <s>Śiva</s> [mantra] is supreme; the <s>Dakṣiṇāmūrti</s> [mantra] is excellent;

children.text: yatīnāṃ tu mahāvākyaṃ kevalaḥ praṇavastathā // NBs_12,2.3 //
children.translated_text: for renunciants (<s>yatis</s>), the <s>mahāvākya</s> (great sentence), and the pure <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ). [NBs 12.2.3]
These and other great mantras, through the practices of <s>puraścarya</s> (preparatory rites) and the like,

children.text: siddhā devaprasādena sadyo muktipradā matāḥ // NBs_12,2.4 //
children.translated_text: perfected by the grace of God, are held to grant immediate liberation. [NBs 12.2.4]
[Section:] <s>Haṭha Yoga</s>
Between <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s> (i.e., the <s>iḍā</s> and <s>piṅgalā</s> channels), seize forcefully the young widowed ascetic woman (<s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>) —
that is the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. [NBs 12.3.1]
And thus <s>Gorakṣa</s> [says]:
"This is the stairway to liberation; this is the deception of time (death).
When the mind, turned away from enjoyment, is attached to the Supreme Self, [NBs 12.3.2]
if there is supreme <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), and diet is as prescribed,
and if there is constant solitary dwelling, then <s>Haṭhayoga</s> is not difficult to attain. [NBs 12.3.3]
However, this is obtained through the initiation of a <s>guru</s> and not otherwise;
in transgression there is great fault, in gradual attainment there is great merit. [NBs 12.3.4]
<s>Haṭha</s> [yoga], of infinite extent, has been taught by the enemy of [the demon] <s>Pura</s> (<s>Śiva</s>);

children.text: sāraṃ tu bandhatritayaṃ tāvatā siddhirāpyate // NBs_12,3.5 //
children.translated_text: but the essence is the three <s>bandhas</s> (locks) — by that much, <s>siddhi</s> (perfection) is attained. [NBs 12.3.5]
At the base is <s>Mūlabandha</s> (root lock); in the middle is <s>Uḍḍīyāna</s> (flying-up lock);

children.text: kaṇṭhe jālandharastena siddho bhavati mārutaḥ // NBs_12,3.6 //
children.translated_text: at the throat is <s>Jālandhara</s> (net-holding lock) — by these, the <s>vāyu</s> (vital breath) becomes perfected. [NBs 12.3.6]
When <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> has entered the <s>Suṣumnā</s> [channel] through the <s>Brahmarandhra</s> (aperture of Brahman) —
<s>Śakti</s> (power) is stationed at the base, <s>Sadāśiva</s> is stationed at the <s>Brahman</s>-place. [NBs 12.3.7]
The <s>Ajapā</s> (unrepeated) <s>Gāyatrī</s> is the liberator of <s>yogins</s>;
by mere intention upon it, one is freed from all sins. [NBs 12.3.8]

children.text: ādhāraṃ prathamaṃ cakraṃ svādhiṣṭhānaṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Ādhāra</s> (support) is the first <s>cakra</s>, and likewise <s>Svādhiṣṭhāna</s>;
the third is <s>Maṇipūra</s>, and the fourth is <s>Anāhata</s>. [NBs 12.3.9]
<s>Viśuddhi</s> is the fifth <s>cakra</s>, and <s>Ājñā</s> <s>cakra</s> is the sixth;

children.text: saptamaṃ brahmarandhraṃ syādbhramarasya guhā hi sā // NBs_12,3.10 //
children.translated_text: the seventh is the <s>Brahmarandhra</s> — that is the cave of the bee. [NBs 12.3.10]

children.text: yonisthānakamaṅghrimūlaghaṭitaṃ kṛtvā dṛḍhaṃ vinyasen meḍhre pādamathaikameva niyataṃ kṛtvā samaṃ vigraham /
children.translated_text: Placing the <s>yonisthāna</s> (perineal region) firmly, joined at the root of the foot, and placing one foot precisely upon the generative organ, keeping the body straight,

children.text: sthāṇuḥ saṃyamitendriyo'caladṛśā paśyanbhruvorantaraṃ hyetanmokṣakapāṭabhedanakaraṃ siddhāsanaṃ procyate // NBs_12,3.11 //
children.translated_text: like a pillar, with senses restrained, with steady gaze looking between the brows — this is called <s>Siddhāsana</s> (the adept's seat), which breaks open the door to liberation. [NBs 12.3.11]

children.text: kṛtvā sampuṭitau karau dṛḍhataraṃ badhvā tu siddhāsanaṃ gāḍhaṃ vakṣasi sannidhāya cubukaṃ dhyānaṃ tataścetasi /
children.translated_text: Having firmly cupped the hands together and bound the <s>Siddhāsana</s>, pressing the chin tightly against the chest, then [fixing] meditation in the mind,

children.text: vāraṃ vāramapānamūrdhvamanilaṃ protsārya sandhārayan prāṇaṃ muñcati bodhayaṃśca śanakaiḥ śaktiprabodho bhavet // NBs_12,3.12 //
children.translated_text: again and again raising the <s>apāna</s> breath upward, retaining and slowly releasing the <s>prāṇa</s> while awakening [the power] — the awakening of <s>Śakti</s> occurs. [NBs 12.3.12]
The wise one should awaken the sleeping serpent-goddess by seizing her tail;

children.text: nidrāṃ vihāya sā śaktirūrdhvamuttiṣṭhate balāt // NBs_12,3.13 //
children.translated_text: abandoning sleep, that <s>Śakti</s> rises upward by force. [NBs 12.3.13]
When the <s>prāṇa</s> has merged upward and all <s>karma</s> has been relinquished,
the natural state (<s>sahajāvasthā</s>) arises of itself through <s>yoga</s>. [NBs 12.3.14]

children.text: jñānaṃ kuto manasi jīvati devi yāvat prāṇo na naśyati mano mriyate na tāvat /
children.translated_text: O Goddess, how can knowledge arise in the mind as long as the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) lives? As long as <s>prāṇa</s> does not perish, the mind does not die.

children.text: prāṇo mano dvayamidaṃ pralayaṃ prayāti mokṣaṃ sa gacchati naro na kadācidanyaḥ // NBs_12,3.15 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> and mind — when these two reach dissolution, that person attains <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), and never another. [NBs 12.3.15]
When the <s>yogin</s> remains with mind and breath dissolved in the inner focus,
with gaze steady and unblinking, outwardly seeing yet not seeing —

children.text: mudreyaṃ kila śāmbhavī bhagavatī yā syātprasādādguroḥ śūnyāśūnyavilakṣaṇaṃ mṛgayate tattvaṃ padaṃ śāṃbhavam // NBs_12,3.16 //
children.translated_text: this <s>mudrā</s> is indeed the blessed <s>Śāmbhavī</s>, which arises by the grace of the <s>guru</s>; it seeks the <s>Śāmbhava</s> (pertaining to <s>Śiva</s>) state, that reality distinguished from both void and non-void. [NBs 12.3.16]
When the activity of <s>prāṇa</s> dissolves, the activity of mind dissolves;
the union of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> is produced through <s>Haṭhayoga</s>. [NBs 12.3.17]
[Adepts] like <s>Gorakṣa</s> and <s>Carpaṭi</s>, by the grace of <s>Haṭhayoga</s>,

children.text: vañcayitvā kāladaṇḍaṃ brahmāṇḍaṃ vicaranti hi // NBs_12,3.18 //
children.translated_text: having cheated the staff of Death, wander throughout the <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> (cosmic egg). [NBs 12.3.18]
Placing the mind within <s>Śakti</s>, and <s>Śakti</s> within the mental [space],
<s>Haṭhayogins</s> accomplish the union of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>. [NBs 12.3.19]
Page 147
The Prowess of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>
Now I shall describe, under the pretext of a hymn, the prowess of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>,

children.text: śodhite sūkṣmayā dṛṣṭyā yasminnirvismayo bhavet // NBs_12,4.1 //
children.translated_text: upon which, when examined with subtle vision, one becomes free from wonder. [NBs 12.4.1]
Her, who is of the form of duality, of the form of both duality and non-duality,
and of the form of non-duality — that <s>Śakti</s> of the Supreme Self, I remember. [NBs 12.4.2]

children.text: keyaṃ kasya kutaḥ kena kasmai kaṃ prati kutra vā /
children.translated_text: 'Who is she? Whose is she? Whence? By whom? For whom? Toward whom? Where?

children.text: kathaṃ kadetyanirṇītā tāṃ vande śaktimadbhutām // NBs_12,4.3 //
children.translated_text: How? What?' — to that wondrous <s>Śakti</s>, which is undetermined [by any of these], I bow. [NBs 12.4.3]

children.text: śivaḥ karttā śivo bhoktā śivo vettā śivaḥ prabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s> is the doer, <s>Śiva</s> is the enjoyer, <s>Śiva</s> is the knower, <s>Śiva</s> is the lord;

children.text: upasarjanamātraṃ yā tāṃ vande śaktimadbhutām // NBs_12,4.4 //
children.translated_text: to that wondrous <s>Śakti</s>, who is merely the subordinate [factor], I bow. [NBs 12.4.4]

children.text: svayaṃ kartrī svayaṃ bhoktrī svayaṃ vettrī svayaṃ prabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: She herself is the doer, she herself the enjoyer, she herself the knower, she herself the lord;

children.text: sākṣimātraṃ śivo yasyāstāṃ vande śaktimadbhutām // NBs_12,4.5 //
children.translated_text: to that wondrous <s>Śakti</s>, of whom <s>Śiva</s> is merely the witness, I bow. [NBs 12.4.5]
Abiding with her own characteristics in <s>Mahādeva</s> who has his own characteristics,

children.text: vittāṃ svalakṣaṇaireva tāṃ vande śaktimadbhutām // NBs_12,4.6 //
children.translated_text: known only through her own characteristics — to that wondrous <s>Śakti</s> I bow. [NBs 12.4.6]
Abiding with [his] characteristics in <s>Mahādeva</s> who has characteristics,

children.text: vittāṃ salakṣaṇaireva tāṃ vande śaktimadbhutām // NBs_12,4.7 //
children.translated_text: known through those very characteristics — to that wondrous <s>Śakti</s> I bow. [NBs 12.4.7]
Abiding as the extraordinary in <s>Mahādeva</s> who is extraordinary,

children.text: vittāṃ vilakṣaṇaireva tāṃ vande śaktimadbhutām // NBs_12,4.8 //
children.translated_text: known only through the extraordinary — to that wondrous <s>Śakti</s> I bow. [NBs 12.4.8]
In <s>Caitanya</s> (Consciousness), which stands as if insentient because its nature is beyond cognition and non-cognition,
[she is] the cause of sentience — to that wondrous <s>Śakti</s> I bow. [NBs 12.4.9]
'Cognized by the cognizer' — from the perspective of its determinate nature,
in <s>Caitanya</s>, [she is] the cause of sentience — to that wondrous <s>Śakti</s> I bow. [NBs 12.4.10]

children.text: śaktireva na yasyāsti so'śaktaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati /
children.translated_text: He who has no <s>Śakti</s> at all — that powerless one, what can he do?

children.text: śaktyā yayā śivaḥ śaktastāṃ vande śaktimadbhutām // NBs_12,4.11 //
children.translated_text: To that wondrous <s>Śakti</s> by which <s>Śiva</s> is empowered, I bow. [NBs 12.4.11]

children.text: śaktā nūnaṃ hi kāryeṣu śaktiḥ śaktimati sthitā /
children.translated_text: <s>Śakti</s>, abiding in the powerful one, is indeed capable in all activities;
without the support of <s>Śiva</s>, she is powerless — to that wondrous <s>Śakti</s> I bow. [NBs 12.4.12]
Since in the undifferentiated [state] of <s>Śakti</s> and the powerful one, there is no [separate] reality,

children.text: sāmarasyaṃ śive yātā tāṃ vande śaktimadbhutām // NBs_12,4.13 //
children.translated_text: having attained equipoise in <s>Śiva</s> — to that wondrous <s>Śakti</s> I bow. [NBs 12.4.13]
When the prowess of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> is contemplated in this way by devotees,
the ocean of the nectar of equipoise spontaneously shines forth in one's own heart. [NBs 12.4.14]

children.text: bhakte bhaktimayīṃ paśau paśumayīṃ vidvatsu vidyāmayīṃ sṛṣṭau brahmamayīṃ sthitau harimayīṃ kalpātpuraścinmayīm /
children.translated_text: In the devotee, she is full of devotion; in the bound soul, she is full of bondage; in the learned, she is full of knowledge; in creation, she is full of <s>Brahman</s>; in preservation, she is full of <s>Hari</s>; before the cosmic cycle, she is full of consciousness;

children.text: jīve vṛttimayīṃ jaḍe jaḍamayīṃ śaktiṃ śivasyādbhutāṃ tāṃ dhyāyāmi pade parātparatare svānandalīlāmayīm // NBs_12,4.15 //
children.translated_text: in the living being, she is full of activity; in the inert, she is full of inertness — that wondrous <s>Śakti</s> of <s>Śiva</s>, I meditate upon her in the state beyond the supreme, whose play is of her own bliss. [NBs 12.4.15]
Setting aside even [spiritual] bliss, [she is] eagerly sought by those seeking sense-pleasures, yet eagerly sought also by the inert for even a fraction of bliss;

she who is proclaimed by the <s>Ānanda</s> Upaniṣads as the authority, the highest peak of bliss — that blessed one, the bearer of the nectar of bliss, whose very form is bliss, I worship. [NBs 12.4.16]
Page 160
<s>Layayoga</s> (Yoga of Absorption)

children.text: cañcalaṃ hi na jānāti mano niścalatāsukham /
children.translated_text: The restless mind indeed does not know the happiness of stillness;
for its reflection, the sages have shown <s>laya</s> (absorption). [NBs 12.5.1]
Innumerable methods of <s>laya</s> have been described by <s>Śambhu</s> to <s>Gaurī</s>;

children.text: kena jñeyāḥ kena varṇyāḥ kiñcittu kathayāmyaham // NBs_12,5.2 //
children.translated_text: who can know them? Who can describe them? But I shall speak of a little. [NBs 12.5.2]
At the onset of sleep, at the end of waking; at the end of sleep, at the arising of waking —

children.text: layo bhavati cittasya kāryaṃ tatrātmacintanam // NBs_12,5.3 //
children.translated_text: there occurs <s>laya</s> (absorption) of the mind; one should practice contemplation of the Self there. [NBs 12.5.3]

children.text: yadā śithilatāṃ yāti bhāraṃ tyaktveva bhārikaḥ /
children.translated_text: When it becomes relaxed, like a porter who has set down his burden,
at that very time, the worship of <s>Śiva</s> should be performed with care for the Self. [NBs 12.5.4]

children.text: yadā yadā śithilatāṃ yāti cittaṃ tadā tadā /
children.translated_text: Whenever the mind becomes relaxed,
at that very time <s>Maheśāna</s> (the Great Lord) should be contemplated — that itself is the worship of <s>Śiva</s>. [NBs 12.5.5]
By cultivating the attitude of desirability toward all desired and undesired states alike,

children.text: nīrāgadveṣatā citte yā saiva śivapūjanam // NBs_12,5.6 //
children.translated_text: the freedom from attachment and aversion in the mind that [results] — that itself is the worship of <s>Śiva</s>. [NBs 12.5.6]
Pain itself is the highest worship, just as pressing of the feet [is worship];

children.text: duḥkhameva parā pūjā rūkṣamudvarttanaṃ yathā // NBs_12,5.7 //
children.translated_text: suffering itself is the highest worship, just as a rough massage. [NBs 12.5.7]

children.text: kheda eva parā pūjā khede citi manolayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Weariness itself is the highest worship — in weariness, the mind dissolves into consciousness;

children.text: bhayaṃ hi paramā pūjā bhīṣā'smāditi ca śruteḥ // NBs_12,5.8 //
children.translated_text: fear is indeed the highest worship — [as] the scripture [says], 'from fear of Him [the wind blows].' [NBs 12.5.8]

children.text: dānaṃ tu paramā pūjā dīyate paramātmane /
children.translated_text: Giving is the highest worship — [for] it is given to the Supreme Self;

children.text: adānaṃ paramā pūjā yadi cittaṃ prasīdati // NBs_12,5.9 //
children.translated_text: non-giving is the highest worship — if the mind thereby becomes tranquil. [NBs 12.5.9]

children.text: rogā eva parā pūjā rogaiḥ pāpakṣayo yataḥ /
children.translated_text: Diseases themselves are the highest worship, since by diseases sins are destroyed;

children.text: ārogyaṃ paramā pūjā nairogyaṃ muktisādhanam // NBs_12,5.10 //
children.translated_text: health is the highest worship — freedom from disease is the means of liberation. [NBs 12.5.10]

children.text: kriyā tu paramā pūjā śivārthaṃ kriyate'khilam /
children.translated_text: Action is the highest worship — everything is performed for <s>Śiva</s>;

children.text: akriyaiva parā pūjā niścalā dhyānarūpiṇī // NBs_12,5.11 //
children.translated_text: non-action too is the highest worship — motionless, in the form of meditation. [NBs 12.5.11]
Good company is the highest worship — good company is the means of liberation;

children.text: asatsaṅgaḥ parā pūjā yatra mohaḥ parīkṣyate // NBs_12,5.12 //
children.translated_text: bad company is the highest worship — where delusion is tested. [NBs 12.5.12]

children.text: dhairyaṃ tu paramā pūjā dhīro hyamṛtaśnute /
children.translated_text: Steadfastness is the highest worship — the steadfast one indeed tastes immortality;

children.text: adhairyaṃ paramā pūjā śīghraṃ kāryavimokṣataḥ // NBs_12,5.13 //
children.translated_text: unsteadiness is the highest worship — because of the swift release from obligations. [NBs 12.5.13]

children.text: stutireva parā pūjā stutau devaḥ prasīdati /
children.translated_text: Praise itself is the highest worship — by praise the deity is pleased;

children.text: nindaiva paramā pūjā suhṛdāṃ gālayo yathā // NBs_12,5.14 //
children.translated_text: censure itself is the highest worship — like the affectionate abuse of friends. [NBs 12.5.14]

children.text: tṛṣṇaiva paramā pūjā devārthaṃ vahu kāṅkṣate /
children.translated_text: Craving itself is the highest worship — one yearns greatly for the deity;

children.text: santoṣaḥ paramā pūjā devaḥ santoṣalakṣaṇaḥ // NBs_12,5.15 //
children.translated_text: contentment is the highest worship — the deity is characterized by contentment. [NBs 12.5.15]
Pilgrimage is indeed the highest worship — it is circumambulation of the deity;

children.text: āsanaṃ paramā pūjā svāsanaṃ yoga uttamaḥ // NBs_12,5.16 //
children.translated_text: sitting is the highest worship — one's own seat (<s>āsana</s>) is the supreme <s>yoga</s>. [NBs 12.5.16]
Eating is the highest worship — in the form of food-offering to the deity;

children.text: abhojanaṃ parā pūjā hyupavāsapriyo hariḥ // NBs_12,5.17 //
children.translated_text: not eating is the highest worship — for <s>Hari</s> is fond of fasting. [NBs 12.5.17]
Standing is the highest worship — it is attendance upon the Self;
falling is the highest worship — in the form of prostration. [NBs 12.5.18]

children.text: bhāṣaṇaṃ paramā pūjā sarvaṃ stutimayaṃ hareḥ /
children.translated_text: Speaking is the highest worship — everything is a hymn of praise to <s>Hari</s>;

children.text: maunaṃ tu paramā pūjā maunaṃ vyākhyānamasya tat // NBs_12,5.19 //
children.translated_text: silence is the highest worship — silence is His exposition. [NBs 12.5.19]
Activity itself is the highest worship — one acts as His manifestation;

children.text: aceṣṭā hi parā pūjā joṣamāsveti vedavāk // NBs_12,5.20 //
children.translated_text: inactivity is the highest worship — 'be silent,' says the Vedic word. [NBs 12.5.20]

children.text: janmaiva paramā pūjā so'vatāro hareḥ sataḥ /
children.translated_text: Birth itself is the highest worship — it is the incarnation of <s>Hari</s> in the good;

children.text: jīvanaṃ paramā pūjā jīvankāryāṇi sādhayet // NBs_12,5.21 //
children.translated_text: living is the highest worship — while alive, one should accomplish [one's] duties. [NBs 12.5.21]
Long life is the highest worship — <s>yogins</s> are long-lived;

children.text: svalpāyuḥ paramā pūjā sadyo hyasmādvimucyate // NBs_12,5.22 //
children.translated_text: short life is the highest worship — one is quickly liberated from this [world]. [NBs 12.5.22]
Death is the highest worship — in the form of offering the worn garland [back to God];

children.text: śoko hi paramā pūjā śoko vairāgyasādhanam // NBs_12,5.23 //
children.translated_text: grief is indeed the highest worship — grief is the means of <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion). [NBs 12.5.23]

children.text: harṣa eva parā pūjā hṛṣṭarūpaḥ sadā hariḥ /
children.translated_text: Joy itself is the highest worship — <s>Hari</s> is always of joyful form;

children.text: puṣṭistu paramā pūjā svasthacitto hi puṣṭimān // NBs_12,5.24 //
children.translated_text: nourishment is the highest worship — one who is well-nourished has a healthy mind. [NBs 12.5.24]

children.text: kṛśatvaṃ paramā pūjā kṛśagātrā hi yoginaḥ /
children.translated_text: Emaciation is the highest worship — <s>yogins</s> are indeed lean of body;

children.text: lābha eva parā pūjā lābhaḥ santoṣakāraṇam // NBs_12,5.25 //
children.translated_text: gain itself is the highest worship — gain is the cause of contentment. [NBs 12.5.25]
Loss itself is the highest worship — by that very thing one is liberated;

children.text: guṇa eva parā pūjā sādhūnāṃ saṃmato guṇī // NBs_12,5.26 //
children.translated_text: virtue itself is the highest worship — the virtuous one is esteemed by the good. [NBs 12.5.26]

children.text: doṣā eva parā pūjā nirahaṅkāratā yataḥ /
children.translated_text: Faults themselves are the highest worship — because [they lead to] the absence of ego;

children.text: māna eva parā pūjā mānyate parameśvaraḥ // NBs_12,5.27 //
children.translated_text: honor is the highest worship — [for] the Supreme Lord is honored. [NBs 12.5.27]
Dishonor is the highest worship — the <s>yogin</s> attains <s>siddhi</s> through humility;

children.text: dhanaṃ hi paramā pūjā dhanaṃ dharmasya sādhanam // NBs_12,5.28 //
children.translated_text: wealth is indeed the highest worship — wealth is the instrument of <s>dharma</s>. [NBs 12.5.28]
Poverty is the highest worship — <s>Brahman</s> is attained by the possessionless;

children.text: apramādaḥ parā pūjā hyapramatto hi siddhyati // NBs_12,5.29 //
children.translated_text: vigilance is the highest worship — the vigilant one indeed attains perfection. [NBs 12.5.29]
Heedlessness is the highest worship — because one forgets what is [ordinarily] to be done;

children.text: suṣuptiḥ paramā pūjā samādhiryogināṃ hi saḥ // NBs_12,5.30 //
children.translated_text: deep sleep is the highest worship — that is the <s>samādhi</s> of <s>yogins</s>. [NBs 12.5.30]

children.text: karmayogaḥ parā pūjā karma brahmārpaṇaṃ harau /
children.translated_text: <s>Karmayoga</s> (yoga of action) is the highest worship — all action is an offering to <s>Brahman</s> in <s>Hari</s>;

children.text: bhaktiyogaḥ parā pūjā yo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ // NBs_12,5.31 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bhaktiyoga</s> (yoga of devotion) is the highest worship — 'he who is my devotee is dear to me.' [NBs 12.5.31]
<s>Jñānayoga</s> (yoga of knowledge) is the highest worship — through knowledge one attains <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute liberation);
the fourth state (<s>turīya</s>) is the highest worship — in the form of direct realization. [NBs 12.5.32]
Hearing is the highest worship — the Supreme Lord is heard;

children.text: mananaṃ paramā pūjā mananaṃ dhyānasādhanam // NBs_12,5.33 //
children.translated_text: reflection (<s>manana</s>) is the highest worship — reflection is the means of meditation. [NBs 12.5.33]
If any <s>guru</s> equal to my <s>guru</s> should touch one's ear,

children.text: sarvameva tadā pūjā devasya layarūpiṇī // NBs_12,5.34 //
children.translated_text: then everything becomes worship of the deity in the form of <s>laya</s> (absorption). [NBs 12.5.34]
Of all <s>layas</s> (absorptions), because it causes forgetfulness of the world,

children.text: śreṣṭhaṃ nādānusandhānaṃ nādo hi paramo layaḥ // NBs_12,5.35 //
children.translated_text: the pursuit of <s>nāda</s> (inner sound) is the best — for <s>nāda</s> is the supreme <s>laya</s>. [NBs 12.5.35]

children.text: makarandaṃ pibanbhṛṅgo yathā gandhaṃ na kāṅkṣati /
children.translated_text: Just as the bee, drinking nectar, does not seek the fragrance [of the flower],
The mind absorbed in <s>nāda</s> (inner sound) does not crave for sense-objects. [NBs 12.5.36]
The Elixir of Devotion (<s>Bhaktirasāyana</s>)
Now hear the elixir of devotion, which is the essence of all established doctrines;
that elixir is the medicine for birth, death, old age, and disease. [NBs 13.1]
For <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>artha</s> (wealth), <s>kāma</s> (desire), and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), as well as for <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) and <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion),
and for the purification of the inner instrument (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) is the supreme means. [NBs 13.2]
That love by which this individual soul attains the nature of <s>Brahman</s>,
accomplished by <s>Sanaka</s> and the others — that is called <s>bhakti</s> (devotion). [NBs 13.3]
If all the wealth of spiritual means is present but devotion is not,
then all that wealth of means is as useless as husking chaff. [NBs 13.4]
If there is no other spiritual means but devotion to the great Lord exists,
then dispassion, knowledge, and liberation are gradually attained. [NBs 13.5]
Indeed no one can become liberated without the grace of the Lord;
liberation comes only through the grace of the Lord — this is the firm conclusion. [NBs 13.6]
The Lord, being perfect and complete, does not need anything;
pleased by love alone, he quickly bestows the supreme grace. [NBs 13.7]
'That unwavering love which the undiscriminating have toward sense-objects —
may it not depart from my heart as I remember You.' [NBs 13.8]
If devotion characterized by love exists toward the Supreme Self, the Lord of the universe,

children.text: sarvameva tadā siddhaṃ kartavyaṃ nāvaśiṣyate // NBs_13.9 //
children.translated_text: then everything is already accomplished; nothing remains to be done. [NBs 13.9]
The direct experience (<s>aparokṣānubhūti</s>) that is described in the <s>Vedānta</s>

children.text: premalakṣaṇabhaktestu pariṇāmaḥ sa eva hi // NBs_13.10 //
children.translated_text: is indeed the culmination of devotion characterized by love. [NBs 13.10]
When the meaning of the scriptures has been fully comprehended and love for the great Lord has arisen,
through the mode of the bliss of love, duality is forgotten. [NBs 13.11]
Everything is pervaded by <s>Vāsudeva</s>; the world has <s>Vāsudeva</s> as its essence;
thus, for one who is immersed in the flavor of duality, what knowledge remains? [NBs 13.12]
