<s>Vāsudeva</s> is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the Supreme Self, higher than the highest;

children.text: antarbahiśca tatsarvaṃ vyāpya nārāyaṇaḥ sthitaḥ // NBs_13.13 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> stands pervading everything, within and without. [NBs 13.13]
Atomic, vast, thin, gross, possessing qualities, beyond qualities, great —
with such words, the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> devotee praises <s>Keśava</s>. [NBs 13.14]

children.text: śivaḥ kartā śivo bhoktā śivaḥ sarveśvareśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s> is the creator, <s>Śiva</s> is the enjoyer, <s>Śiva</s> is the Lord of all lords;

children.text: śiva atmā śivo jīvaḥ śivādanyanna vidyate // NBs_13.15 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s> is the Self, <s>Śiva</s> is the individual soul — there exists nothing other than <s>Śiva</s>. [NBs 13.15]
With the eight forms of space, wind, fire, water, earth, the individual self (<s>kṣetrajña</s>), sun, and moon,

children.text: aṣṭābhiraṣṭamūrtiṃ ca śāṃbhavaḥ stauti śaṅkaram // NBs_13.16 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Śāmbhava</s> (devotee of Śiva) praises <s>Śaṅkara</s> as the eight-formed one. [NBs 13.16]

children.text: idaṃ yadā pariṇataṃ prema tajjñānameva hi
children.translated_text: When this love reaches maturity, it is indeed knowledge itself.
Now another line of reasoning:
A child speaks to his father, saying 'father, father' —

children.text: na punastātaśabdārthaṃ sa tu jānāti kiñcana // NBs_13.17 //
children.translated_text: but he does not know anything of the meaning of the word 'father.' [NBs 13.17]
When he gradually comes to understand the meaning of the word 'father,'

children.text: tadā tu satyamevāyaṃ tāta ityeti niścayam // NBs_13.18 //
children.translated_text: then indeed he arrives at the certainty that 'this is truly my father.' [NBs 13.18]
Similarly, the devotee, worshipping God through the methods taught in the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>śāstras</s>,

children.text: vyutpatiṃ paramāṃ prāpya mukto bhavati hi kramāt // NBs_13.19 //
children.translated_text: having attained the highest understanding, gradually becomes liberated. [NBs 13.19]

children.text: kiṃ ca lakṣaṇabhedo hi vastubhedasya kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: Moreover, a difference in definition is the cause of a difference in substance;
but no difference in definition between the devotee and the knower is seen in the scriptures. [NBs 13.20]
Dispassion, inquiry, purity, control of the senses,

children.text: vede ca paramā prītistadekaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ dvayoḥ // NBs_13.21 //
children.translated_text: and supreme delight in the <s>Veda</s> — this is the one definition common to both. [NBs 13.21]
In the chapter called <s>Bhaktiyoga</s> in the <s>Gītā</s>, the characteristics of devotion
that are stated in eight verses — I have seen those very [characteristics] in the knowers. [NBs 13.22]
One worships saying 'I am Yours,' while another says 'You alone are I' —

children.text: iti kiñcidviśeṣepi pariṇāmaḥ samo dvayoḥ // NBs_13.23 //
children.translated_text: despite this slight difference, the culmination is the same for both. [NBs 13.23]
When the devotee sees God within and without,
even while contemplating 'I am a servant,' he forgets the 'I' [in 'servant']. [NBs 13.24]
This has been observed in exclusive devotees such as <s>Nārada</s> and others;
I shall state a slight distinction — listen with concentrated mind. [NBs 13.25]
If the devotee is absorbed in the essence of the Lord, and the wise one is [also] absorbed in the essence of the Lord,
though both are of one essence, they are slightly different. [NBs 13.26]
The wise, from the flavor of knowledge, have become devoid of the flavor of everything else;
but devotees never [become devoid of] the excess flavor of love. [NBs 13.27]
Now the question:
Objection: Without knowledge, liberation does not exist, even by hundreds of reasonings;

children.text: tathā bhaktiṃ vinā jñānaṃ nāstyupāyaśatairapi // NBs_13.28 //
children.translated_text: similarly, without devotion, knowledge does not exist, even by hundreds of methods. [NBs 13.28]
From devotion, knowledge; from knowledge, liberation — this is the common sequence;

children.text: jñāninastu vasiṣṭhādyā bhaktā vai nāradādayaḥ // NBs_13.29 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and others are knowers, while <s>Nārada</s> and others are devotees. [NBs 13.29]
What is the reason for such an arrangement?
Let it be determined. To this it is said — hear the wonderful reason: [NBs 13.30]
I shall explain with an illustration, by which the meaning will become clear;

children.text: syāttāpasya ca pāpasya gaṃgāsnānena hi kṣayaḥ // NBs_13.31 //
children.translated_text: by bathing in the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, there is the destruction of both heat and sin. [NBs 13.31]
For one who seeks relief from heat, there is also the destruction of sin;
for one who seeks relief from sin, the heat also is destroyed. [NBs 13.32]
The destruction of heat, the destruction of sin, and bathing — these three are the same for both;

children.text: tathāpyekastu śaityārthī śuddhyarthī tu dvitīyakaḥ // NBs_13.33 //
children.translated_text: yet one seeks coolness, while the other seeks purification. [NBs 13.33]
Just as from the difference in intention, a difference in name arose for those two —
in the same way, those wise ones who have resorted to God for the sake of liberation, [NBs 13.34]

children.text: bhaktyā jñānamavāpyaiva ye muktā jñānino hi te /
children.translated_text: having obtained knowledge through devotion, those who are liberated — they are indeed the knowers;
while those who, disgusted with <s>saṃsāra</s>, have resorted to <s>Hari</s> for the sake of devotion, [NBs 13.35]
and then, through the power of devotion, knowledge arose naturally —

children.text: tajjñānaṃ prāpya muktā ye te bhaktā iti varṇitāḥ // NBs_13.36 //
children.translated_text: those who, having obtained that knowledge, are liberated — they are described as devotees. [NBs 13.36]
Dispassion, devotion, higher knowledge, and liberation are the same for both;
yet from the difference in attitude, a difference in name arose for them. [NBs 13.37]
For the knower, liberation is the primary fruit, and devotion serves as its means;
for the devotee, devotion itself is primary, and liberation comes incidentally. [NBs 13.38]
By this reasoning too, O wise one, devotion to the Lord is the most excellent.
Now another glory [of devotion]:
The Supreme Self, <s>Hari</s> himself, is of the nature of supreme bliss; [NBs 13.39]
placing devotion to <s>Śiva</s> foremost, he partakes of the elixir of devotion;
<s>Sanaka</s> and the others, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and the others, <s>Nandin</s>, <s>Skanda</s>, <s>Śuka</s>, and the rest, [NBs 13.40]
even having attained his abode, partake of the elixir of devotion.

children.text: dvaitaṃ vinā kathaṃ bhaktiriti tatrottaraṃ śṛṇu // NBs_13.41 //
children.translated_text: 'How can there be devotion without duality?' — hear the answer to that: [NBs 13.41]
Duality, prior to the attainment of knowledge, leads to delusion; but after knowledge is attained, by the wise,
duality is conceived for the sake of devotion — and it is more beautiful than non-duality. [NBs 13.42]
Thus it is also said in the <s>Bhāgavata</s>:
'Those who delight in the Self, the sages free from bondage, nevertheless
perform causeless devotion to <s>Urukrama</s> (Viṣṇu) — such are the qualities of <s>Hari</s>.' [NBs 13.43]
When the bliss of equal essence has arisen, even duality is like nectar,
like [the relationship] between friends, between husband and wife — between the individual self and the Supreme Self. [NBs 13.44]

children.text: hṛdaye vasati prītyā lokarītyā ca lajjate /
children.translated_text: She dwells in the heart with love and is bashful in the ways of the world —
like a bride who is full of wonder and eternally blissful. [NBs 13.45]
Non-duality is the ultimate truth; duality exists for the purpose of worship;

children.text: tādṛśī yadi bhaktiścetsā tu muktiśatādhikā // NBs_13.46 //
children.translated_text: if there is such devotion, it is worth more than a hundred liberations. [NBs 13.46]

children.text: priyatamahṛdaye vā khelatu premarītyā padayugaparicaryāṃ preyasī vā vidhattām /
children.translated_text: Let [love] play in the heart of the most beloved in the manner of love, or let the beloved perform the service of his feet — let the realized one sport in thought-free <s>samādhi</s> (absorption), or in the practice of worship — both are indeed equal. [NBs 13.47]

children.text: viharatu viditārtho nirvikalpe samādhau nanu bhajanavidhau vā taddvayaṃ tulyameva // NBs_13.47 //
viśveśvarastu sudhiyā galite'pi bhede bhāvena bhaktisahitena samarcanīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The Lord of the universe should be worshipped by the wise with the attitude of devotion, even when difference has dissolved; the Lord of one's life should be gazed upon by the clever woman through a veil of fluttering cloth, even when hearts have merged. [NBs 13.48]

children.text: prāṇeśvaraścaturayā milite'pi citte cailāñcalavyavahitena nirīkṣaṇīyaḥ // NBs_13.48 //

children.translated_text: Now, a verse based on the rasa of devotion:

children.text: yoge nāsti gatirna nirguṇavidhau sambhāvanādurgame nityaṃ nīrasayā dhiyā parihṛte dve aihikāmuṣmike /
children.translated_text: There is no progress in <s>yoga</s>, nor in the difficult-to-conceive method of the attributeless; both the worldly and the other-worldly are abandoned by the ever-dry intellect — yet some cowherd has been made his friend, and he [Kṛṣṇa] consorts with various women; sages seek our abode — what is more wondrous than this? [NBs 13.49]

children.text: gopaḥ ko'pi sakhā'kṛtaḥ sa tu punarnānāṅganāsaṅgavānasmākaṃ padamarthayanti munayaścitraṃ kimasmātparam // NBs_13.49 //
romāñcena camatkṛtā tanuriyaṃ bhaktyā mano nanditaṃ premāśrūṇi vibhūṣayantiṃ vadanaṃ kaṇṭhaṃ giro gadgadāḥ /
children.translated_text: This body is thrilled with goosebumps of wonder by devotion, the mind is delighted, tears of love adorn the face, the throat is choked with faltering speech — we who are engaged in worshipping <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> have not even a moment's leisure; the fourfold liberation itself stands at our door, eager to serve. [NBs 13.50]

children.text: nāsmākaṃ kṣaṇamātramapyavasaraḥ kṛṣṇārcanaṃ kurvatāṃ muktirdvāri caturvidhāpi kimiyaṃ dāsyāya lolāyate // NBs_13.50 //
ghanaḥ kāmo'smākaṃ tava tu bhajane'nyatra na rucistavaivāṃghridvandve natiṣu ratirasmākamatulā /
children.translated_text: Our desire for Your worship is intense and we have no taste for anything else; our delight in bowing to Your pair of feet is unequaled — [we are] desireless in our desire, yet desire-ful the moment we approach Your feet; liberation full of desire seeks us — such is Your greatness, O <s>Hari</s>! [NBs 13.51]

children.text: sakāme niṣkāmā sapadi tu sakāmā padagatā sakāmā'smānmuktirbhajati mahimā'yaṃ tava hare // NBs_13.51 //

children.translated_text: The Illuminator of the Stages in <s>Rāja-yoga</s>
Beginning with the stages and until the completion of the treatise,
in this profound <s>Bodhasāra</s>, <s>Rāja-yoga</s> is expounded. [NBs 14.1.1]
Now this 'Illuminator of the Stages' should be established in the heart,

children.text: yasya prasādamātreṇa tamo hārdaṃ vilīyate // NBs_14,1.2 //
children.translated_text: by whose grace alone the darkness of the heart dissolves. [NBs 14.1.2]
There are seven stages of ignorance and seven stages of knowledge;
seed-waking, then waking, then great-waking, [NBs 14.1.3]
waking-dream, then dream, dream-waking, and deep sleep —

children.text: iti saptavidho mohasteṣāṃ vivaraṇaṃ śṛṇu // NBs_14,1.4 //
children.translated_text: thus ignorance is sevenfold; hear their elaboration. [NBs 14.1.4]

children.text: kusūle saṃsthitaṃ bījaṃ tatra sarvo yathā drumaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a seed stored in a granary contains the entire tree within it,

children.text: tathā yatra sthitaṃ viśvaṃ na tu vyaktimupāgatam // NBs_14,1.5 //
children.translated_text: so [in this state] the universe exists but has not come to manifestation. [NBs 14.1.5]
The waking state existing in seed-form is called 'seed-waking' (<s>bījajāgrat</s>);

children.text: saṃsāraprathamāvasthā mahāmohaḥ sa eva hi // NBs_14,1.6 //
children.translated_text: it is the first state of <s>saṃsāra</s> — it is indeed the great delusion (<s>mahāmoha</s>). [NBs 14.1.6]
That very thing is called <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance), which dissolves through self-knowledge;

children.text: kusūle saṃsthitaṃ bījaṃ kṣetre nikṣipyate yadā // NBs_14,1.7 //
children.translated_text: when the seed stored in the granary is cast into the field, [NBs 14.1.7]
it reaches the state of inclination toward sprouting — that state is called 'waking' (<s>jāgrat</s>);
this is what the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s> describe as <s>mahat-tattva</s> (the great principle). [NBs 14.1.8]
And by the <s>Vedāntins</s> [it is called] 'seeing' (<s>īkṣaṇa</s>); and the general ego-sense (<s>sāmānyāhaṅkṛti</s>),
and the bliss-sheath (<s>ānandamayakośa</s>); and its witness is remembered as <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord). [NBs 14.1.9]
The specific ego-sense, like a subtle sprout, pertaining to conventional [experience],

children.text: mahājāgradbudhaiḥ proktā vyaṣṭyavasthātraye tu sā // NBs_14,1.10 //
children.translated_text: is called 'great-waking' (<s>mahājāgrat</s>) by the wise; it is the individual-soul state in the three conditions. [NBs 14.1.10]
The three states called waking, dream, and deep sleep are known as [the subdivisions of] 'waking';

children.text: jāgradeva yadā jīvo manorājyaṃ karoti hi // NBs_14,1.11 //
children.translated_text: when the individual soul, while in the waking state, engages in daydreaming, [NBs 14.1.11]

children.text: jāgrataḥ svapna iva yatsa jāgratsvapna ucyate /
children.translated_text: that which is like a dream while awake — that is called 'waking-dream' (<s>jāgratsvapna</s>);

children.text: lokaprasiddho yaḥ svapnaḥ sa svapna iti kathyate // NBs_14,1.12 //
children.translated_text: the commonly known dream is called simply 'dream' (<s>svapna</s>). [NBs 14.1.12]
When, even though waking has occurred, the objects seen in dream appear to the being
as if directly perceptible, due to impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) — that is called 'dream-waking' (<s>svapnajāgrat</s>). [NBs 14.1.13]
When the six [previous] states are abandoned, the seventh is considered 'deep sleep' (<s>suṣupti</s>);
these are the stages of ignorance — now hear the stages of knowledge. [NBs 14.1.14]
The Stages of Knowledge
The desire to know (<s>jijñāsā</s>), then inquiry (<s>vicāra</s>), then the subtle mind (<s>tanumānasā</s>),
attainment of being (<s>sattvāpatti</s>), non-attachment (<s>asaṃsakti</s>), and the state of non-perception of objects (<s>padārthābhāvinī</s>); [NBs 14.2.1]
the seventh is called <s>turya</s> (the fourth state), and beyond that is <s>turyātīta</s> (beyond the fourth).
Their alternative names are:

children.text: mumukṣā ca samakṣā ca parīkṣā ca parokṣakā // NBs_14,2.2 //
children.translated_text: The desire for liberation (<s>mumukṣā</s>), direct vision (<s>samakṣā</s>), examination (<s>parīkṣā</s>), indirect knowledge (<s>parokṣā</s>), [NBs 14.2.2]
direct knowledge (<s>aparokṣā</s>), great initiation (<s>mahādīkṣā</s>), and the supreme state (<s>parākakṣā</s>) — these are the seven.
The first is called the stage of qualification (<s>adhikāra</s>); the second is that of hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>); [NBs 14.2.3]
the third is predominantly reflection (<s>manana</s>); the fourth is meditation (<s>nididhyāsana</s>).

children.text: sākṣātkāraḥ pañcamī syātṣaṣṭhī pariṇatiḥ smṛtā // NBs_14,2.4 //
children.translated_text: Direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>) is the fifth; the sixth is called maturation (<s>pariṇati</s>). [NBs 14.2.4]

children.text: saptamī tu parā kāṣṭhā saiva turyamitīritā /
children.translated_text: The seventh is the supreme limit, and that very [state] is declared to be <s>turīya</s> (the fourth state);

children.text: prathamāyāṃ tu vidyārthī dvitīyāyāṃ padārthavit // NBs_14,2.5 //
children.translated_text: in the first [stage], one is a student of knowledge; in the second, a knower of the meaning of words. [NBs 14.2.5]
In the third, one becomes free from doubt; in the fourth, one becomes a <s>paṇḍita</s> (learned);
in the fifth, one attains experience; in the sixth, one is overwhelmed by bliss. [NBs 14.2.6]
The seventh is the innate <s>turīya</s>; beyond that is <s>turīyātīta</s> (beyond the fourth);

children.text: bhūmikā tritayaṃ pūrvaṃ tvatra jāgraditi smṛtam // NBs_14,2.7 //
children.translated_text: the first triad of stages is considered here as the waking state. [NBs 14.2.7]
Here, for the seeker, <s>saṃsāra</s> remains as before;

children.text: caturthī svapna ityuktā svapnābhaṃ yatra vai jagat // NBs_14,2.8 //
children.translated_text: the fourth is called the dream state, where the world [appears] dream-like. [NBs 14.2.8]

children.text: suṣuptiḥ śithilā gāḍhā dvividhā''dyā tu pañcamī /
children.translated_text: <s>Suṣupti</s> (deep sleep) is of two kinds — loose and deep; the first [loose] is the fifth;
the sixth is deep <s>suṣupti</s>; the seventh is called <s>turīya</s>. [NBs 14.2.9]
Here a question [arises]:

children.text: saṃsārameva yo vetti mokṣamārgaṃ na vetti yaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who knows only <s>saṃsāra</s> and does not know the path of liberation —

children.text: tasya saṃsāriṇaḥ pūrvaṃ mumukṣā jāyate katham // NBs_14,2.10 //
children.translated_text: how does the desire for liberation (<s>mumukṣā</s>) first arise in such a worldly person? [NBs 14.2.10]
As are one's dispositions (<s>saṃskāra</s>s), so are one's latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>s);
how then does the desire for liberation arise in one with dispositions of <s>saṃsāra</s>? [NBs 14.2.11]

children.text: mokṣe tu viṣayo nāsti sukhaṃ na viṣayairvinā /
children.translated_text: In liberation there are no sense-objects; there is no pleasure without sense-objects —

children.text: iti mūḍhadhiyāṃ pūrvaṃ mumukṣaiva kathaṃ bhavet // NBs_14,2.12 //
children.translated_text: thus, for those of deluded intellect, how can the desire for liberation first arise? [NBs 14.2.12]
Here is the answer:

children.text: niṣkāmā vā sakāmā vā bhaktirviṣṇoḥ śivasya vā /
children.translated_text: Whether desireless or with desire, devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s> or <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: saprema hṛdaye jātā mumukṣākāraṇaṃ hi tat // NBs_14,2.13 //
children.translated_text: arising with love in the heart — that is indeed the cause of the desire for liberation. [NBs 14.2.13]
Once, with a pure disposition, austerity was performed on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>;
by the ripening of that merit, the desire for liberation arises in the virtuous. [NBs 14.2.14]
Through the service of food, water, and the like to the learned and dispassionate,
through association [with them] and through affection — the desire for liberation may arise spontaneously. [NBs 14.2.15]
Thus it is said [in the <s>Gītā</s>]:
Among thousands of men, scarcely one strives for perfection;

children.text: yatatāmapi siddhānāṃ kaścinmāṃ vetti tattvataḥ // NBs_14,2.16 //
children.translated_text: and among those who strive and succeed, scarcely one knows me in truth. [NBs 14.2.16]
And thus in the <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s> [<s>Yoga Vāsiṣṭha</s>]:
Like a turtle's neck entering through a hole in a yoke floating on the restless ocean —
after many births, a discriminating person is born. [NBs 14.2.17]

children.text: sopāstīnāṃ karmaṇāṃ tu cittaśuddhiḥ phalaṃ matam /
children.translated_text: The fruit of actions performed with auxiliary rites is considered to be purification of the mind;

children.text: vedanecchā vedanaṃ vā citrā satkarmaṇāṃ gatiḥ // NBs_14,2.18 //
children.translated_text: the desire to know, or knowledge itself — the course of good actions is varied. [NBs 14.2.18]
Even by the <s>Vedānta</s>s, for the seeker, action is therefore made a companion;
faith, tranquility of mind, self-restraint, and withdrawal [of the senses],
along with the desire for liberation — the first stage is the attainment of the means (<s>sādhana-saṃpat</s>). [NBs 14.2.19]
The seeker of liberation should first approach the <s>Guru</s>;
'One should approach the <s>Guru</s> alone for the sake of knowledge' — thus says the <s>śruti</s>. [NBs 14.2.20]
Its characteristics:
'May liberation alone be mine, O Lord; may there be no vision of <s>saṃsāra</s>' —

children.text: iti yaḥ sudṛḍho bhāvo mumukṣālakṣaṇaṃ hi tat // NBs_14,2.21 //
children.translated_text: one who has such a firm conviction — that is the mark of the desire for liberation. [NBs 14.2.21]

children.text: puṇyakṣetreṣu yā buddhiḥ puṇyatīrtheṣu yā ruciḥ /
children.translated_text: The faith that [arises] toward sacred places, the taste for holy pilgrimage sites,

children.text: mokṣadharmeṣu yā śraddhā mumukṣālakṣaṇaṃ hi tat // NBs_14,2.22 //
children.translated_text: the conviction in the duties leading to liberation — that is the mark of the desire for liberation. [NBs 14.2.22]
One who procures scriptures of knowledge from wherever [possible] and examines them,

children.text: cintayaṃstasya tātparyaṃ mumukṣālakṣaṇaṃ hi tat // NBs_14,2.23 //
children.translated_text: contemplating their purport — that is the mark of the desire for liberation. [NBs 14.2.23]
Even with great effort, one should seek the company of the learned,
placing one's head at the lotus of their feet. [NBs 14.2.24]
One should ask questions that are in the mind, and reveal one's own ignorance;
one should contemplate in the heart the purport of their answers. [NBs 14.2.25]

children.text: nādharmo rocate yasya yasya dharme sadā ruciḥ /
children.translated_text: One in whom <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) does not please, in whom there is always a taste for <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: kāmyadharme na ca śraddhā mumukṣālakṣaṇaṃ hi tat // NBs_14,2.26 //
children.translated_text: and in whom there is no faith in desire-motivated duty — that is the mark of the desire for liberation. [NBs 14.2.26]
One who, by nature, feels weariness toward the activities
of attachment, aversion, pride, anger, greed, and jealousy — that is the mark of the desire for liberation. [NBs 14.2.27]
Here is a verse:

children.text: prekṣituṃ na vijānāti prekṣaṇe kurute manaḥ /
children.translated_text: She does not know how to look [at him], yet she directs her mind to seeing;

children.text: lajjāṃ jahāti naiveyaṃ vayaḥsandhirayaṃ kila // NBs_14,2.28 //
children.translated_text: she does not abandon her modesty — this indeed is the juncture of adolescence. [NBs 14.2.28]
The bride, having set out for her husband's home, is distressed and weeps;

children.text: idamatra samādhānaṃ padamagre dadhāti yat // NBs_14,2.29 //
children.translated_text: the remedy here is that she places her foot forward [and proceeds]. [NBs 14.2.29]
Now the second [stage].
This is the definition of <s>prakṛti</s> (nature); this is the definition of <s>vikṛti</s> (modification);
this is the essential nature of <s>puruṣa</s> (the person) — that is the mark of inquiry. [NBs 14.3.1]

children.text: idaṃ satyamidaṃ mithyā tvidaṃ cetyamiyaṃ hi cit /
children.translated_text: 'This is real, this is false; this is the knowable, this is consciousness;

children.text: idaṃ brahma tviyaṃ māyā tadvicārasya lakṣaṇam // NBs_14,3.2 //
children.translated_text: this is <s>Brahman</s>, this is <s>māyā</s>' — that is the mark of inquiry. [NBs 14.3.2]

children.text: kasminnidaṃ kutaścedaṃ kimidaṃ kena vā kṛtam /
children.translated_text: 'In what does this [exist]? From what [does] this [come]? What is this? By whom is it made?
How does this dissolve?' — that is the mark of inquiry. [NBs 14.3.3]

children.text: ka īśvaraśca ko jīvaḥ kā muktiḥ kintu bandhanam /
children.translated_text: 'Who is <s>Īśvara</s>? Who is the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul)? What is liberation? What is bondage?

children.text: kiṃ dvaitaṃ kathamadvaitaṃ tadvicārasya lakṣaṇam // NBs_14,3.4 //
children.translated_text: What is duality? How is non-duality?' — that is the mark of inquiry. [NBs 14.3.4]
Through the discrimination of the eternal and the non-eternal — [seeing] reality in the eternal substance,
and worthlessness in the non-eternal — that is the mark of inquiry. [NBs 14.3.5]
Thus, through the practice of yoga with the mind, for the learned,

children.text: jāyate brahmavādo yaḥ sā tu prauḍhavicāraṇā // NBs_14,3.6 //
children.translated_text: when the discourse on <s>Brahman</s> arises — that is the mature inquiry. [NBs 14.3.6]
This self, whose nature is self-luminous — if asked 'Who are you?', one would reply:

children.text: ahamajño na jānāmi māmahaṃ ko'hamityuta // NBs_14,3.7 //
children.translated_text: 'I am ignorant, I do not know myself; who am I?' [NBs 14.3.7]
Without the awareness of the self, the statement 'I am ignorant' cannot arise;

children.text: ātmānameva no vetti tarhyayaṃ jaḍa eva hi // NBs_14,3.8 //
children.translated_text: if he truly does not know the self, then he is indeed inert matter. [NBs 14.3.8]
And being inert, how could it illuminate pots and the like?
Therefore the conclusion is: this [self] does indeed know itself. [NBs 14.3.9]

children.text: athātmānamasau vetti parantu na hi vetti yat /
children.translated_text: Now, he does know the self; but what he does not know
is the distinction within himself — therefore he possesses ignorance of his own nature. [NBs 14.3.10]

children.text: atra brūmo viśeṣo'tra nāstyavācye tu cidghane /
children.translated_text: Here we say: there is no distinction in the inexpressible, dense consciousness;

children.text: nirviśeṣasvarūpe'tra viśeṣaṃ yadi vetti saḥ // NBs_14,3.11 //
children.translated_text: in this nature that is without distinction — if he [claims to] know a distinction [therein] — [NBs 14.3.11]
that [distinction], being knowable, is superimposed upon oneself — what then is the use of such inquiries?
One who is known as without distinction possesses a nature that is without distinction. [NBs 14.3.12]
Then full knowledge has arisen, and inquiry itself is purposeless.

children.text: kiñjātīyaḥ kiṃguṇo'sau kiñceṣṭo nāma tasya kim // NBs_14,3.13 //
children.translated_text: Of what species is he? Of what qualities? Of what activity? What is his name? [NBs 14.3.13]
Of what mode? Of what form? Of what modification do you ask?

children.text: na jātirnirguṇasyāsya niśceṣṭo nāma tasya na // NBs_14,3.14 //
children.translated_text: He who is without qualities has no species; he is without activity; he has no name. [NBs 14.3.14]
Without mode, without form, without modification — he is established.
If one says, 'He is to be inquired into in the form of <s>Sat-Cit-Ānanda</s>' — [NBs 14.3.15]
he is indeed already known in the form of <s>Sat-Cit-Ānanda</s>.
Explanation of this:

children.text: ayamātmā svamātmānaṃ sadrūpeṇa na vetti kim // NBs_14,3.16 //
children.translated_text: Does not this self know itself in the form of existence (<s>sat</s>)? [NBs 14.3.16]
'I am' — [the self] knows this; it does not [say] 'I am not' — state this!
'I am' — [the self] knows this; the self is to be known thereafter. [NBs 14.3.17]

children.text: dharme cārthe ca kāme ca mokṣe ca yatate svayam /
children.translated_text: It strives of its own accord in <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s> (wealth), <s>kāma</s> (desire), and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation);
therefore, regarding its nature as existence, there is no ignorance of the self. [NBs 14.3.18]
One who says 'I am conscious; I know pots and the like' —

children.text: svasya cidrūpatāyāṃ tu tasyājñānaṃ na vidyate // NBs_14,3.19 //
children.translated_text: regarding his own nature as consciousness — there is no ignorance for him. [NBs 14.3.19]
Everything is dear for one's own sake; therefore one's own self is the dearest;
hence the nature of the self as bliss (<s>ānanda</s>) is clearly established. [NBs 14.3.20]
Therefore, the nature of the self as <s>Sat-Cit-Ānanda</s> is manifest;
hence, in this self-luminous [self] whose nature is <s>Sat-Cit-Ānanda</s> — [NBs 14.3.21]
Just as blue color in the sky, water in desert-mirages,
and darkness in water are superimposed by another consciousness —
ignorance is superimposed by consciousness upon itself within itself. [NBs 14.3.22]
The very nature of delusion (<s>moha</s>) is to shine forth in the form of the universe;

children.text: vidyayā nāśite mohe tatsvabhāvo na bhāsate // NBs_14,3.23 //
children.translated_text: when delusion is destroyed by knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>), its nature does not shine [anymore]. [NBs 14.3.23]
At the dissolution of the mental modifications (<s>vṛtti</s>s) illuminated by the consciousness of the <s>jīva</s>, there is dissolution;

children.text: vṛttīnāṃ pralayādeva na bhāsante'tra vṛttayaḥ // NBs_14,3.24 //
children.translated_text: from the dissolution of the modifications alone, the modifications do not shine here. [NBs 14.3.24]
But the consciousness of the <s>jīva</s> continues as before;
the <s>jīva</s>, whose nature is the illumination of modifications, does not perish there. [NBs 14.3.25]
Similarly, at the dissolution of delusion illuminated by the consciousness of the self —

children.text: moha eva nivarteta yathā pūrvaṃ lasatyasau // NBs_14,3.26 //
children.translated_text: delusion alone ceases; as before, that [consciousness] shines. [NBs 14.3.26]
Just as when white and black cloths come into the light of a lamp,

children.text: tau tayā kāśitau paścāttannāśe sā yathā sthitā // NBs_14,3.27 //
children.translated_text: they are illuminated by it; after their removal, [the light] remains as it was. [NBs 14.3.27]
Just as delusion and knowledge come in succession into the light of the self,

children.text: tayā prakāśitau paścāttannāśena sā yathā sthitā // NBs_14,3.28 //
children.translated_text: they are illuminated by it; after their destruction, [the light of the self] remains as it was. [NBs 14.3.28]
Through the tradition of <s>Vedānta</s>, in the contemplation of 'it is done' and the like,
together with the impossibility [of it being otherwise] — the notion of the contrary [is overcome]. [NBs 14.3.29]

children.text: sā naśyati dvitīyāyāṃ prajñātaikṣṇyaṃ ca vardhate /
children.translated_text: That [contrary notion] perishes in the second [stage], and the sharpness of wisdom increases;

children.text: dṛśyate tvagrayayā buddhyā sā buddhistasya jāyate // NBs_14,3.30 //
children.translated_text: the penetrating intellect that sees [the truth] — that intellect arises in him. [NBs 14.3.30]
Just as in the purification of gold performed with alkalis and fire-treatment,

children.text: śyāmikā kṣayamāyāti kevalaṃ hema tiṣṭhati // NBs_14,3.31 //
children.translated_text: the dark tarnish is eliminated and pure gold alone remains — [NBs 14.3.31]
so too, in the purification of <s>Brahman</s> performed with hundreds of knowledge-treatments,

children.text: avidyā kṣayamāyāti kevalaṃ brahma tiṣṭhati // NBs_14,3.32 //
children.translated_text: <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is eliminated and <s>Brahman</s> alone remains. [NBs 14.3.32]
Now the determination of the third stage.
From the practice of the second stage, the third — <s>tanumānasā</s> (attenuated mind) —
which is another name for <s>manana</s> (reflection) — arises. Hear its characteristics: [NBs 14.4.1]
Just as for one dwelling in a dark room, through prolonged contemplation,

children.text: sūkṣmo'rtho bhāsate yadvattṛtīyāyāṃ tathā muneḥ // NBs_14,4.2 //
children.translated_text: a subtle meaning shines forth — so too for the sage in the third [stage]. [NBs 14.4.2]
Just as a child, like a <s>śūdra</s>, attains the status of a twice-born

children.text: yathā dvijatvamāyāti tathā jātyantaraṃ muneḥ // NBs_14,4.3 //
children.translated_text: through the instruction of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> — so too the sage undergoes a change of birth [status]. [NBs 14.4.3]

children.text: dṛṣṭvā lokasthitiṃ lolāṃ savismaya iva sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having seen the unsteady nature of the world, standing as if in wonder,

children.text: antareva viṣīdeta tṛtīyālakṣaṇaṃ hi tat // NBs_14,4.4 //
children.translated_text: he would grieve inwardly — that is the mark of the third [stage]. [NBs 14.4.4]
The day has gone, the night has gone, life has gone, youth has gone —

children.text: kadā sthāsyāmi niṣṭhāyāṃ yatra moho na bādhate // NBs_14,4.5 //
children.translated_text: when shall I abide in the final state where delusion does not afflict? [NBs 14.4.5]
When a day has passed, he repeatedly grieves: 'What was achieved by the day that passed?'

children.text: gatāyāṃ ca tathā rātrau kiṃ me rātryā'nayā'rjitam // NBs_14,4.6 //
children.translated_text: And when a night has passed: 'What was achieved by this night of mine?' [NBs 14.4.6]
Even when non-prohibited pleasures come by chance,
he regards them as if prohibited — that state is [called] <s>tanumānasā</s> (attenuated mind). [NBs 14.4.7]
He is embarrassed by the praise of the worldly-minded, as if he were being censured;
he finds contentment in the praise of those who know the supreme truth. [NBs 14.4.8]
Here is a verse:
Her husband is always eager to give himself to her,

children.text: ādātuṃ na vijānāti nityamutkaṇṭhitā'pi sā // NBs_14,4.9 //
children.translated_text: but she does not know how to receive — though she too is constantly eager. [NBs 14.4.9]
The woman desirous of good fortune, the hero who bestows delight —
but through the state of naïveté, there is some delay. [NBs 14.4.10]

children.text: idameva kathaṃ nu syāditi kliśyati cātmanā /
children.translated_text: 'How indeed can this be?' — thus she torments herself;

children.text: bhūyaḥ kaṭākṣakalahaṃ karoti svāminā saha // NBs_14,4.11 //
children.translated_text: and she engages in a quarrel of sidelong glances with her lord. [NBs 14.4.11]
The determination of the fourth stage.
From the practice of the third stage, <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> are destroyed;
the arising of <s>sattva</s> is the fourth [stage], which has the form of <s>nididhyāsana</s> (profound meditation). [NBs 14.5.1]
Here, an objection and its resolution:

children.text: bhogārthameva devattvaṃ prāptā devā na muktaye /
children.translated_text: The gods attained divinity for the sake of enjoyment, not for liberation;
because of the absence of the desire for liberation in them, the arising of <s>sattva</s> does not produce liberation [for them]. [NBs 14.5.2]
Here is a verse:
Even among the gods — <s>Śakra</s> [<s>Indra</s>], <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and others —

children.text: ye mumukṣāṃ gatāsteṣāṃ muktiprāptiḥ kimadbhutam // NBs_14,5.3 //
children.translated_text: those who attained the desire for liberation — what wonder is their attainment of liberation? [NBs 14.5.3]
Now the characteristics:
Singing the songs of liberation in solitude, and weeping [from devotion] —

children.text: romāñco gadgadaḥ kaṇṭhe sattvāpattestu lakṣaṇam // NBs_14,5.4 //
children.translated_text: horripilation and a choking of the throat are the marks of <s>sattvāpatti</s> (attainment of being). [NBs 14.5.4]
He states his own view:
When <s>Vedānta</s> has been properly studied, then <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord) is to be meditated upon;
for the bee that has attained supreme fragrance, the drinking of nectar is an additional virtue. [NBs 14.5.5]

children.text: nityo'smi śuddha evāsmi kvājñānaṃ kva ca bandhanam /
children.translated_text: 'I am eternal, I am pure indeed — where is ignorance, where is bondage?'
Such wonder and the like are the marks of <s>sattvāpatti</s>. [NBs 14.5.6]
Just as he listens to stories about himself, so he hears the teachings of the <s>Upaniṣads</s>;
just as [he listens to] another's stories, so he hears the conversations of the world. [NBs 14.5.7]
Observing the various activities of body, sense-organs, mind, vital breath,
intellect, ego, and consciousness, the sage remains as if astonished. [NBs 14.5.8]
He recognizes knowing, agency, enjoyment, birth, death, old age, and the like
as states belonging to another, and knows his own state as different from those. [NBs 14.5.9]
Having emerged from the net of delusion, like a bird from a net,
having attained the state of moving in the sky, he finds blessedness. [NBs 14.5.10]

children.text: daridra iva saṃprāpya nidhānaṃ vismayaṃ gataḥ /
children.translated_text: Like a poor man who, having found a treasure, is struck with wonder —

children.text: īśvarānugraho jāta iti nṛtyati hṛṣyati // NBs_14,5.11 //
children.translated_text: 'The grace of the Lord has arisen!' — thus he dances and rejoices. [NBs 14.5.11]
He who, even by pleasant sense-objects — sounds, touches,
smells, forms, and tastes — is not made such, having attained <s>sāttvika</s> bliss. [NBs 14.5.12]
Seeing the self as if separate, even while present in states [of the body],

children.text: cāṇḍālīmiva yo māyāṃ na spṛśandūravatsthitaḥ // NBs_14,5.13 //
children.translated_text: he who does not touch <s>māyā</s> (illusion), as one avoids a <s>caṇḍālī</s> (untouchable woman), standing far away — [NBs 14.5.13]
he who, with indifference, sees the world in the waking state as dream-like —
this is described as the mark of the ripening of <s>sattvāpatti</s>. [NBs 14.5.14]
Here is a verse:
The state has been properly known; the mind too has been set on grasping [it];
what remains is just the taking — having made it an ornament of oneself. [NBs 14.5.15]

children.text: ahaṃ tvanūḍhā taruṇī na kasyāpi parigrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I am an unmarried young woman, the possession of no one;

children.text: enameva variṣyāmi patiṃ ko vā hasiṣyati // NBs_14,5.16 //
children.translated_text: I shall choose this one alone as my husband — who will laugh [at me]?' [NBs 14.5.16]
One struck by the sidelong glance of some doe-eyed woman
falls into ruin — so too does this one [fall] for the beloved of liberation. [NBs 14.5.17]
Just as a humming beetle, hearing the buzzing of a bee, hums along in its hole,

children.text: brahmāsmīti tathaivāyaṃ bhavituṃ brahma guñjati // NBs_14,5.18 //
children.translated_text: so too this one buzzes 'I am <s>Brahman</s>' to become <s>Brahman</s>. [NBs 14.5.18]
The Fifth Stage
Through the practice of the [previous] four stages, the fifth is <s>asaṃsakti</s> (non-attachment);
it is the first state of deep sleep, the new sprout of direct realization. [NBs 14.6.1]

children.text: sā'parokṣā naīva niśā śṛṇu tasyāstu lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: That is <s>aparokṣā</s> (direct knowledge), not [mere] darkness — hear its characteristics:
The first [is] self-wonder, characterized by the bliss of one's own nature. [NBs 14.6.2]
That very [experience] is the remembrance of one's <s>Brahman</s>-nature; that very [experience] is the forgetting of one's individual-soul nature;
that very [experience] is the death of ignorance; that very [experience] is indeed immortality. [NBs 14.6.3]
It has manifested, and yet it is not of the nature of having manifested;

children.text: kathaṃ bhūyo bhramatyeṣa bhrāntireva gatā yadi // NBs_14,6.4 //
children.translated_text: how would this [person] be deluded again, if delusion itself has departed? [NBs 14.6.4]
Just as round stones, having fallen from the peak of a mountain,

children.text: dhvaṃsaṃtyeva na tiṣṭhanti vikārāstadvadatra hi // NBs_14,6.5 //
children.translated_text: shatter and do not remain — so too are the modifications [of the mind] here. [NBs 14.6.5]
Whatever modification the sage observes with a half-glance,

children.text: sadyaḥ patatyasau pṛthvyāṃ nottiṣṭhati yathā punaḥ // NBs_14,6.6 //
children.translated_text: it immediately falls to the ground and does not rise again. [NBs 14.6.6]

children.text: avigīte na tuṣyettu vigīte na viṣīdati /
children.translated_text: He is not pleased when praised, nor dejected when criticized;
he forgets all duties and delights in the self by the self. [NBs 14.6.7]
As if possessed by a spirit, he spontaneously follows or abandons

children.text: preritaḥ pūrvasaṃskāraiḥ karoti na karotyapi // NBs_14,6.8 //
children.translated_text: the prescribed duties of <s>varṇa</s> (class) and <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life), impelled by past impressions. [NBs 14.6.8]
Just as the eye and the rest are the means of valid knowledge in worldly knowledge,
so too the <s>Upaniṣads</s> are regarded as such in the domain of knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>. [NBs 14.6.9]
That by whose witnessing the means of knowledge are [validated] — who doubts that?
Having abandoned servitude to injunctions, having attained the state of doing nothing,
having become one who possesses nothing, he does not worry about anything. [NBs 14.6.10]
Like a rock of the <s>Himālaya</s> — even when the sun's heat is applied to it —

children.text: bahirantaśca saṃpūrṇaḥ śītalatvaṃ na muñcati // NBs_14,6.11 //
children.translated_text: he who, full within and without, does not abandon his coolness. [NBs 14.6.11]
If crystal knew its crystal-nature, water knew its water-nature,

children.text: gaganaṃ gaganatvajñaṃ yadi syātsā daśā citaḥ // NBs_14,6.12 //
children.translated_text: and sky knew its sky-nature — that would be the state of consciousness. [NBs 14.6.12]
Just as a wise man is not bewildered even in many-colored playhouses,
so this self is not bewildered even in many-colored playhouses [of existence]. [NBs 14.6.13]
The <s>yogī</s> plays, sleeps, laughs, and speaks,
[seen by] the outward-facing people, like <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva) [is seen] by the <s>piśācas</s> (goblins). [NBs 14.6.14]
<s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>) does not deserve to be compared with one who has attained the supreme reality;
<s>Indra</s> [merely] aspires to that state — he [the sage] does not desire Indra-hood. [NBs 14.6.15]
Just as fire-cooked meat remains attached to the bones as before,
yet is [essentially] detached — so too the sage in his own body. [NBs 14.6.16]
Here are verses:
Turning away [from others], she gazes upon her husband with
a look gracious with love — for her youth has arrived. [NBs 14.6.17]
She does not play with her girl-friends; she is slack in household duties;

children.text: rahaḥ paśyati cihnāni prāptā prāṇapateḥ sukham // NBs_14,6.18 //
children.translated_text: in secret she looks at the signs — she has attained the joy of her lord of life. [NBs 14.6.18]

children.text: na veṣo vihitaḥ kaścinna vā vacanacāturī /
children.translated_text: No special attire is prescribed, nor eloquence of speech;
but through the extreme constancy of love, the young girl has nurtured <s>Hari</s>. [NBs 14.6.19]

children.text: nālaṅkṛtā no kulīnā na vidagdhā na sundarī /
children.translated_text: She is neither adorned, nor of noble birth, nor clever, nor beautiful;

children.text: yasyāṃ tu ramate svāmī sā saubhāgyavatī vadhūḥ // NBs_14,6.20 //
children.translated_text: yet the bride in whom the lord delights — she is the fortunate one. [NBs 14.6.20]

children.text: yasmindeśe sitā nāsti taddeśyo vetti kiṃ sitām /
children.translated_text: In a land where sugar does not exist, does the native of that land know sugar?

children.text: sa eva veda mādhuryaṃ yenaivāsvāditā sitā // NBs_14,6.21 //
children.translated_text: Only he knows its sweetness who has tasted sugar. [NBs 14.6.21]
Having abandoned thirst for trifles, the sage has attained the state of being free from thorns;
with his soul satisfied by his own elixir, he grows day by day. [NBs 14.6.22]
The Sixth Stage
Through the practice of the five stages, the sixth arises — <s>padārthābhāvinī</s> (non-perception of objects);

children.text: ṣaṣṭhī ghanasuṣuptiḥ syānmahādīkṣeti sā bhavet // NBs_14,7.1 //
children.translated_text: it is dense deep sleep, and it is called the 'great initiation' (<s>mahādīkṣā</s>). [NBs 14.7.1]
It is called the 'great sleep' (<s>mahānidrā</s>), in which, whirled by bliss,

children.text: padārthavismṛtiḥ saiva proktā pariṇatiśca sā // NBs_14,7.2 //
children.translated_text: there is forgetfulness of objects — that very [experience] is called 'ripening' (<s>pariṇati</s>). [NBs 14.7.2]
Its characteristics:
Just as kings, mounted on a man-borne palanquin, move about as if asleep,

children.text: calanti tadvatsvānande supta eva calatyasau // NBs_14,7.3 //
children.translated_text: so too this one, asleep in his own bliss, moves about. [NBs 14.7.3]
In his sacrifice of meditation, the senses beginning with sight
present themselves of their own accord as sacrificial animals, as in the sacrifice of <s>Rantideva</s>. [NBs 14.7.4]
When full awakening has arisen, the mind, intellect, senses, and the rest,

children.text: apūrṇāḥ pūrṇatāṃ yānti kā vācyā tasya pūrṇatā // NBs_14,7.5 //
children.translated_text: though incomplete, attain completeness — what then can be said of his own completeness? [NBs 14.7.5]
Everything is nectar for him — whatever he eats or drinks;

children.text: yatra tiṣṭhati sā kāśī sa japo yatprajalpati // NBs_14,7.6 //
children.translated_text: wherever he stays is <s>Kāśī</s>; whatever he mutters is <s>japa</s> (recitation). [NBs 14.7.6]
His wandering is pilgrimage; the sage's sleeping is <s>samādhi</s>;

children.text: yaṃ paśyati sa viśveśaḥ śṛṇotyupaniṣacca sā // NBs_14,7.7 //
children.translated_text: whomever he sees is <s>Viśveśvara</s> (Lord of the Universe); what he hears is the <s>Upaniṣad</s>. [NBs 14.7.7]
The nectar of love is drunk; the supreme art is embraced;

children.text: bhujyate paramānando yoginā na sa bhoginā // NBs_14,7.8 //
children.translated_text: supreme bliss is enjoyed by the <s>yogī</s>, not by the sensualist. [NBs 14.7.8]

children.text: saṃprāpte paramānande na śocati gataṃ vayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having attained supreme bliss, he does not grieve for the passing of time;
the past, the present, and the future — all has become bliss. [NBs 14.7.9]
Now the Seventh [Stage]
Then, having transcended the sixth, [the sage] enters the seventh, called <s>turīya</s> (the fourth);
it is also called the 'great enclosure' (<s>mahākakṣā</s>); it is itself the 'hidden deep sleep.' [NBs 14.8.1]

children.text: yoganidreti sā proktā parā kāṣṭheti sā smṛtā /
children.translated_text: It is called <s>yoganidrā</s> (yogic sleep); it is remembered as the 'supreme limit' (<s>parā kāṣṭhā</s>);
and [called] the 'unsurpassed,' the 'innate' (<s>sahaja</s>), and 'abiding in one's own nature.' [NBs 14.8.2]
<s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, and the other [gods] themselves resort to silence in that [state];

children.text: sā tu varṇayituṃ śakyā na kenāpi kadācana // NBs_14,8.3 //
children.translated_text: it can never be described by anyone, at any time. [NBs 14.8.3]
The thorn of ignorance, clinging by chance to the tender limb of consciousness,

children.text: taṃ bodhakaṇṭakenāyaṃ vinivārya sukhaṃ sthitaḥ // NBs_14,8.4 //
children.translated_text: this one has warded it off with the thorn of knowledge and abides in bliss. [NBs 14.8.4]

children.text: amṛtajaladhau yasminvārttā na mīnataraṃgayor na ca paricayaḥ pārāvārasthiterapi kutracit /
children.translated_text: In that ocean of nectar, there is no news of fish or waves, nor any acquaintance with the condition of shore or farther shore anywhere;

children.text: samarasaparabrahmānandapraṇunnavikalpanaḥ sahajagalitadvaitajvālaḥ sa bhāti mahāmuniḥ // NBs_14,8.5 //
children.translated_text: with all mental constructs dissolved by the bliss of the supreme <s>Brahman</s> of equal essence, with the flame of duality naturally extinguished — that great sage shines. [NBs 14.8.5]

children.text: baṃdhadhvaṃsamabhīpsunā sumanasā jijñāsayā tīvrayā jñāte brahmaṇi bādhitākṣaviṣaye bodhe camatkurvati /
children.translated_text: By the virtuous one who desires the destruction of bondage, with intense desire to know — when <s>Brahman</s> is known and the sense-objects are negated, when awakening causes wonder,

children.text: svāntarmantṛvimānamānyavivṛtivyāvṛttinirbhaṅgako bhāti jñānasukhātmakaḥ svayamayaṃ yogyāpagānāṃ patiḥ // NBs_14,8.6 //
children.translated_text: destroying the unfolding and withdrawal within the counseling-chamber of his inner mind — this one, whose nature is the bliss of knowledge, shines by himself — the lord of the rivers of the qualified. [NBs 14.8.6]

children.text: vācā maunamayī gatiḥ sthitimayī nidrāmayo jāgaro nidrā bodhamayī niśā dinamayī naktaṃmayo vāsaraḥ /
children.translated_text: His speech has become silence; his movement has become stillness; his waking has become sleep; his sleep has become waking; his night has become day; his night has become day;

children.text: karma brahmamayaṃ jagatsukhamayaṃ kiñcinna kiñcinmayaṃ durlaṅghyaṃ guṇavartma laṅghitavato vārttā kathaṃ varṇyatām // NBs_14,8.7 //
children.translated_text: his action has become <s>Brahman</s>; the world has become bliss; nothing is anything — how can the condition of one who has crossed the insurmountable path of qualities be described? [NBs 14.8.7]
Extremely destitute of strength and manliness, possessing nothing, his pride dissolved —

children.text: tenaiva nītā ripavo vināśaṃ na ye hatāstāta mahendramukhyaiḥ // NBs_14,8.8 //
children.translated_text: by him alone were the enemies destroyed that were not slain, O dear one, by the great <s>Indra</s> and others. [NBs 14.8.8]
The knower of <s>Brahman</s>, having become a son in [the family of] <s>Bhavānī</s> (the mother goddess), through the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>,
is fondled on his own body by <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self), <s>Sadāśiva</s>. [NBs 14.8.9]
The Determination of the Meaning of the Teaching on Stages
The three [initial] stages constitute the waking state; the fourth is called dream;
these represent the seeker's (<s>sādhaka</s>) condition, in degrees, for the <s>yogīs</s>. [NBs 14.9.1]

children.text: pañcamīṃ tu samārabhya siddhāvasthaiva sā tridhā /
children.translated_text: Beginning from the fifth, it is the accomplished state (<s>siddha</s>), and that is threefold;
an illustration for these three states is presented here. [NBs 14.9.2]
The first state of deep sleep — whatever bliss is obtained therein,

children.text: suṣupteryā ghanāvasthā tasyāmapi tadeva hi // NBs_14,9.3 //
children.translated_text: and the dense state of deep sleep — in that too, it is the same. [NBs 14.9.3]
The bliss in dense deep sleep is the same bliss in profound deep sleep;
even in the seventh <s>turīya</s>, the experience of bliss is the same. [NBs 14.9.4]

children.text: tathā ya eva pañcamyāṃ ṣaṣṭhyāmapi sa eva hi /
children.translated_text: Likewise, that which is in the fifth is the same in the sixth;

children.text: turyāyāmapi saptamyāṃ brahmānandaḥ sa eva hi // NBs_14,9.5 //
children.translated_text: even in the seventh <s>turīya</s>, that <s>Brahmānanda</s> (bliss of Brahman) is the same. [NBs 14.9.5]
The gradation is in the duration of abidance, based on the gradation of practice;
but in the direct experience itself, O Bodiless One, the gradation is slight. [NBs 14.9.6]
As long as sugar has not been tasted, it has indeed not been tasted;

children.text: ekadāsvāditā cetsā naiva nāsvāditā bhavet // NBs_14,9.7 //
children.translated_text: but once it has been tasted, it can never be untasted. [NBs 14.9.7]

children.text: jātā cetsā tu jātaiva jātu nājātatāṃ bhajet /
children.translated_text: If it has arisen, it has indeed arisen — it can never revert to the un-arisen state;

children.text: kathaṃ bhūyo bhramatyeṣa bhrāntireva gatā yadi // NBs_14,9.8 //
children.translated_text: how would this [person] be deluded again, if delusion itself has departed? [NBs 14.9.8]
Now a distinction:
The <s>turīya</s> in its first appearance has the character of a lightning flash;
then [it becomes] like the glow of a flickering lamp; then like a steady lamp. [NBs 14.9.9]
Then like the light of the sun — the seventh is long-lasting;
devoid of rising and setting, [it pervades] day, fortnight, season, and year. [NBs 14.9.10]

body.translated_text: Abundant, unmoving, complete — beautiful with supreme bliss. [NBs 14.9.11]

children.translated_text: Those in whose art of meditation the rows of qualities dissolve,
by whose compassionate sidelong glance, immediate liberation is attained — [NBs 14.9.12]
those who have taken refuge in the fifth, sixth, or seventh [stage] —
for them there is no return, even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages). [NBs 14.9.13]

children.text: pūrvāvasthācatuṣke ye sthitā dehaṃ vihāya te /
children.translated_text: Those who remain in the first four states — when they abandon the body,
having obtained another body, they continue the practice of <s>Brahman</s>. [NBs 14.9.14]
They are called <s>yogabhraṣṭas</s> (fallen from yoga), gradually heading toward <s>Brahman</s>;
the <s>yogīs</s> and the yoga-accomplished ones [include] <s>Datta</s> and others, <s>Janaka</s> and others. [NBs 14.9.15]
Some later ones also, having received the grace of the Lord

children.text: svarūpānubhavaṃ prāptā muktāste sarva eva hi // NBs_14,9.16 //
children.translated_text: and having attained the experience of their own nature — they are all indeed liberated. [NBs 14.9.16]
Some are established in <s>suṣupti</s> (deep sleep), some in dense deep sleep,
some in profound deep sleep — for all of them, the nectar [of bliss] is the same. [NBs 14.9.17]
Page 305
The Arrangement of States
Now hear the chapter called 'the arrangement of states,'
upon whose thorough examination, nothing remains to be examined. [NBs 15.1]
Waking, dream, deep sleep, and also deluded <s>samādhi</s>,
stupor, death, and <s>turīya</s> (the fourth) — these seven states are declared. [NBs 15.2]
Waking, dream, and deep sleep are manifest; deluded <s>samādhi</s>,

children.text: mūrcchā mṛtyusturīyaṃ ca vyaktā nityānubhūtitaḥ // NBs_15.3 //
children.translated_text: stupor, death, and <s>turīya</s> are also manifest — from constant experience. [NBs 15.3]
The deluded <s>samādhi</s>, designated as '<s>bhavapratyaya</s>' (born of worldly existence),
was previously [described] in the account of the divisions of <s>asaṃprajñāta samādhi</s>. [NBs 15.4]
Those established in that <s>samādhi</s>, having conquered <s>Indra</s> and the rest, attained the lordship of heaven;
death and stupor are well-known; now <s>turīya</s> is described. [NBs 15.5]
According to the <s>Vedānta</s> tradition, through the firmness of <s>nididhyāsana</s> (deep meditation),
the dissolution of the mind in the Supreme Self is called <s>turya</s> (the fourth state). [NBs 15.6]
Therein, <s>Brahman</s> is directly realized, destroying the root-ignorance (<s>mūlāvidyā</s>).
Here a question:
O sage, the spectacle of <s>saṃsāra</s> is equal in dream and waking. [NBs 15.7]
Then by what distinguishing feature is the difference of designation between those two? Tell us.
Here is the answer:

children.text: jānīhi prathamaṃ tāta bhedaṃ vismṛtibodhayoḥ // NBs_15.8 //
children.translated_text: First understand, dear one, the difference between forgetting and awakening. [NBs 15.8]
Then you will know the difference between dream and waking — listen.
Forgetting is when [something] does not appear; awakening is the ascertainment of falsity. [NBs 15.9]

children.text: jāgarānantaraṃ nidrā tatra svapno yadā bhavet /
children.translated_text: When, after waking, sleep [comes] and therein dream occurs,

children.text: svapne syājjāgarābhānaṃ na tu jāgarabodhanam // NBs_15.10 //
children.translated_text: in dream there is the appearance of waking, but not the awakening [to its falsity]. [NBs 15.10]

children.text: jāgaro'yaṃ tu mithyeti buddhiḥ svapne na vartate /
children.translated_text: The cognition 'this waking is false' does not occur in dream;
rather, by the forgetting of waking, there is the seeing of dream-objects in dream. [NBs 15.11]
This is the essential nature of dream; now hear about waking.

children.text: svapnasyānantaraṃ tāta jāgaro hi yadā bhavet // NBs_15.12 //
children.translated_text: Dear one, when waking occurs after dream, [NBs 15.12]
then, through the cognition of the falsity of the dream, there is awakening from the dream of the Self.
And another [point]:

children.text: svapne tu yādṛśī tāta bhavejjāgaravismṛtiḥ // NBs_15.13 //
children.translated_text: Dear one, whatever forgetting of waking occurs in dream, [NBs 15.13]
such forgetting of the world of dream does not exist in waking.
In waking, the dream is remembered, and its falsity is seen. [NBs 15.14]
In dream, waking is not remembered, nor is its falsity seen.
By this great distinction lies the difference between dream and waking. [NBs 15.15]
Now another question:
But in deluded <s>samādhi</s>, in stupor, death, and deep sleep,

children.text: turīye ca na dṛśyaśrīstarhi teṣāṃ bhidā kutaḥ // NBs_15.16 //
children.translated_text: and in <s>turīya</s>, there is no glory of the visible — so whence the difference among them? [NBs 15.16]
Here is the answer:

children.text: siddhikāmanayā yaistu tapa ugraṃ kṛtaṃ mahat /
children.translated_text: Those by whom intense and great austerity was performed with the desire for <s>siddhi</s> (supernatural powers),
by whom even the body was forgotten — it was consumed by worms and insects. [NBs 15.17]

children.text: neyaṃ mūrcchā na rogo'yaṃ na mṛtyurjīvanādayam /
children.translated_text: This is not stupor, this is not disease, this is not death — because of [continued] living;
because of the absence of the bliss of deep sleep, it is clearly not deep sleep. [NBs 15.18]
Because of the absence of the attainment of one's true nature, and because of delusion, it is not <s>turīya</s>;

children.text: dṛśyabhānaṃ tu nāstyāsu tāvatā na kṛtārthatā // NBs_15.19 //
children.translated_text: the appearance of the visible is absent in those [states] — by that alone, the goal is not achieved. [NBs 15.19]
When, after their emergence, <s>saṃsāra</s> also persists,
when there is no vision of the Self, <s>saṃsāra</s> is unsublated — therefore. [NBs 15.20]
I shall tell an illustration here — listen with attentive mind.

children.text: svapne tu vismṛtaṃ jāgrajjāgratsvapne na bādhitam // NBs_15.21 //
children.translated_text: In dream, waking is forgotten; [but] in waking, dream is not unsublated. [NBs 15.21]
Therefore, after [waking], waking [sublates] dream — as it actually is;
in waking, the dream is sublated — thereby it has become false. [NBs 15.22]

children.text: tathā mūḍhasamādhau tu vismṛtaṃ sakalaṃ jagat /
children.translated_text: Similarly, in deluded <s>samādhi</s>, the entire world is forgotten;
but after emergence, it persists as before. [NBs 15.23]
In <s>turīya</s>, the universe is sublated — therefore it has become false;

children.text: vyutthāne'pi munestāta tanmithyaiva na vāstavam // NBs_15.24 //
children.translated_text: even after emergence, for the sage, dear one, it remains false, not real. [NBs 15.24]
Just as one who, having seen a rope-snake, goes to another place —

children.text: yadā punaḥ samāyāti tadā tasmādbibhetyasau // NBs_15.25 //
children.translated_text: when he returns again, he fears it. [NBs 15.25]

children.text: nāyaṃ sarpa iti jñātvā yadi deśāntaraṃ gataḥ /
children.translated_text: But if, having known 'this is not a snake,' he goes to another place —

children.text: yadā punaḥ samāyāti tadā tasmādbibheti na // NBs_15.26 //
children.translated_text: when he returns again, he does not fear it. [NBs 15.26]
Similarly, one who from deluded <s>samādhi</s> has gone to the forgetting of <s>saṃsāra</s> —

children.text: yadā vyutthānamāpnoti tadā saṃsārajaṃ bhayam // NBs_15.27 //
children.translated_text: when he attains emergence, then [there is] fear born of <s>saṃsāra</s>. [NBs 15.27]
But if from the <s>samādhi</s> of the wise one has gone to the forgetting of <s>saṃsāra</s> —
when he attains emergence, because [saṃsāra] has been sublated, he does not fear. [NBs 15.28]
If liberation of the embodied being were [achieved] merely by forgetting,

children.text: suṣuptirjāyate nityaṃ tayā mukto na kiṃ bhavet // NBs_15.29 //
children.translated_text: deep sleep occurs every day — would one not be liberated by it? [NBs 15.29]
Therefore, among all [states], <s>turīya</s> is the highest and most distinctive;

children.text: ṣaḍapyavasthā etasyāḥ kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm // NBs_15.30 //
children.translated_text: the six other states are not worth even a sixteenth part of it. [NBs 15.30]
If <s>Garuḍa</s> were to fly with full speed for the duration of <s>Brahmā</s>'s lifetime,

children.text: na cāpnoti tathāpyenaṃ dūrāddūrataraiva sā // NBs_15.31 //
children.translated_text: he would still not reach it — it is ever farther and farther away. [NBs 15.31]

children.text: śraddhā yadyasti vedānte tīvrā yadi mumukṣutā /
children.translated_text: If there is faith in <s>Vedānta</s>, if the desire for liberation is intense,

children.text: dhyānābhyāsastathā gāḍhaḥ sarvatra sulabhaiva sā // NBs_15.32 //
children.translated_text: and if the practice of meditation is deep — it is easily attainable everywhere. [NBs 15.32]
Death, stupor, and deep sleep are not <s>tapas</s> — therefore they are fruitless;
established deluded <s>samādhi</s> is intense <s>tapas</s> of great fruit. [NBs 15.33]

children.text: vidyā vidvatsamādhistu tena mokṣaprado hi saḥ /
children.translated_text: Knowledge [is true] knowledge; the <s>samādhi</s> of the wise — therefore it is liberation-granting;
such is the arrangement of the seven states. [NBs 15.34]

children.text: saptāvasthā imāḥ santi cittasyaiva citestu na /
children.translated_text: These seven states belong to the mind (<s>citta</s>) alone, not to consciousness (<s>cit</s>);
the mind is the abode of states, while consciousness is the witness of states. [NBs 15.35]
If this arrangement of states is contemplated further,
then the witness of the states directly perceives [the truth]. [NBs 15.36]
Page 324
Determination of the Morning Awakening
With wonderful arrangements of letters, with the nectar of pure meanings,
I purify my own speech through the daily routine of the chief sage. [NBs 16.1.1]

body.translated_text: The Daily Routine of the Chief Sage

children.translated_text: <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord) told <s>Gaurī</s> of the state consisting of consciousness and bliss;
I shall speak of the shadow of that teaching under the guise of a daily routine. [NBs 16.1.2]
That waking upon whose arising sleep is never again born —

children.text: sumaṅgalaṃ munīṃdrāṇāṃ prātarjāgaraṇaṃ hi tat // NBs_16,1.3 //
children.translated_text: that is the most auspicious morning awakening of the chief sages. [NBs 16.1.3]
Page 326
Determination of Purification
In the body, sense-organs, mind, <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), intellect, ego, and <s>citta</s> (mind-stuff),
the sense of self in what is impure — that is the cause of impurity. [NBs 16.2.1]
With the waters of the contemplation of witnesshood, and with the clay of <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion),
one should diligently perform purification that removes the stain of [identification with] the scent [of the body]. [NBs 16.2.2]
Whatever earning of auspiciousness is [achieved] by such a method —
that itself is the morning purification of the chief sages, effecting purity. [NBs 16.2.3]
For those made serene by <s>Jñānayoga</s> (the yoga of knowledge), the desire for liberation is called the 'face';
its purification with the water of faith — that indeed is the washing of the face. [NBs 16.2.4]
Page 330
Now, Morning Remembrance
In the morning, the sages remember the glory of the divine <s>Savitṛ</s> (the sun-god),

children.text: vareṇyaṃ taddhiyaḥ sākṣi tadevāsmīti saṃtatam // NBs_16,3.1 //
children.translated_text: the most excellent — 'That witness of [our] intellects — that indeed I am,' [they remember] continuously. [NBs 16.3.1]
Through the method of agreement and difference (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), in waking, dream, and deep sleep,

children.text: yadekaṃ kevalaṃ jñānaṃ tadevāhamahaṃ hi tat // NBs_16,3.2 //
children.translated_text: that which is the one, absolute knowledge — that indeed I am; I am indeed that. [NBs 16.3.2]
Knowledge and ignorance, their objects, and the ego-sense too —

children.text: prakāśyante yena bhūmnā tadahaṃ hyahameva tat // NBs_16,3.3 //
children.translated_text: by which plenitude they are illuminated — that I am; I am indeed that. [NBs 16.3.3]
<s>Viśva</s>, <s>Taijasa</s>, and <s>Prājña</s> — I am not [any of these] in my true nature;

children.text: yataste tu prakāśyante tadahaṃ nāsmi cetarat // NBs_16,3.4 //
children.translated_text: that by which they are illuminated — that I am; I am not anything other. [NBs 16.3.4]
In this expanse of knowledge and ignorance, when knowledge and ignorance are destroyed,

children.text: yatsacchiṣṭaṃ paraṃ brahma hyahaṃ tannetaratsmaret // NBs_16,3.5 //
children.translated_text: what remains as the real, the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — I am that; one should not remember anything else. [NBs 16.3.5]
Page 336
Now, Determination of the Time of Bathing
'Having seen the eastern direction seized by the red rays [of dawn], one should bathe' — from this instruction, bathing [is determined]. [NBs 16.4.1]
Namely:
When the sleep of delusion is perishing, when the darkness is dissolving,
when the sun of knowledge ascends the peak of the mountain of inquiry, [NBs 16.4.2]
when the directions become somewhat luminous, when the delusion of directions has departed,
when the jackal of doubt has perished, when the early dawn of redness has appeared — [NBs 16.4.3]
Page 339
Now, Determination of Bathing
One who is immersed from toenail to crown in the pure lake of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> of knowledge,

children.text: yaḥ snāti mūlamaṃtreṇa sarvadaiva sa nirmalaḥ // NBs_16,5.1 //
children.translated_text: who bathes with the root <s>mantra</s> — he is always pure. [NBs 16.5.1]
Page 341
Now, Wearing of Garments
Then the sage, having donned the garment called 'the grace of devotion' —

children.text: yatrodayaḥ saiva pūrvā kāṣṭhā tasyāśca sanmukhaḥ // NBs_16,6.1 //
children.translated_text: wherever there is arising [of knowledge], that is the eastern direction, and he faces it. [NBs 16.6.1]
Page 342
Now, Determination of Wearing the Sacred Thread and Other [Items]
The sacred [threads] are the meanings of the subtle scriptures — sharp-pointed and pure;

children.text: śātanā kutsitasyaite kuśā iti nirūpitāḥ // NBs_16,7.1 //
children.translated_text: these are determined to be <s>kuśa</s> (sacred grass) that cuts away what is base. [NBs 16.7.1]
Having become one who holds the sacred [thread], the sage, by the right-hand path —
whose sacred thread is the <s>Vedānta-sūtra</s>, whose tuft is the <s>Atharvaśikhā</s> — [NBs 16.7.2]

body.translated_text: should commence the rite of <s>Brahman</s>, with the desire to know (<s>jijñāsā</s>) as the long <s>tilaka</s>-mark.

children.translated_text: Page 344
Now, Determination of <s>Ācamana</s> (Sipping of Water)
Having placed the inert [world] in the palm of the hand, like <s>Agastya</s> (the pot-born one) [drinking] the ocean —
when the king of <s>yogins</s> sips, that is the supreme <s>ācamana</s>. [NBs 16.8.1]
Page 346
Now, Determination of the Morning <s>Sandhyā</s> (Twilight Worship)
Now the determination of the morning <s>sandhyā</s> is set forth as applicable.
The birth of the mind is the birth of the world; the destruction of the mind is the dissolution of the world. [NBs 16.9.1]
Since through its opening and closing [of the eyes], arising and dissolution [occur],
for one who is habituated to the practice of <s>samādhi</s>, due to prior <s>saṃskāras</s> (impressions), [NBs 16.9.2]
that arising from <s>samādhi</s> is the <s>sandhi</s> (juncture) — the juncture is here indeed.
Therein too, through the instruction of <s>gurus</s> who have attained the truth, [NBs 16.9.3]

body.text: khaṇḍitaṃ nānusandhānaṃ sā sandhyetyucyate budhaiḥ // NBs_16,9.4 //
body.translated_text: the unbroken meditation — that is called <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight worship) by the wise. [NBs 16.9.4]

children.translated_text: Page 348
Now, Determination of <s>Prāṇāyāma</s> (Breath Control)
The vital breath within the body is called <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>;
that very [breath], by the difference of its movements, has acquired ten designations. [NBs 16.10.1]
Its movement is principally twofold — upward and downward;
moving upward, it is <s>prāṇa</s>; moving downward, it is <s>apāna</s>. [NBs 16.10.2]

children.text: apānaḥ karṣati prāṇaṃ prāṇo'pānaṃ ca karṣati /
children.translated_text: <s>Apāna</s> draws <s>prāṇa</s>, and <s>prāṇa</s> draws <s>apāna</s>;

children.text: anayoḥ śṛṅkhalā dehe tena jīvo na niścalaḥ // NBs_16,10.3 //
children.translated_text: the chain of these two is in the body — therefore the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) is not still. [NBs 16.10.3]

children.text: cale vāte calaṃ cittaṃ niścale niścalaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: When the breath moves, the mind moves; when [breath is] still, [the mind] becomes still;

children.text: citte cale calaḥ prāṇo niścale niścalo bhavet // NBs_16,10.4 //
children.translated_text: when the mind moves, <s>prāṇa</s> moves; when [mind is] still, [prāṇa] becomes still. [NBs 16.10.4]
Some attain the stillness of mind through the conquest of <s>prāṇa</s> alone;
some attain the stillness of <s>prāṇa</s> through the conquest of mind alone. [NBs 16.10.5]
Some attain the stillness of mind through the conquest of both;

children.text: iti yogagatijñānāṃ trividhā yogināṃ gatiḥ // NBs_16,10.6 //
children.translated_text: thus the threefold path of <s>yogins</s> is known to those versed in the way of <s>yoga</s>. [NBs 16.10.6]

children.text: prāṇadvārā manaḥ sādhyaṃ mataṃ hi haṭhayoginām /
children.translated_text: That the mind is to be mastered through the gateway of <s>prāṇa</s> — this is the view of <s>Haṭhayogins</s>;
that the mind is to be mastered by the mind itself — this is [the view] of <s>Jñānayogins</s>. [NBs 16.10.7]
Those who employ both mind and <s>prāṇa</s> together are considered the most excellent;

children.text: cecchuṣkahaṭhino mūḍhāste bhaṇḍā na tu yoginaḥ // NBs_16,10.8 //
children.translated_text: but the dry <s>haṭha</s>-practitioners who are deluded — they are charlatans, not <s>yogins</s>. [NBs 16.10.8]
They are called half-<s>yogins</s>, <s>yogins</s> seeking minor <s>siddhis</s> (powers).

children.text: piṅgaleḍā suṣumṇā ca mukhyāstisrastu nāḍiṣu // NBs_16,10.9 //
children.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalā</s>, <s>Iḍā</s>, and <s>Suṣumnā</s> — these are the three chief among the <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels). [NBs 16.10.9]
<s>Iḍā</s> is on the left, <s>Piṅgalā</s> is on the other [right] side, and <s>Suṣumnā</s> runs through the middle;
the vital breath always flows through the left and right passages. [NBs 16.10.10]
When both passages of <s>prāṇa</s> are blocked by the accomplished <s>yogin</s>,
then <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), like a serpent, enters the channel of its own accord. [NBs 16.10.11]
<s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>, the supreme life-force, rests at the base;

children.text: tāmutthāpya tayā sārdhaṃ suṣumṇāṃ prāṇa āviśet // NBs_16,10.12 //
children.translated_text: having raised her, <s>prāṇa</s> should enter the <s>suṣumnā</s> together with her. [NBs 16.10.12]
When <s>prāṇa</s>, flowing through the <s>suṣumnā</s>, has reached the <s>brahmarandhra</s> (crown aperture),

children.text: tatra niścalatāṃ yāte mano niścalatāṃ vrajet // NBs_16,10.13 //
children.translated_text: and when it becomes still there, the mind too becomes still. [NBs 16.10.13]
If the mind alone is restrained by the <s>jñāna-yogin</s> (the yogin of knowledge),
<s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> cease at that very moment through the cessation of the mind. [NBs 16.10.14]
Therefore the established conclusion is one and the same for the <s>haṭha-yogin</s> and the <s>vijñāna-yogin</s>;
knowing this to be as stated in the scriptures, [one should make] the determination regarding <s>prāṇa</s> and mind. [NBs 16.10.15]

body.translated_text: The sage should perform <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control) accompanied by the dissolution of the mind. [NBs 16.10.16]

children.translated_text: Now the offering of water (<s>arghya</s>):
Three offerings of full handfuls, with the water of the mental <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
should be given to the witness of all actions, for the purification of all sins. [NBs 16.11.1]
'This visible [world] exists, I am the seer' — this is the first offering of the wise;

children.text: brahma satyaṃ jaganmithyā dvitīyor'ghastataḥ paraḥ // NBs_16,11.2 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Brahman</s> is real, the world is unreal' — this is the second offering, higher than the first. [NBs 16.11.2]
'This [world] does not exist; I alone am' — this is the third offering, the supreme;
by such an offering of water, the Sun of Consciousness is pleased. [NBs 16.11.3]
Now the determination of <s>Gāyatrī</s> <s>japa</s> (recitation):
Remembering the God who is of the form of an unbroken sphere, full of light,
'from instruction, there is constant repetition' — this is from the <s>Vedānta-sūtra</s>. [NBs 16.12.1]
One should stand and recite the <s>Gāyatrī</s> three hundred and eight times;

children.text: gāyantaṃ trāyatte yasmādgāyatrī tena sā smṛtā // NBs_16,12.2 //
children.translated_text: because it protects the one who sings, it is remembered as '<s>Gāyatrī</s>.' [NBs 16.12.2]
In the form of the Inner Controller, the impeller of all mental activities,
the supreme light, the highest meaning of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, should be meditated upon in the orb of the sun. [NBs 16.12.3]
By the <s>Gāyatrī</s> of twenty-four syllables, which is the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>,
the pure <s>brāhmaṇa</s> effects the dissolution of the twenty-four <s>tattvas</s> (principles). [NBs 16.12.4]
Now the determination of <s>upasthāna</s> (standing salutation):
The sage, extending both his straight, outstretched arms, wearing the sacred thread —

children.text: sāṃkhyayogau nijau bāhū upatiṣṭheta bhāskaram // NBs_16,13.1 //
children.translated_text: [which represent] <s>Sāṅkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s> — should salute the sun. [NBs 16.13.1]
Salutation to <s>Savitṛ</s> (the Sun), the one eye of the world, the cause of the world's creation, sustenance, and destruction,
who is the embodiment of the three <s>Vedas</s>, who bears the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), who is the Self of <s>Viriñci</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, and <s>Śaṅkara</s>. [NBs 16.13.2]
Now the determination of the fire-offering (<s>homa</s>) with its subsidiary offerings:

children.text: evaṃ samāpya vidhinā prātaḥ saṃdhyāvidhiṃ muniḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus completed the morning <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight worship) according to the prescribed method, the sage,

children.text: homasyāvasaraṃ jñātvā yajñaśālāṃ tato viśet // NBs_16,14.1 //
children.translated_text: knowing the occasion for the fire-offering, should then enter the sacrificial hall. [NBs 16.14.1]
The sacrificial hall is the third stage, the 'subtle mind' (<s>tanumānasā</s>).
One should perform the rites on the left side [using] the left, and the rites on the right side [using] the right;

children.text: saṃcareta tathā naiva prāyaścittīyate yathā // NBs_16,14.2 //
children.translated_text: one should so conduct oneself that there is no need for expiation. [NBs 16.14.2]
Now if there is a lapse in the ritual, due to the difficulty of the sacred rite,

children.text: prāyaścittavidhiṃ jñātvā tacca sadyaḥ samācaret // NBs_16,14.3 //
children.translated_text: having known the procedure for expiation, one should immediately perform it. [NBs 16.14.3]
'At that very time' — from this statement, [the need for] expiations [is established]. [NBs 16.14.4]

body.translated_text: Expiation for ritual lapse:

children.translated_text: Now the expiations:
One should conquer anger through forgiveness alone; one should conquer untruth through truth alone;

children.text: aśraddhāṃ śraddhayā jittvā dānaiḥ kṛpaṇatāṃ jayet // NBs_16,14.5 //
children.translated_text: having conquered faithlessness through faith, one should conquer miserliness through generosity. [NBs 16.14.5]
These four firm bridges are proclaimed in the <s>Setu-sāma</s>;
this is merely illustrative — one should likewise conquer the others also. [NBs 16.14.6]
One should conquer sleep through wakefulness; desire through the abandonment of mental resolve;

children.text: santoṣeṇa jayellobhaṃ mohaṃ bodhadṛśā jayet // NBs_16,14.7 //
children.translated_text: one should conquer greed through contentment; delusion should be conquered through the vision of knowledge. [NBs 16.14.7]
Pride, jealousy, and the like [should be conquered] through the contemplation that the Self is in all beings;
one should conquer other defects also through the discrimination between the eternal and the non-eternal. [NBs 16.14.8]
When the mind sinks into torpor, one should awaken it; when agitated, one should calm it again;
one should recognize when it is tainted [with passion]; when it has reached equipoise, one should not disturb it. [NBs 16.14.9]
One should not relish the taste [of bliss] there; one should become free from attachment through wisdom;
entering with one-pointed intellect, one would attain perfection. [NBs 16.14.10]
When the <s>gārhapatya</s> (household) fire is raised up, consecrated with the appropriate rites,

children.text: satyarūpaḥ svayaṃ yajvā śraddhā patnī pativratā // NBs_16,14.11 //
children.translated_text: the sacrificer himself is of the form of truth; faith is the devoted wife. [NBs 16.14.11]
The house is the body; the husband is the individual soul, covered with the ash of delusion;
the raising up of the household fire of the individual soul — that is the supreme [act]. [NBs 16.14.12]
Two oblations are offered according to the <s>agnihotra</s> (fire-sacrifice) procedure:

children.text: mamatāṃ prathamaṃ hutvā'hantāṃ ca juhuyāttataḥ // NBs_16,14.13 //
children.translated_text: first offering the sense of 'mine' (<s>mamatā</s>), and then offering the sense of 'I' (<s>ahantā</s>). [NBs 16.14.13]
When these two oblations are offered, everything becomes offered;
for those dwelling in the house of the desire for liberation, accompanied by the wife named Faith, [NBs 16.14.14]

body.translated_text: this <s>agnihotra</s> (fire-sacrifice) is the daily [duty] — that which one attains by not performing it [i.e., the consequences of neglect].

children.translated_text: Now the determination of the <s>brahmayajña</s> (worship of <s>Brahman</s>):
Non-violence, truth, non-stealing, celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), and non-possessiveness —

children.text: iti pañcāṅgulimayo yamanāmā tu satkaraḥ // NBs_16,15.1 //
children.translated_text: these five-fingered [virtues] form the auspicious hand called <s>yama</s> (restraint). [NBs 16.15.1]
Purity, contentment, self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), austerity (<s>tapas</s>), and contemplation of the Lord —

children.text: iti pañcāṅgulimayo niyamo nāma satkaraḥ // NBs_16,15.2 //
children.translated_text: these five-fingered [virtues] form the auspicious hand called <s>niyama</s> (observance). [NBs 16.15.2]
The sage, joining the two hands of <s>niyama</s> and <s>saṃyama</s> (discipline) together,
should directly perform the <s>brahmayajña</s>, which consists of the praise of <s>Brahman</s>. [NBs 16.15.3]
Thus it is said in <s>Patañjali</s>:
'From self-study, one should sit in <s>yoga</s>; from <s>yoga</s>, one should aspire to self-study;
through the perfection of <s>yoga</s> and self-study, the Supreme Self is revealed.' [NBs 16.15.4]
Whatever meritorious fruit is mentioned in the <s>Vedas</s>, <s>śāstras</s>, and <s>Purāṇas</s> —
the fruit of the <s>brahmayajña</s> is declared to be greater than all of those. [NBs 16.15.5]
Now the determination of <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation):
By whom a handful of water has been given to gods, sages, ancestors, and beings —
with the <s>mantra</s> 'I am <s>Brahman</s>' — that <s>tarpaṇa</s> is the supreme satisfaction. [NBs 16.16.1]
Now the determination of worship of the deity (<s>devapūjā</s>):
Within the belly of innumerable cosmic eggs born from the play of <s>Māyā</s>'s power — though of the nature of playful wonder and delight, yet of the nature of inner illumination —

children.text: dhyātvā kiṃcidacintyacidghanarasaṃ svānandasattādvayaṃ siddhāṃtasvarasena pūjanavidhiṃ vakṣyāmi viśvātmanaḥ // NBs_16,17.1 //
