children.translated_text: meditating on that somewhat inconceivable, dense essence of consciousness, the non-dual reality of self-existent bliss, I shall describe, in the natural flow of the established doctrine, the mode of worship of the Self of the universe. [NBs 16.17.1]

children.text: sevyaḥ śrīguruvedavākyajanitaścidbodha āvāhanaṃ sarvavyāpakatāviniścayamatiḥ pūrṇaṃ pavitrāsanam /
children.translated_text: The consciousness-knowledge born from the words of the revered <s>guru</s> and the <s>Vedas</s> is to be served — that is the invocation (<s>āvāhana</s>); the conviction of [God's] all-pervasiveness is the complete and pure seat (<s>āsana</s>);

children.text: tvatto nānyadavaimi kiṃciditi tatpuṇyāmbu pādodakaṃ tvayyevāstvacalā mameśa matirityargho'stu te suṃdaraḥ // NBs_16,17.2 //
children.translated_text: 'I know nothing other than You' — that meritorious water is the foot-washing; 'may my mind be steady in You alone, O Lord' — let that be Your beautiful offering of water (<s>arghya</s>). [NBs 16.17.2]

children.text: śītoṣṇaṃ kaṭutiktamamlamadhuraṃ kṣāraṃ vicitraṃ rasair yattasyāsya samatvabhāvamadhunā parkaḥ kṛtaścedyadi /
children.translated_text: Cold, hot, pungent, bitter, sour, sweet, salty — if now, equanimity toward these various tastes is achieved, that offering of flavors (<s>parka</s>) has been made;

children.text: mukhyoyaṃ madhuparka uttamarasastenāmunā sādaraṃ pūjyānāmapi pūjya eṣa paramo devaḥ sadā pūjyatām // NBs_16,17.3 //
children.translated_text: this is the primary honey-mixture (<s>madhuparka</s>), the supreme essence — with this, let the supreme God, who is worthy of worship even by the worshipful, be worshipped always with devotion. [NBs 16.17.3]

children.text: sarvāṅgīṇasukhāvahaṃ muhuraho yajjanmano majjanaṃ śuddhe bodhasudhāmbudhau śucitare snānaṃ viśuddhipradam /
children.translated_text: Oh, the immersion of the mind, which brings bliss to every limb, again and again in the pure ocean of the nectar of knowledge, the most purifying — that bathing bestows complete purity;

children.text: ābhānaṃ sphurati dvitīyamiva yattatsarvamācamyatām ityukto gurubhistadeṣa vidhṛtaścitte sa evācamaḥ // NBs_16,17.4 //
children.translated_text: the 'shining forth' that appears as if a second [self] — let all of that be sipped as <s>ācamana</s> (ritual sipping). Thus instructed by the <s>gurus</s>, that [practice], held in the mind, is itself the <s>ācamana</s>. [NBs 16.17.4]

children.text: śraddhā nirmamatā virāgaśucitā niḥsaṅgatā pūrṇatā bhaktipremarasaprasādaparamānandādayo ye guṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Faith, freedom from possessiveness, the purity of dispassion, non-attachment, fullness, devotion, the flavor of love, grace, supreme bliss, and other qualities —

children.text: vastrālaṅkaraṇāni tatra viduṣā deyāni viśvambhare so'haṃ bhāvamanohareṇa vidhinā yadyadyathā rocate // NBs_16,17.5 //
children.translated_text: these should be given to the Sustainer of the universe by the wise as garments and ornaments; with the 'I am He' attitude, by an enchanting method, whatever and however one is inclined. [NBs 16.17.5]

children.text: advaitapratipattirātmaviṣayā sā sāmarasyāñcitā gātrālepanacārucandanamidaṃ devasya deyaṃ priyam /
children.translated_text: The realization of non-duality pertaining to the Self, adorned with the harmony of equal vision — this is the beautiful sandal-paste to be offered to the beloved God as body-anointing;

children.text: śāntiḥ kṣāntiralolatā saralatā nirmatsaratvādayaḥ śāstrārthā yadi na kṣatāśca vituṣāḥ śuddhāsta evākṣatāḥ // NBs_16,17.6 //
children.translated_text: peace, forbearance, steadiness, simplicity, freedom from jealousy and the like — these meanings of the scriptures, if unimpaired and unhusked, are themselves the pure unbroken rice (<s>akṣata</s>). [NBs 16.17.6]

children.text: saṃphullairnijabhāvaśuddhakusumaiḥ sadvāsanāsundaraiḥ saṃpūjyo hi maheśvaraḥ sumanasāṃ sā dhanyatā varṇitā /
children.translated_text: With fully blossomed flowers of one's own pure inner nature, beautiful with wholesome impressions, the great Lord is to be worshipped; the blessedness of flowers (<s>sumanas</s>, also 'good-minded ones') has been thus described;

children.text: karmajñānamayo yadindriyagaṇaḥ kṣipto virāgānale devasyāsya daśāṅgadāhasurabhirdhūpaḥ sadā vallabhaḥ // NBs_16,17.7 //
children.translated_text: when the group of sense-organs, consisting of action and knowledge, is cast into the fire of dispassion — that is the eternally beloved ten-ingredient (<s>daśāṅga</s>) fragrant incense (<s>dhūpa</s>) of this God. [NBs 16.17.7]

children.text: yasminnujjvalite na tiṣṭhati tamo bāhyaṃ na cābhyantaraṃ so'yaṃ jñānamayaḥ prakāśaparamo dīpaḥ samujjvālyatām /
children.translated_text: When this [lamp] is lit, neither outer nor inner darkness remains — let this supreme illuminating lamp of knowledge be kindled;

children.text: yadbhakṣyaṃ priyamasya yasya paramā tṛptirbhavedbhakṣaṇe dvaitaṃ tattu nivedanīyamamitaṃ naivedyamatyuttamam // NBs_16,17.8 //
children.translated_text: that which is the beloved food of him whose supreme satisfaction comes from its consumption — duality itself should be offered as the immeasurable, most excellent food-offering (<s>naivedya</s>). [NBs 16.17.8]

children.text: paścādācamanīyamatra vihitaṃ sadyo viśuddhipradaṃ santoṣāmṛtameva pūjanavidhau pānīyamānīyatām /
children.translated_text: Afterwards, the ritual sipping (<s>ācamanīya</s>) prescribed here, immediately bestowing purity — let the nectar of contentment itself be brought as the drinking-water in this worship;

children.text: yanmaitryādicatuṣṭayaṃ munimate pātañjale varṇitaṃ tāmbūlaṃ vadanaprasādajanakaṃ devāgrataḥ sthāpyatām // NBs_16,17.9 //
children.translated_text: that fourfold [practice] of friendliness and the rest, described in the <s>Pātañjala</s> [system] according to the sage's view — let that be placed before the deity as the betel-offering (<s>tāmbūla</s>), which produces radiance in the face. [NBs 16.17.9]

children.text: niṣkāmottamadharmasaṃbhramajuṣāṃ janmāvalīnāṃ phalaṃ bhaktiḥ sā parameśvarasya padayorāvedanīyā mayā /
children.translated_text: Devotion, which is the fruit of generations of lifetimes devoted to selfless, supreme <s>dharma</s> — that devotion to the feet of the Supreme Lord is to be declared by me;

children.text: sarvasvaṃ mama tatkileti sa mayā klṛptasya pūjāvidheḥ pūrṇatvāya nivedito nijamanaścintāmaṇirdakṣiṇā // NBs_16,17.10 //
children.translated_text: 'all that is mine is indeed His' — thus, for the completion of this worship I have devised, my own mind, the wish-fulfilling gem (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>), is offered as the teacher's fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>). [NBs 16.17.10]

children.text: yāvantyeva bhuvāṃ rajāṃsyagaṇitabrahmāṇḍakoṭispṛśāṃ tāvadbhī rajasāṃ gaṇairgaṇayituṃ śakyā guṇā yasya na /
children.translated_text: As many as are the dust-particles of the worlds touching countless millions of cosmic eggs — by that many groups of particles, his qualities cannot be counted;

children.text: tvaṃ tādṛgguṇavāṃstathāpi munibhiryannirguṇaḥ stūyase tatkiṃ staumi maheśa he śiva bhavadrūpaṃ vidūraṃ dhiyām // NBs_16,17.11 //
children.translated_text: You are possessed of such qualities, yet You are praised by the sages as attributeless — how then should I praise You, O Great Lord, O <s>Śiva</s>? Your form is far beyond the reach of the mind. [NBs 16.17.11]

children.text: śvetaṃ śyāmamiti prakāśayati cedarkaḥ sa kiṃ śyāmatāṃ śvetatvaṃ ca dadhāti tadvaditaro mugdheṣu buddheṣu yaḥ /
children.translated_text: If the sun reveals both 'white' and 'dark,' does the sun itself bear darkness and whiteness? So too is the other [God], to the deluded and the wise;

children.text: dvaitādvaitavikalpajālakalanātītāya śuddhātmane jāgratsvānubhavaprakāśamahase devāya tasmai namaḥ // NBs_16,17.12 //
children.translated_text: to that pure Self, transcending the net of duality-and-non-duality conceptions, to that God whose radiance is the light of self-experience in the waking state — salutation! [NBs 16.17.12]

children.text: saṃprāpyāpi padāravindapadavīmadvaitavidyāvatām etāvantamanehasaṃ na tu vayaṃ līnāḥ sadā brahmaṇi /
children.translated_text: Even having attained the path of the lotus-feet of those possessing the knowledge of non-duality, for so long we have not been absorbed in <s>Brahman</s> at all times, constantly;

children.text: muktānāmapi mohataḥ samarasatvadbhāvapūrṇātmanām asmākaṃ hyaparādha eva paramaḥ kṣantavya evaṃ prabho // NBs_16,17.13 //
children.translated_text: even among the liberated, whose beings are full of the equal-essence state of Your nature, out of delusion — this is our supreme fault, O Lord; may it be forgiven. [NBs 16.17.13]

children.text: ātmaivāyamanantacidghanaraso nityaṃ vimuktaḥ svayaṃ ko bandhaḥ kimu bandhanaṃ kathamasau baddho vimuktaḥ katham /
children.translated_text: This Self itself is the infinite, dense essence of consciousness, eternally liberated by nature — what is bondage? What is the bond? How was it bound? How was it liberated?

children.text: sānandāśru sagadgadaṃ sapulakaṃ cidbodhapūjāvidhau devasyāstu madīyavismayamayaḥ saṃpūrṇapuṣpāñjaliḥ // NBs_16,17.14 //
children.translated_text: With tears of bliss, with faltering voice, with goosebumps — in this worship of consciousness-knowledge, may my offering of a full handful of flowers, consisting of wonder, be for the deity! [NBs 16.17.14]
Now the determination of the scriptural meaning useful for worship of the deity:

children.text: tyaktvā mohamayīṃ pūjāṃ pūjāṃ bodhamayīṃ kuru /
children.translated_text: Abandoning worship consisting of delusion, perform worship consisting of knowledge;

children.text: candanairarcanīyo'yaṃ na tu paṅkena śaṃkaraḥ // NBs_16,18.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śaṅkara</s> is to be worshipped with sandal-paste, not with mud. [NBs 16.18.1]
First know the deity, then become devoted to the worship of the deity;

children.text: deve paricayo nāsti vada pūjā kathaṃ bhavet // NBs_16,18.2 //
children.translated_text: if there is no acquaintance with the deity, tell me — how can worship occur? [NBs 16.18.2]

children.text: tāvatpūjāṃ na manute yāvatparicayo na hi /
children.translated_text: One does not value worship so long as there is no acquaintance;

children.text: jāte paricaye devaḥ pūjāmapi na kāṅkṣati // NBs_16,18.3 //
children.translated_text: once acquaintance arises, the deity does not even desire worship. [NBs 16.18.3]
In both cases I see the worship of the deity as difficult to accomplish;
the distinction of worshipped and worshipper is not known — the fool is infected with the impurity of ignorance. [NBs 16.18.4]
I do not know where the incense, lamp, unbroken rice, and the rest vanish;
in our worship of the deity, the deity alone remains. [NBs 16.18.5]
When, through the meditation contemplating the deity, the order of worship is forgotten,

children.text: pūjāyāṃ jāyate vighnaḥ pūrṇapūjāphalaṃ hi tat // NBs_16,18.6 //
children.translated_text: an obstacle arises in worship — that indeed is the fruit of complete worship. [NBs 16.18.6]
In the act of commencing the worship of <s>Govinda</s>, the dense [essence] of bliss,

children.text: bodhe sphurati mohātmā yajamānaḥ palāyitaḥ // NBs_16,18.7 //
children.translated_text: when knowledge shines forth, the self-deluded sacrificer has fled. [NBs 16.18.7]
Now the five great sacrifices (<s>pañca mahāyajñas</s>):
Steadfastness in knowledge, forgiveness, truth, discrimination, fullness —

children.text: ete pañca mahāyajñāḥ saṃmatā brahmavedinām // NBs_16,19.1 //
children.translated_text: These five great sacrifices (<s>mahāyajñas</s>) are accepted by the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>. [NBs 16.19.1]
Now, the determination of supplementary sacrifices.
In this daily routine, at each sacred occasion that arises,

children.text: madhye madhye copayajñāḥ kartavyā dīkṣitena hi // NBs_16,20.1 //
children.translated_text: supplementary sacrifices should be performed by the initiated. [NBs 16.20.1]
When a portion of time becomes a sacrificial cake, and the mind becomes the sacrificial animal,
such sacrifices should be performed for the sake of pleasing <s>Indra</s> (the lord of the senses). [NBs 16.20.2]
If the <s>Suparṇa</s> altar (<s>Suparṇacit</s>) is built by uniting the two birds [individual self and supreme self],
the fruit of a hundred fire-altars is attained by that chief among sages. [NBs 16.20.3]
Now, daily giving (<s>nityadāna</s>).
At the sacred ford of <s>samādhi</s>, by the sage, during the eclipse of the moon and sun,
gold equal to the self is given to a worthy recipient — [that is,] to the Supreme Self. [NBs 16.21.1]
Now, the midday <s>sandhyā</s> (junction-worship).
In seeing, touching, smelling, tasting, hearing, and the rest,
the wonder of consciousness that arises for the sage — that is his midday [worship]. [NBs 16.22.1]
Now, the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (offering to the All-Gods).
The self is the deity of the universe; it is worshipped by the universe as the oblation.
That ritual is called <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, for the removal of all slaughter-sites [i.e., sins of killing]. [NBs 16.23.1]
Now, the offering of <s>bali</s> (food-offering to beings).
By the compassionate one, to the beings that inhabit this city of nine gates [the body],
a <s>bali</s> offering should be given, characterized by eating, drinking, and the like. [NBs 16.24.1]
Now, the rules of eating.
Together with the guru, fellow-students, and disciples,
the excellent nectar of knowledge, flavorful and delightful, should be consumed. [NBs 16.25.1]
Now, the determination regarding the taking of betel.

children.text: satyaṃ priyaṃ ca pathyaṃ ca brahmacarcā''tmakaṃ vacaḥ /
children.translated_text: Speech that is true, pleasant, and salutary, consisting of discourse on <s>Brahman</s> —

children.text: tāmbūlagrahaṇaṃ kāryaṃ vadanaṃ yena rājate // NBs_16,26.1 //
children.translated_text: the taking of betel should be done, by which the mouth shines. [NBs 16.26.1]
Now, the determination regarding reclining on the left side.
Until the fall of the body, the acquisition and preservation [of worldly goods], brought about by prior <s>karmas</s>,

children.text: yogakṣemau na cintyau hi niryogakṣema ātmavān // NBs_16,27.1 //
children.translated_text: should not be worried about; the self-possessed one is beyond acquisition and preservation. [NBs 16.27.1]
On the pure bed of <s>samādhi</s>, having taken a pleasant sleep,
after resting for a moment, one should then engage in hearing the <s>Purāṇas</s>. [NBs 16.27.2]
Now, the determination regarding hearing the <s>Purāṇas</s>.
Now, the determination regarding hearing the <s>Bhārata</s>.
That in which the <s>Gītā</s> of eighteen chapters is expounded,
[which contains] the essence of all <s>Upaniṣads</s> — hear that <s>Mahābhārata</s>. [NBs 16.28.1.1]
In the <s>Bhārata</s>, the sage <s>Vyāsa</s> elaborated the stories.
Thereby he revealed that this universe is nothing but a story. [NBs 16.28.1.2]
At the conclusion of the <s>Bhārata</s>, the <s>Śāntiparva</s> (Book of Peace) is expounded.
This indicates that all śāstras conclude in peace (<s>śānti</s>). [NBs 16.28.1.3]
Through various narratives, the greatly delightful <s>mokṣadharmas</s> (doctrines of liberation) are expounded.

children.text: taduktaṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ mokṣadharmā parā matāḥ // NBs_16,28.1.4 //
children.translated_text: This indicates that among all doctrines, the doctrines of liberation are considered supreme. [NBs 16.28.1.4]
Now, the determination regarding hearing the <s>Bhāgavata</s>.
He who sports with the <s>gopī</s>-like mental modifications yet does not abandon celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>),
in which the inner self (<s>antarātman</s>) is the cowherd (<s>Gopāla</s>) — that is the excellent <s>Bhāgavata</s>. [NBs 16.28.2.1]
<s>Pūtanā</s>, the fearsome [demoness] who is the corrupt desire that devours children [i.e., immature seekers],

children.text: kṛṣṇena rudhiraṃ pītvā prāpitā sāpi tatpadam // NBs_16,28.2.2 //
children.translated_text: even she, having had her blood drunk by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, was led to that supreme state. [NBs 16.28.2.2]
For the protection of the helpless — his own people — to grant them immortality, by <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
even the serpent of time (<s>Kālasarpa</s>) was struck; the entire world was made joyful. [NBs 16.28.2.3]
Those cows are like brāhmaṇas, dwelling on the banks, living on wild [food];
swallowed by the python of delusion, they were rescued by <s>Govinda</s>. [NBs 16.28.2.4]
He, the embodied ego (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>), named <s>Kaṃsa</s>, of great strength,
leaping up himself, was seized and cast down by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. [NBs 16.28.2.5]
Now, the determination regarding hearing the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>.
By the reflected particles [of consciousness], the inert body and the rest become conscious —
just as <s>Ahalyā</s>, though a stone, [was revived] by the dust of <s>Rāma</s>'s feet. [NBs 16.28.3.1]
A monkey, by whose grace, crossed the salt ocean —

children.text: naraḥ kiṃ tatprasādena na taredbhavasāgaram // NBs_16,28.3.2 //
children.translated_text: would not a man, by that grace, cross the ocean of existence? [NBs 16.28.3.2]
<s>Rāma</s>, crossing the ocean by a bridge of stones, proclaimed:
The crossing of the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> is by <s>nirvikalpa samādhi</s> (thought-free absorption). [NBs 16.28.3.3]
<s>Sītā</s>, who is peace (<s>śānti</s>), was brought back; <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who is delusion (<s>moha</s>), was slain;
by <s>Rāma</s>, who delights in the self (<s>ātmārāma</s>) — that is the excellent <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>. [NBs 16.28.3.4]
In whom the yogins delight, who delights in the hearts of yogins,

children.text: tārakaṃ brahma rāmākhyaṃ ramatāṃ hṛdaye mama // NBs_16,28.3.5 //
children.translated_text: that saving <s>Brahman</s> named <s>Rāma</s> — may it delight in my heart. [NBs 16.28.3.5]
Thus it is stated in the <s>Yājñavalkyasmṛti</s>:
<s>Purāṇas</s>, <s>Nyāya</s>, <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>, <s>Dharmaśāstra</s>, the auxiliary sciences — mixed with

children.text: vedāḥ sthānāni vidyānāṃ dharmasya ca caturdaśa // NBs_16,28.4.1 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Vedas</s> — these are the fourteen seats of knowledge and of <s>dharma</s>. [NBs 16.28.4.1]

body.translated_text: The determination of the eighteen seats of knowledge.
<s>Āyurveda</s>, <s>Dhanurveda</s>, <s>Gāndharva</s> [veda], and the science of statecraft (<s>Arthaśāstra</s>). [NBs 16.28.4.2]
Thus there are eighteen seats of knowledge.

children.translated_text: Now, the determination regarding the <s>Purāṇas</s>.
If intense love has not arisen for the primordial Person (<s>Purāṇapuruṣa</s>),
then what is the use of hearing the <s>Purāṇas</s> in their eighteen divisions? [NBs 16.28.4.1.1]

children.text: purāṇo'pi na jīrṇo yaḥ sa purāṇastu na śrutaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who, though ancient (<s>purāṇa</s>), is not aged — that <s>Purāṇa</s> [Being] has not been heard [by you].

children.text: kāyaḥ purāṇatāṃ prāptaḥ purāṇaśravaṇena kim // NBs_16,28.4,1.2 //
children.translated_text: The body has become old — what is the use of hearing the <s>Purāṇas</s>? [NBs 16.28.4.1.2]
The determination regarding the science of logic (<s>Nyāyaśāstra</s>).
When there is unwavering rest in the pure essence of the self —

children.text: sa eva nyāya ityuktaḥ śeṣaṃ tvanyāyalakṣaṇam // NBs_16,28.4,2.1 //
children.translated_text: that alone is called <s>nyāya</s> (justice/logic); the rest has the character of <s>anyāya</s> (injustice). [NBs 16.28.4.2.1]
The non-thinking of [external] objects — the knowers of logic know that as true logic.
How can one who relishes the path of non-logic be a knower of the science of logic? [NBs 16.28.4.2.2]
What the logician himself states — "reasoning leads to undesirable consequences" —
then how can the logician's own reasoning lead to what is desirable? [NBs 16.28.4.2.3]

children.text: na tarkitaṃ paraṃ brahma medhayā tīkṣṇatarkayā /
children.translated_text: The supreme <s>Brahman</s> is not attained by reasoning, [not] by the intellect, [nor] by sharp argumentation.
Then the harshness of reasoning of this sophist is in vain. [NBs 16.28.4.2.4]
Even if all sixteen categories have been reasoned through by you, O logician —

children.text: tarko nāvasthitastarhi tarkātīte manaḥ kuru // NBs_16,28.4,2.5 //
children.translated_text: reasoning itself is not stable; therefore, fix the mind on what is beyond reasoning. [NBs 16.28.4.2.5]
The determination regarding <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> and the rest.
Now, in connection with reasoning, the determination is made

children.text: vaiśeṣikasya sāṃkhyasya tathā pātañjalasya ca // NBs_16,28.4,3.1 //
children.translated_text: regarding <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>, <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, and also <s>Pātañjala</s> [yoga]. [NBs 16.28.4.3.1]
First, the determination regarding <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>.

children.text: saviśeṣāḥ padārthā ye tatra vaiśeṣikaḥ kṛtī /
children.translated_text: The <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> is skilled in the categories that have distinctions (<s>viśeṣa</s>).

children.text: nirviśeṣaṃ paraṃ brahma tatra vaiśeṣikasya kim // NBs_16,28.4,3.1,1 //
children.translated_text: The supreme <s>Brahman</s> is without distinctions — what then has <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> to do with that? [NBs 16.28.4.3.1.1]
Liberation is said to be free from similarity and dissimilarity; the knowledge of truth is for liberation.
Knowledge of truth based on similarity and dissimilarity is not for liberation. [NBs 16.28.4.3.1.2]
Scripture says that liberation is through the forgetting of all categories.

children.text: tarhi sarvapadārthānāṃ cintanaiḥ kiṃ prayojanam // NBs_16,28.4,3.1,3 //
children.translated_text: Then what is the purpose of thinking about all categories? [NBs 16.28.4.3.1.3]
How can similarity and dissimilarity be the cause of the knowledge of truth,
when there is no similarity and dissimilarity in the non-dual Supreme Self? [NBs 16.28.4.3.1.4]
If you say, "Through the discrimination of categories, the Supreme Self is revealed" —

children.text: iti cedvadasi prājña tarhīdaṃ mama saṃmatam // NBs_16,28.4,3.1,5 //
children.translated_text: O wise one, if so, then this is my view too. [NBs 16.28.4.3.1.5]
In the framework of bondage and liberation, the many selves are not real.
"The multiplicity of selves is in the framework" — thus says the sage <s>Gautama</s>. [NBs 16.28.4.3.1.6]
"Complexity of assumptions is a fault; simplicity of assumptions is a merit" —

children.text: iti yattārkikairuktaṃ tadeva mama rocate // NBs_16,28.4,3.1,7 //
children.translated_text: what the logicians have stated, that indeed pleases me. [NBs 16.28.4.3.1.7]
Now, the determination regarding <s>Sāṃkhya</s>.
O <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, the counts of categories are innumerable; you who have counted them —

children.text: kiṃ sāṃkhyasaṃkhyayā brahma saṃkhyātītaṃ vicintaya // NBs_16,28.4,4.1 //
children.translated_text: what is the use of the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> count? Contemplate <s>Brahman</s>, which is beyond all counting. [NBs 16.28.4.4.1]

children.text: tattvajñānaṃ tvayā proktaṃ tattvajñānaṃ mataṃ mama /
children.translated_text: You have taught "knowledge of truth" — knowledge of truth is my view too.

children.text: tattvātītasya vijñānaṃ tattvajñānaṃ hi muktaye // NBs_16,28.4,4.2 //
children.translated_text: But the knowledge of what is beyond the categories — that is the knowledge of truth for liberation. [NBs 16.28.4.4.2]
"The enumeration was set forth by me for the examination of <s>Puruṣa</s>" —

children.text: sāṃkhya evaṃ yadi prāha tarhīdaṃ mama saṃmatam // NBs_16,28.4,4.3 //
children.translated_text: if the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> says thus, then this is my view. [NBs 16.28.4.4.3]

children.text: puruṣān na paraṃ kiñcitsā kāṣṭhā sā parā gatiḥ /
children.translated_text: "There is nothing higher than <s>Puruṣa</s>; that is the final end, that is the supreme goal."

children.text: puruṣaṃ paśya re sāṃkhya saṃkhyayā kiṃ prayojanam // NBs_16,28.4,4.4 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, see <s>Puruṣa</s> — what is the use of enumeration? [NBs 16.28.4.4.4]
Now, the determination regarding <s>Pātañjala</s> [yoga].
This labor of the <s>Pātañjala</s> practitioner, attached to <s>yoga</s>-powers (<s>siddhis</s>),
is merely artistic skill, not abiding in one's own true nature. [NBs 16.28.4.5.1]

children.text: re yogasiddha jīvānāṃ kāyavyūho na durlabhaḥ /
children.translated_text: O <s>yoga</s>-adept, the projection of multiple bodies is not difficult for living beings;

children.text: videhamuktatā siddhiḥ kāyavyūho na siddhaye // NBs_16,28.4,5.2 //
children.translated_text: liberation while disembodied (<s>videhamukti</s>) is the true attainment — body-projection is not for liberation. [NBs 16.28.4.5.2]
O <s>yoga</s>-adept, you know the entry into another's body;

children.text: paraṃ tu naiva jānāsi parakāyapraveśanam // NBs_16,28.4,5.3 //
children.translated_text: but you do not know the supreme entry into another's body [i.e., entering <s>Brahman</s>]. [NBs 16.28.4.5.3]
Even ghosts and the like know the entry into another's body.

children.text: sā siddhirnaiva bandhaḥ sā yaddhi kāyapraveśanam // NBs_16,28.4,5.4 //
children.translated_text: That is not a true <s>siddhi</s>; that is indeed bondage — for it is merely body-entry. [NBs 16.28.4.5.4]
Death is certain; then what kind of long life is that?
Drink the nectar of knowledge that destroys birth, death, and old age. [NBs 16.28.4.5.5]

children.text: paracittasthitaṃ vastu tvayā jñātaṃ tataśca kim /
children.translated_text: You have known the object situated in another's mind — so what?

children.text: svacittasaṃsthitaṃ vastu paraṃ brahma vilokaya // NBs_16,28.4,5.6 //
children.translated_text: Behold the supreme <s>Brahman</s> situated in your own mind. [NBs 16.28.4.5.6]
If there is no hearing and seeing of the self that is near at hand,

children.text: kā siddhiḥ sā tu yā siddhirdūraśravaṇadarśanam // NBs_16,28.4,5.7 //
children.translated_text: what kind of <s>siddhi</s> is that — the <s>siddhi</s> of hearing and seeing at a distance? [NBs 16.28.4.5.7]
Even crows and the like possess flying through the sky and such [abilities].

children.text: siddhibhirnaiva sidhyeta siddhibhiḥ kiṃ prayojanam // NBs_16,28.4,5.8 //
children.translated_text: One does not attain perfection through <s>siddhis</s>; what is the use of <s>siddhis</s>? [NBs 16.28.4.5.8]
True <s>siddhi</s> is not the <s>yoga</s>-attainment that produces strength, vigor, and the like.

children.text: etena yogaḥ pratyukta iti vedāntabhāṣitam // NBs_16,28.4,5.9 //
children.translated_text: "By this, <s>yoga</s> is refuted" — thus speaks <s>Vedānta</s>. [NBs 16.28.4.5.9]
"The true <s>siddhi</s> is the knowledge of the self; the [other] <s>siddhis</s> are obstacles" —
if the knower of <s>yoga</s> says thus, then that is indeed our view. [NBs 16.28.4.5.10]
Now, the determination regarding <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>.

children.text: kaṣṭaṃ karmetyayaṃ nyāyo mato mīmāṃsakasya cet /
children.translated_text: If the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> holds the view that "action is toilsome" —
then by that very [admission], the self's share of affliction has been accepted. [NBs 16.28.4.6.1]
The <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s>, the knower of action, truly says "action is toilsome."
Then he too should inquire into <s>Brahman</s>, for the removal of the undesirable. [NBs 16.28.4.6.2]
Birth arises from <s>karma</s>, and <s>karma</s> arises from birth.

children.text: tarhi karmajaḍasyāsya janmamuktiḥ kathaṃ bhavet // NBs_16,28.4,6.3 //
children.translated_text: Then how can liberation from birth occur for this one mired in the dullness of <s>karma</s>? [NBs 16.28.4.6.3]
For those who maintain the primacy of knowledge, liberation is primary.
For those who maintain the primacy of action, birth [i.e., continued rebirth] is primary. [NBs 16.28.4.6.4]
He who, through the dullness of <s>karma</s>, [having] no qualification for [selfless] sacrifices,

children.text: niṣkāmamaśuciprāyaṃ jagāda sa kathaṃ śuciḥ // NBs_16,28.4,6.5 //
children.translated_text: declared [sacrifices] that are predominantly impure and desire-ridden — how can he be pure? [NBs 16.28.4.6.5]
If <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> would teach purifying <s>karma</s> freed from desire,
then the <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> that deals with desire-motivated <s>karma</s> is merely a form of toil. [NBs 16.28.4.6.6]
Through <s>karmas</s>, purification of the mind; through purification, knowledge is attained —

children.text: iti cetkarmaṭhaḥ prāha tarhīdaṃ mama saṃmatam // NBs_16,28.4,6.7 //
children.translated_text: if the ritualist says thus, then this is my view. [NBs 16.28.4.6.7]
Now, the determination regarding <s>Dharmaśāstra</s>.
Through the study of <s>Dharmaśāstra</s>, the <s>dharma</s> of liberation (<s>mokṣadharma</s>) is the great fruit.
Here there is no loss of what has been begun, and no adverse consequence arises. [NBs 16.28.4.7.1]
And thus <s>Yājñavalkya</s> [says]:
Of sacrifice, good conduct, self-restraint, non-violence, charity, and the duties of study —
this alone is the supreme <s>dharma</s>: the vision of the self through <s>yoga</s>. [NBs 16.28.4.7.2]
Now, the determination regarding <s>Śrauta</s> and <s>Smārta</s> [rites].
Hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>) is said to be <s>śrauta</s> (scriptural); remembrance (<s>smaraṇa</s>) is called <s>smārta</s> (tradition-based);
hearing and reflection — this is the determination of <s>śrauta</s> and <s>smārta</s>. [NBs 16.28.4.8.1]
What has been heard from the mouths of the revered <s>Guru</s>s, remembered and not forgotten —

children.text: śrautasmārtamidaṃ yeṣāṃ śrautasmārttavido hi te // NBs_16,28.4,8.2 //
children.translated_text: those for whom this is the <s>śrauta</s> and <s>smārta</s> — they are indeed the knowers of <s>śrauta</s> and <s>smārta</s>. [NBs 16.28.4.8.2]
Now the auxiliary sciences (<s>aṅga</s>s).

children.text: śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ chanda eva ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Śikṣā</s> (phonetics), <s>Kalpa</s> (ritual procedure), <s>Vyākaraṇa</s> (grammar), <s>Nirukta</s> (etymology), <s>Chandas</s> (meter),

children.text: jyotiṣaṃ ca ṣaḍaṅgāni teṣāmeva vinirṇayaḥ // NBs_16,28.4,9.1 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Jyotiṣa</s> (astronomy) — these six auxiliary sciences; [now follows] their determination. [NBs 16.28.4.9.1]
Now the determination of <s>Śikṣā</s> (phonetics):
That instruction (<s>śikṣā</s>) by which one is trained in the state of being free from the body, [attaining] purity —

children.text: sā śikṣā yadi na prāptā śikṣayā śikṣitaṃ kimu // NBs_16,28.4,9.2 //
children.translated_text: if that instruction is not obtained, then what has been taught by [mere phonetic] instruction? [NBs 16.28.4.9.2]
Now the determination of <s>Kalpa Sūtra</s> (ritual manual):

children.text: kalpānāṃ prathamaḥ kalpo nirvikalpamidaṃ na cet /
children.translated_text: The first <s>kalpa</s> (procedure) of all procedures is this <s>nirvikalpa</s> (thought-free state); if not,
what is achieved by <s>kalpa sūtra</s>s filled with thought-constructions and intentions? [NBs 16.28.4.10.1]
That <s>kalpa</s> (procedure) by which the performer becomes fit for <s>Brahman</s> —

children.text: sa kalpo naiva kḷptaścetkalpasūtraṃ nirarthakam // NBs_16,28.4,10.2 //
children.translated_text: if that <s>kalpa</s> has not been fashioned, then the <s>Kalpa Sūtra</s> is purposeless. [NBs 16.28.4.10.2]
Now the determination of <s>Vyākaraṇa</s> (grammar):
The derivation of words is to be sought for understanding the meaning of the <s>Mahāvākya</s>s (great sentences);

children.text: sa eva yadi na jñātastarhi vyākaraṇena kim // NBs_16,28.4,11.1 //
children.translated_text: if that [meaning] itself is not known, then of what use is grammar? [NBs 16.28.4.11.1]

children.text: yenedaṃ vyākṛtaṃ viśvaṃ tadeva vyākṛtaṃ na cet /
children.translated_text: That by which this universe has been 'analyzed' (<s>vyākṛta</s>) — if that itself is not analyzed,

children.text: bṛhanno vetti yattarhi taddhi vyākaraṇena kim // NBs_16,28.4,11.2 //
children.translated_text: and one does not know the great (<s>bṛhat</s>) — then of what use is grammar? [NBs 16.28.4.11.2]
If, even through perfectly formed words from the scriptures repeatedly,

children.text: heyādeyau na vijñātau tarhi vyākaraṇena kiṃ // NBs_16,28.4,11.3 //
children.translated_text: what is to be rejected and what is to be accepted are not known — then of what use is grammar? [NBs 16.28.4.11.3]
Now the determination of <s>Nirukta</s> (etymology):
True <s>nirukta</s> (etymology) is the abiding of consciousness; true <s>nirukta</s> is the awakening of consciousness —

children.text: tanniruktaṃ na cedveda niruktasya kimuktibhiḥ // NBs_16,28.4,12.1 //
children.translated_text: if one does not know that <s>nirukta</s>, of what use are the utterances of [conventional] etymology? [NBs 16.28.4.12.1]
Now the determination of <s>Chandas</s> (meter):

children.text: tacchando yadi na jñātaṃ svacchando yena khelati /
children.translated_text: If that <s>chandas</s> (measure/meter) is not known, by which [the self] plays freely (<s>svacchandaḥ</s>),
then what is the purpose of meters with their <s>ya</s>, <s>ra</s>, <s>sa</s>, <s>ta</s>, <s>ja</s>, <s>bha</s>, <s>na</s>, <s>ma</s> [syllabic formulas]? [NBs 16.28.4.13.1]
Now the determination of <s>Jyotiṣa</s> (astronomy):

children.text: jyotiṣā yena sūryādi jyotirbhāti na vetti tat /
children.translated_text: If one does not know that <s>jyotis</s> (light) by which the sun and other luminaries shine,

children.text: yadi yena tadā tena jyotirgranthena kiṃ kṛtam // NBs_16,28.4,14.1 //
children.translated_text: then what is accomplished by a treatise on astronomy? [NBs 16.28.4.14.1]
Now the <s>Veda</s>s.
First, the determination of the <s>Ṛg Veda</s>:

children.text: yaḥ parānandadaḥ svātmā taṃ tvā vayaṃ yajāmahe /
children.translated_text: The Self that grants supreme bliss — 'We worship you' —

children.text: ityāhuto na viśvātmā ṛcā hautreṇa kiṃ tadā // NBs_16,28.4,15.1 //
children.translated_text: if the Self of all is not thus invoked, then of what use is the <s>Ṛc</s> and the office of the <s>Hotṛ</s>? [NBs 16.28.4.15.1]
Now the determination of the <s>Yajur Veda</s>:
If the unborn (<s>ajā</s>) — red, white, and black — the cause of creation,
is not attained in the sacrifice of <s>Brahman</s>, then of what use is the <s>Yajus</s> and the office of the <s>Adhvaryu</s>? [NBs 16.28.4.16.1]
Now the determination of the <s>Sāma Veda</s>:
If <s>Brahman</s> is not sung through the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> with a voice

children.text: sāmnā gītaṃ na cedbrahma sāmodgātreṇa kiṃ tadā // NBs_16,28.4,17.1 //
children.translated_text: choked with love, through the <s>Sāman</s>, then of what use is the <s>Sāma</s> and the office of the <s>Udgātṛ</s>? [NBs 16.28.4.17.1]
Now the determination of the <s>Atharva Veda</s>:
The <s>Atharvanic</s> knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, flowing from the mouth of <s>Pippalāda</s> —

children.text: camatkṛtā na hṛdaye kiṃ phalaṃ tarhyatharvabhiḥ // NBs_16,28.4,18.1 //
children.translated_text: if it has not produced wonder in the heart, then what is the fruit of the <s>Atharva</s> [hymns]? [NBs 16.28.4.18.1]
Now the determination of <s>Āyurveda</s> (medicine):
If the nectar of knowledge has not been drunk and immortality not achieved,

children.text: mṛtyureva punaḥ prāpta āyurvedo nirarthakaḥ // NBs_16,28.4,19.1 //
children.translated_text: and death is once again encountered — then <s>Āyurveda</s> is purposeless. [NBs 16.28.4.19.1]
Now the determination of <s>Dhanurveda</s> (archery):
If <s>Brahman</s>, the target, has not been pierced by the bow of <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ)

children.text: lakṣyaṃ brahma na cedviddhaṃ dhanurvedo nirarthakaḥ // NBs_16,28.4,20.1 //
children.translated_text: and the arrow of awakening, then <s>Dhanurveda</s> is purposeless. [NBs 16.28.4.20.1]
Now the determination of <s>Gāndharva</s> (music):

children.text: ātmā kalena gītena gāndhāreṇa svareṇa hi /
children.translated_text: If the Self has not been sung in the <s>Gāndhāra</s> note, in due measure,

children.text: na cedgandharvavadgīto gāndharveṇa kṛtaṃ kimu // NBs_16,28.4,21.1 //
children.translated_text: like a <s>Gandharva</s>, then of what use is the <s>Gāndharva</s> [science of music]? [NBs 16.28.4.21.1]
Now the determination of <s>Arthaśāstra</s> (political science):
All [worldly] 'wealth' (<s>artha</s>) is worthless; the [true] possessor of wealth is one who sees the supreme truth;
if the supreme truth (<s>paramārtha</s>) is not obtained, then <s>Arthaśāstra</s> is purposeless. [NBs 16.28.4.22.1]
Now the determination of the evening <s>sandhyā</s> (junction-worship):
Thus, with the play of knowledge and curiosity about Vedic sciences,

children.text: divasaṃ sakalaṃ yātaṃ sāyaṃsandhyā samāgatā // NBs_16,29.1 //
children.translated_text: the entire day has passed; the evening <s>sandhyā</s> has arrived. [NBs 16.29.1]
After observing worldly affairs for some time,

children.text: punaḥ samādhau sandhānaṃ sāyaṃsandhyā hi sā smṛtā // NBs_16,29.2 //
children.translated_text: there is once again absorption in <s>samādhi</s> — that is known as the evening <s>sandhyā</s>. [NBs 16.29.2]
Now the determination of nighttime conduct:

children.text: yāte'tha vyavahāranāmni divase bhukte ca sandhyāsukhe jātāyāṃ niśi niścalena manasā datvā kapāṭārgalāḥ /
children.translated_text: When the day called worldly activity has passed and the bliss of the <s>sandhyā</s> has been enjoyed, when night has come, with a motionless mind, having bolted the doors,

children.text: pītvā saṃprati śuddhabodhamadhuraṃ kṣīraṃ yatheṣṭaṃ yuvā paryaṅke susamādhināmani muhuḥ kāñcidbhunakti priyām // NBs_16,30.1 //
children.translated_text: having drunk as much as desired the milk that is sweet with pure knowledge — the youth, on the bed named <s>samādhi</s>, repeatedly enjoys a certain beloved. [NBs 16.30.1]

children.text: tanvaṅgīṃ taruṇīṃ vilāsarasikāṃ citte camatkāriṇīṃ jāte premaṇi nityameva sukhadāmānandalīlāmayīm /
children.translated_text: She of delicate limbs, youthful, relishing in playfulness, producing wonder in the mind, always bestowing happiness when love has arisen, consisting of the play of bliss,

children.text: khelantīmurasi priyāṃ nijakalāmāliṅgya tatsaṅgamād bhogīndratvamupāgataḥ sukhanidhiryogīndracūḍāmaṇiḥ // NBs_16,30.2 //
children.translated_text: frolicking upon his chest — embracing his beloved, his own art; from that union, the crest-jewel of the lords of <s>yoga</s>, the treasure of happiness, has attained the state of the king of serpents [<s>Śeṣa</s>, the cosmic supporter]. [NBs 16.30.2]
Now the determination of the fruit of contemplating the daily routine of the chief sage.
This daily routine of the chief sage should be contemplated day after day;

children.text: na cirāccintanenāsyā naro niścintatāṃ vrajet // NBs_16,31.1 //
children.translated_text: before long, through this contemplation, a person attains the state of freedom from anxiety. [NBs 16.31.1]
When this is properly known, with the connections of what is to be accomplished, the means, the relation, the fruit, and the dispositions —
nothing remains to be known. [NBs 16.31.2]
This daily routine of the chief sage is difficult to express even by chief sages;

children.text: mama vācālatāṃ tatra kṣamyatāṃ pārvatīpatiḥ // NBs_16,31.3 //
children.translated_text: may the Lord of <s>Pārvatī</s> [<s>Śiva</s>] forgive my loquacity in this [regard]. [NBs 16.31.3]
The <s>Nirañjana</s> Fifty (Fifty Verses on the Stainless One).
Where the <s>Vedānta</s>s are the authority, as is the experience of the virtuous —

children.text: devo nirañjanaḥ so'yaṃ bodhasāre nirūpyate // NBs_17.1 //
children.translated_text: that God, the stainless (<s>Nirañjana</s>), is here set forth in the <s>Bodhasāra</s>. [NBs 17.1]
'I am ignorant; I do not know myself; who am I?' —

children.text: ajñānaprabhavo bhāva ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.2 //
children.translated_text: this notion arises from ignorance; the Self is pure, stainless (<s>nirañjana</s>). [NBs 17.2]
If this notion regarding the <s>jīva</s> is that <s>Brahman</s> is to be meditated upon —

children.text: sa hi bhrāntimayo bhāva ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.3 //
children.translated_text: that notion is indeed born of delusion; the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.3]
'I am bound by the three <s>guṇa</s>s; I transmigrate in <s>saṃsāra</s>' —

children.text: ityādyāḥ prākṛtā bhāvāḥ ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.4 //
children.translated_text: these and other notions belonging to <s>Prakṛti</s> — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.4]
Mind (<s>manas</s>), intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), ego (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>), and thought (<s>citta</s>) — this fourfold [inner organ];

children.text: antaḥkaraṇajā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.5 //
children.translated_text: these notions born of the inner instrument — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.5]

children.text: yacca saṅkalpyate pūrvaṃ saṅkalpya ca vikalpyate /
children.translated_text: What is first imagined and then, having been imagined, is differentiated —

children.text: ete manobhavā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.6 //
children.translated_text: these notions born of the mind — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.6]
'This is thus; this is not thus' — what is determined —

children.text: sa hi buddhimayo bhāva ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.7 //
children.translated_text: that is indeed a notion born of the intellect; the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.7]
Knowership, doership, enjoyership, being killed, being the killer, and the like —

children.text: ahaṅkārabhavā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.8 //
children.translated_text: these notions born of the ego — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.8]
Memory — [the recall] of what was previously experienced — and recognition of the same kind —

children.text: ete cittabhavā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.9 //
children.translated_text: these notions born of <s>citta</s> (thought) — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.9]
The <s>Viśva</s>, <s>Taijasa</s>, and <s>Prājña</s> [selves] in waking, dreaming, and deep sleep —

children.text: avasthābhedajā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.10 //
children.translated_text: these notions born of the distinction of states — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.10]
Sleep, laziness, negligence, bewilderment, and despondency —

children.text: ete tamobhavā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.11 //
children.translated_text: these notions born of <s>tamas</s> — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.11]
Tranquility, discrimination, gentleness, luminosity, and serenity —

children.text: ete sattvamayā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.12 //
children.translated_text: these notions consisting of <s>sattva</s> — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.12]
Greed, restlessness of the senses, the initiation of actions —

children.text: ete rajobhavā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.13 //
children.translated_text: these notions born of <s>rajas</s> — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.13]
Injunction and prohibition, <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, auspicious and inauspicious —

children.text: kartṛtvabhāvitā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.14 //
children.translated_text: these notions produced by the sense of doership — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.14]

children.text: kṛtiḥ kāryaṃ ca karaṇaṃ tatra ceṣṭāḥ pṛthagvidhāḥ /
children.translated_text: The act, the effect, and the instrument; and the various activities therein —

children.text: kartṛtvasyānugā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.15 //
children.translated_text: these notions that follow doership — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.15]

children.text: śabdaḥ sparśaśca rūpaṃ c raso gandhaśca pañcamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell as the fifth —

children.text: pañcabhūtodbhavā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.16 //
children.translated_text: these notions born of the five elements — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.16]
Space, wind, fire, water, and earth as the fifth —

children.text: pañcabhūtamayā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.17 //
children.translated_text: these notions consisting of the five elements — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.17]
Ear, skin, eye, tongue, and the organ of smell as the fifth —

children.text: jñānendriyamayā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.18 //
children.translated_text: these notions consisting of the organs of knowledge — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.18]
Speech, hands, feet, the organ of excretion, and the organ of generation as the fifth —

children.text: karmendriyamayā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.19 //
children.translated_text: these notions consisting of the organs of action — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.19]
The varieties of sound — struck (<s>āhata</s>), unstruck (<s>anāhata</s>), and others —

children.text: śabdabhedamayā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.20 //
children.translated_text: these notions consisting of the varieties of sound — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.20]
<s>Niṣāda</s>, <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Gāndhāra</s>, <s>Ṣaḍja</s>, <s>Madhyama</s>, <s>Dhaivata</s> —

children.text: svarabhedamayā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.21 //
children.translated_text: these notions consisting of the varieties of musical notes — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.21]
Cold, hot, soft, hard, sharp, rough, and other varieties —

children.text: sparśabhedamayā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.22 //
children.translated_text: these notions consisting of the varieties of touch — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.22]

children.text: raktaṃ pītaṃ sitaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ haritaṃ citramityapi /
children.translated_text: Red, yellow, white, black, green, and variegated —

children.text: rūpabhedamayā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.23 //
children.translated_text: these notions consisting of the varieties of form — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.23]
Pungent, astringent, sweet, salty, sour, and bitter —

children.text: rasabhedamayā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.24 //
children.translated_text: these notions consisting of the varieties of taste — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.24]
Various fragrances — <s>parimala</s>, <s>āmoda</s>, <s>saurabha</s>, <s>asaurabha</s>, and others —

children.text: gandhabhedamayā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.25 //
children.translated_text: these notions consisting of the varieties of smell — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.25]
Born from the womb, born from eggs, born from moisture, and born from sprouts —

children.text: prāṇibhedamayā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.26 //
children.translated_text: these notions consisting of the varieties of living beings — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.26]
Gods, demons, <s>Gandharva</s>s, <s>Yakṣa</s>s, <s>Rākṣasa</s>s, humans, and others —

children.text: jīvajātimayā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.27 //
children.translated_text: these notions consisting of the species of <s>jīva</s>s — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.27]
<s>Śaiva</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, <s>Sāvitra</s>, <s>Śākta</s>, <s>Gāṇapata</s>, and others —

children.text: iṣṭadaivatajā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.28 //
children.translated_text: these notions born of chosen deities — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.28]
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Gārgya</s>, <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>, <s>Bhārgava</s>, <s>Āṅgirasa</s>, and others —

children.text: gotrapravarajā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.29 //
children.translated_text: these notions born of <s>gotra</s> (clan) and <s>pravara</s> (lineage) — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.29]
Mythologists, Vedic scholars, astronomers, physicians, and others —

children.text: vidyāvṛttibhavā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.30 //
children.translated_text: these notions born of learning and vocation — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.30]
Eastern, northern, western, and others; southern and others —

children.text: yāgabhedodbhavā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.31 //
children.translated_text: these notions born of varieties of ritual [and region] — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.31]
Painter, scribe, carpenter, reader, reciter, and others —

children.text: kriyābhedabhavā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.32 //
children.translated_text: these notions born of varieties of craft — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.32]
Golden-complexioned, large-eyed, lion-built, and the like —

children.text: kāyasaundaryajā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.33 //
children.translated_text: these notions born of bodily beauty — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.33]
Mute, blind, lame, deaf, one-eyed, squint-eyed, and the like —

children.text: kāyavairūpyajā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.34 //
children.translated_text: these notions born of bodily deformity — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.34]
<s>Pātāla</s> (netherworld), earth, heaven, <s>Mahas</s>, <s>Tapas</s>, <s>Jana</s>, and other [worlds] —

children.text: lokabhedabhavā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.35 //
children.translated_text: these notions born of the varieties of worlds — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.35]
Lion, tiger, boar, bear, deer, monkey, and others —

children.text: paśubhedabhavā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.36 //
children.translated_text: these notions born of the varieties of animals — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.36]
Skin, blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow, semen, and the rest —

children.text: dhātubhedabhavā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.37 //
children.translated_text: these notions born of the varieties of bodily constituents (<s>dhātu</s>) — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.37]
<s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Apāna</s>, <s>Samāna</s>, <s>Udāna</s>, and <s>Vyāna</s> — these five;

children.text: prāṇabhedabhavā bhavā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.38 //
children.translated_text: these notions born of the varieties of vital breath — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.38]
<s>Nāga</s>, <s>Kūrma</s>, <s>Kṛkara</s>, <s>Devadatta</s>, and <s>Dhanañjaya</s> —

children.text: upaprāṇamayā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.39 //
children.translated_text: these notions consisting of the subsidiary vital breaths (<s>upaprāṇa</s>) — the Self is pure, stainless. [NBs 17.39]
Fever, epilepsy, leprosy, <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and the like —

children.text: dhātuvaiṣamyajā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.40 //
children.translated_text: States arising from the imbalance of bodily constituents — the <s>ātman</s> is pure and stainless. [NBs 17.40]
<s>Piṅgalā</s>, <s>Iḍā</s>, <s>Suṣumnā</s>, <s>Gāndhārī</s>, <s>Hastikā</s>, and the rest —

children.text: nāḍībhedabhavā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.41 //
children.translated_text: states arising from the differentiation of <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels) — the <s>ātman</s> is pure and stainless. [NBs 17.41]
The departures, goings, and comings that lead to heaven and hell —

children.text: liṅgabhedodbhavā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.42 //
children.translated_text: states arising from the differentiation of the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>) — the <s>ātman</s> is pure and stainless. [NBs 17.42]
<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s>, <s>Śūdra</s>, and so forth —

children.text: varṇabhedabhavā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.43 //
children.translated_text: states arising from the differentiation of <s>varṇa</s> (caste) — the <s>ātman</s> is pure and stainless. [NBs 17.43]
<s>Brahmacārī</s> (celibate student), <s>gṛhī</s> (householder), <s>vānaprastha</s> (forest-dweller), <s>bhikṣu</s> (mendicant) — in order,

children.text: āśramaprabhavā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.44 //
children.translated_text: states arising from <s>āśrama</s> (stages of life) — the <s>ātman</s> is pure and stainless. [NBs 17.44]
<s>Kāpālikas</s>, <s>Kṣapaṇakas</s> (Jain monks), libertines, <s>Digambaras</s> (sky-clad ones) —

children.text: pākhaṇḍaprabhavā bhāvā ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.45 //
children.translated_text: states arising from heretical sects — the <s>ātman</s> is pure and stainless. [NBs 17.45]
'Mine-ness' (<s>mamatā</s>) is approved by the deluded, not esteemed by those established in equanimity;

children.text: so'pyahantābhavo bhāva ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.46 //
children.translated_text: that state too, the absence of the ego — the <s>ātman</s> is pure and stainless. [NBs 17.46]
O wise one, 'ego' and 'mine-ness' are both daughters of the same mother [i.e., ignorance];

children.text: te parasparakuṭṭinyau tadekāmapi mā spṛśa // NBs_17.47 //
children.translated_text: they are each other's pimps — do not touch even one of them. [NBs 17.47]

children.text: sarve bhāvāḥ pralīyante yasmin bhāve samudgate /
children.translated_text: All states dissolve in that state which has arisen;

children.text: sopi bodhamayo bhāva ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.48 //
children.translated_text: even that state, consisting of awakening — the <s>ātman</s> is pure and stainless. [NBs 17.48]

children.text: yatra bodhamayo bhāvo nāsti bhāve samudgate /
children.translated_text: Where, when a state has arisen, the awakening-state itself is absent,

children.text: sa hi śūnyamayo bhāva ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.49 //
children.translated_text: that state, consisting of the void — the <s>ātman</s> is pure and stainless. [NBs 17.49]

children.text: śūnyāśūnye same yasmin bhāve ca samatāṃ gate /
children.translated_text: When the void and the non-void have become equal, when that state has reached equanimity,

children.text: sa bhāvastvamasi prājña ātmā śuddho nirañjanaḥ // NBs_17.50 //
children.translated_text: that state — 'You are That,' O wise one — the <s>ātman</s> is pure and stainless. [NBs 17.50]
Through the investigation of the stainless God in fifty [verses],
may one attain the stainless abode of the stainless God. [NBs 17.51]
The Eight Verses on the <s>Yamunā</s>

children.text: ujjvalā madhurā śītā pavitrā yamuneva cit /
children.translated_text: Luminous, sweet, cool, and pure — consciousness (<s>cit</s>) is like the <s>Yamunā</s>;

children.text: vivicya dṛṣṭā hi mayā śyāmikā yā'tra sa bhramaḥ // NBs_18.1 //
children.translated_text: having carefully examined, I have seen that the darkness [seemingly] in her — that is a delusion. [NBs 18.1]

children.text: yattvaṃ vadasi ciddevī nīrūpā tūjjvalā katham /
children.translated_text: 'You say the goddess of consciousness is formless — how then is she luminous?'

children.text: tayā prakṣālitaṃ paśya nirmalaṃ hṛdayaṃ mama // NBs_18.2 //
children.translated_text: See my heart, purified by her — it is spotless! [NBs 18.2]

children.text: yattvaṃ vadasi ciddevī nīrasā madhurā katham /
children.translated_text: 'You say the goddess of consciousness is without essence — how then is she sweet?'

children.text: āsvādayanti tāṃ nityaṃ rasikāḥ śaṅkarādayaḥ // NBs_18.3 //
children.translated_text: The connoisseurs — <s>Śaṅkara</s> and others — constantly savor her. [NBs 18.3]

children.text: yattvaṃ vadasi ciddevī niḥsparśā śītalā katham /
children.translated_text: 'You say the goddess of consciousness is without touch — how then is she cool?'

children.text: paśya tasyāḥ prasādena gataṃ tāpatrayaṃ mama // NBs_18.4 //
children.translated_text: See — by her grace, my threefold suffering has departed. [NBs 18.4]

children.text: yattvaṃ vadasi ciddevī nirguṇā pāvanī katham /
children.translated_text: 'You say the goddess of consciousness is without qualities — how then is she purifying?'
See those purified by her — <s>Kaca</s>, <s>Datta</s>, <s>Śuka</s>, and others. [NBs 18.5]
Then the disciple asks:
'O <s>Guru</s>, why do you indicate with merely indicative marks?
O master, indicate with marks such that the indicated [reality] may be apprehended.' [NBs 18.6]
Here is the reply:
In the indicated [reality], the indicated is like the mark — but here, in the indicated, the mark does not [fully apply];
this indicated [reality] is different from the mark — here, the absence of marks is itself the mark. [NBs 18.7]
In the pure, deep water [of the <s>Yamunā</s>], the darkness is of the nature of illusion;
in the pure, deep <s>Brahman</s> too, <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is of the nature of illusion. [NBs 18.8]
The Six Verses on the Stone
What have the rays of infinite crores of moons accomplished?

children.text: āhlādarūpiṇī dṛṣṭā mayā dhenuḥ śilāmayī // NBs_19.1 //
children.translated_text: I have beheld, in the form of delight, a cow made of stone. [NBs 19.1]

children.text: na dhāvati na hantyeva na khādati pibatyapi /
children.translated_text: She does not run, nor does she strike, nor eat, nor drink;
naturally pure, she stands, full of joy and nourishment. [NBs 19.2]
In her hair-lines, crores of universes are contained;

children.text: aparyantā sthitā dhenuḥ sā kāśmīraśilāmayī // NBs_19.3 //
children.translated_text: boundless stands that cow, made of the stone of <s>Kāśmīra</s>. [NBs 19.3]

children.text: āyānti yānti dhāvanti nṛtyanti ca hasanti ca /
children.translated_text: They come, they go, they run, they dance, and they laugh —

children.text: pratibimbā jīvarūpāstasyāḥ sā tu yathā sthitā // NBs_19.4 //
children.translated_text: the reflections in the form of individual souls — while she remains as she is. [NBs 19.4]
Though without essence, she is sweeter than nectar; though without qualities, she is dear to the good;

children.text: nīrūpā'pyatikāntā sā mayā dṛṣṭā na tu śrutā // NBs_19.5 //
children.translated_text: though without form, she is exceedingly beautiful — I have seen her, not merely heard of her. [NBs 19.5]
With the tongue of the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, she constantly streams forth nectar;

children.text: vatsaḥ śilāmayo bhūtvā piba dhenuṃ śilāmayīm // NBs_19.6 //
children.translated_text: become a calf made of stone, and drink from the cow made of stone. [NBs 19.6]
The Five Verses on Sleep
In that sleep, waking, dream, and deep sleep do not exist,
which are of the nature of the three states — because all dualities are abandoned. [NBs 20.1]
Because of being beyond the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), not a trace of <s>tamas</s> (darkness) is found there;
because of being self-luminous in nature, there is no non-illumination either. [NBs 20.2]
To attain which, the greatly meritorious ascetics perform austerities,
and the learned examine the statements of <s>Vedānta</s>. [NBs 20.3]
The enjoyment of pleasure is not the fruit here — it itself is of the nature of bliss;
because of being the nature of the supreme goal of life, it is not a mere pastime. [NBs 20.4]
Easy for those of pure awakening, difficult for those attached to sense-objects,

children.text: sahajā mādhavādīnāṃ sā nidrā tu mahāphalam // NBs_20.5 //
children.translated_text: innate for <s>Mādhava</s> and others — that sleep is indeed the great fruit. [NBs 20.5]
The Nine Verses on Experience
Declared by the <s>gurus</s> who are dense with the bliss of self-knowledge — my own nature is indeed the dense bliss of self-knowledge;

children.text: svānandabodhaghanayā kalayā kayā cit svānandabodhaghanameva mayā'nubhūtam // NBs_21.1 //
children.translated_text: by some art of the dense bliss of self-knowledge, the dense bliss of self-knowledge has indeed been experienced by me. [NBs 21.1]

children.text: śraddhābhaktibhṛtāṃ viśeṣaviduṣāṃ śikṣāvatāṃ yogināṃ mithyāvastuni vastutāṃ vijahatāṃ tyāge gate gāḍhatām /
children.translated_text: For the <s>yogīs</s> endowed with faith, devotion, special learning, and training — who abandon the reality of the unreal, whose renunciation has become deep,

children.text: satye satyatayā sphuratyavirataṃ citte camatkāriṇi svairaṃ sphūrjati nirvikalpaparamānandasvarūpo hariḥ // NBs_21.2 //
children.translated_text: when truth shines as truth unceasingly in the wonder-causing mind — <s>Hari</s>, whose nature is the supreme bliss of the thought-free state, freely blazes forth. [NBs 21.2]

children.text: tṛṣṇāṃ saṃhara saṃharendriyacayaṃ saṃhṛtya sarvāḥ kriyāś cetaḥ saṃhara saṃharānyadhiṣaṇāṃ khādapyaṇustvaṃ bhava /
children.translated_text: Withdraw craving; withdraw the host of senses; having withdrawn all actions, withdraw the mind; withdraw all other faculties; eat up [everything]; become minute.

children.text: antaḥ saṃpraviśātmadhāmani manāgāsādite tatpade sarvājñānakapāṭabhañjanapaṭurbhāvaḥ sthiraḥ sthāsyati // NBs_21.3 //
children.translated_text: When you enter within [your own] abode of the self even slightly, upon reaching that state, a firm state will stand — skilled at breaking open all the doors of ignorance. [NBs 21.3]

children.text: kiṃ māṃ pṛcchasi sādareṇa manasā sādho samādhikramaṃ nūnaṃ nirgatameva mohatimiraṃ jātaḥ prakāśo mahān /
children.translated_text: 'Why do you ask me so earnestly, O good one, about the method of <s>samādhi</s>? Surely the darkness of delusion has already departed — a great light has arisen.',

children.text: ātmasnehaghanāṃ daśāmupagate bodhapradīpe mayi drāguḍḍīya patanti vṛttinivahā naṣṭuṃ pataṅgā iva // NBs_21.4 //
children.translated_text: When the lamp of knowledge, having reached a state dense with self-love, is in me — swiftly flying, the hosts of mental modifications fall to be destroyed, like moths. [NBs 21.4]

children.text: gāḍhaṃ vā'stu vilīnamastu na ghṛtaṃ sādho ghṛtatvādgataṃ caitanyasya camatkṛtiḥ kila tathā cittaṃ tadevādvayam /
children.translated_text: Let the butter be dense or dissolved — O good one, the butter has not departed from its butter-nature; the wonder of consciousness is just like that — the mind is that very non-dual [reality];

children.text: tasmāccittalayasya sādhanamasau tattve tu sākṣātkṛte pratyāhārapariśramo'pi sa mayā saṃtyakta evādhunā // NBs_21.5 //
children.translated_text: therefore, this [dissolution of mind] is the means of <s>cittalaya</s> (dissolution of mind); but when the truth is directly realized, even the effort of <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal) has now been abandoned by me. [NBs 21.5]

children.text: jāte vidvadanugraheṇa sahajānandāgame sādhakair audāsyena yathā yathā parihṛtaḥ kaṣṭaḥ sa yogodyamaḥ /
children.translated_text: When, by the grace of the wise, the advent of innate bliss has occurred, and seekers have gradually abandoned, with indifference, that painful exertion of yoga —

children.text: āścaryaṃ na manīṣitā'pi nibiḍā nidrā yatheyaṃ balād āyātyeva tathā tathā munimato gāḍhaḥ samādhikramaḥ // NBs_21.6 //
children.translated_text: wonder! Just as the dense sleep that was not even wished for comes forcefully of its own accord, so too does the profound course of <s>samādhi</s> come, according to the sage's view. [NBs 21.6]
With the entire form immersed in the ocean of the nectar of meditation, when the truth of <s>Vedānta</s> is ascertained by the subtle intellect,

children.text: ālokiteṣvatha taṭasthadhiyā'khileṣu bhāveṣu bodhaghanatā sahajā'bhyupaiti // NBs_21.7 //
children.translated_text: and then all states are observed with a detached intellect — the innate density of awakening spontaneously arrives. [NBs 21.7]
This is the <s>madhumatī vidyā</s> (honey-knowledge), because of seeing honey everywhere;
even in the tree of one's own body-sun, abundant honey has been seen. [NBs 21.8]
'May I have the vision of <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — such was my heart's desire;

children.text: idānīṃ kṛpayā viṣṇoḥ sarvaṃ viṣṇumayaṃ jagat // NBs_21.9 //
children.translated_text: now, by the grace of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the entire world is pervaded by <s>Viṣṇu</s>. [NBs 21.9]
The Nine Verses on the Power of the Wise

children.text: abhāvo yatra bhāvānāṃ sa bhāvo yatra varṇitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Where there is the absence of [worldly] states — that state in which [it] is described;
listen, O dear one, to the nine verses on the power [of the wise], which bestow natural happiness. [NBs 22.1]
This sage, having abandoned desire and other petty [passions], has gone far away;

children.text: paśyatyapi kadācittānna cainaṃ prāpnuvanti te // NBs_22.2 //
children.translated_text: even if he sometimes sees them, they do not reach him. [NBs 22.2]

children.text: na yānti nūnaṃ tajjñasya sammukhe dvaitadṛṣṭayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Surely the views of duality do not come before the face of the knower of truth;

children.text: duṣṭā duṣṭatayā jñātā darśayanti mukhaṃ katham // NBs_22.3 //
children.translated_text: the wicked, known as wicked — how can they show their face? [NBs 22.3]
<s>Māyā</s>, recognized as <s>Māyā</s>, the transformer of all forms,

children.text: gatā kutrāpyanāvṛtyai saṃsthito nirmalo muniḥ // NBs_22.4 //
children.translated_text: has gone somewhere, never to return — the sage remains pure. [NBs 22.4]
The sense-objects have surely been conquered and slapped with blows;
they do not approach, [thinking] 'this one will strike us.' [NBs 22.5]
Having abandoned thirst for trifles, the sage has attained the state of being free from thorns;
with his soul satisfied by his own elixir, he grows day by day. [NBs 22.6]

children.text: pūrvāṃ māṃ vallabhāṃ tyaktvā ramate vidyayā'dhunā /
children.translated_text: 'Having abandoned me, his former beloved, he now delights in Knowledge' —

children.text: ityavidyā lajjiteva nāyāti mama saṃmukham // NBs_22.7 //
children.translated_text: thus Ignorance, as if ashamed, does not come before my face. [NBs 22.7]

children.text: brahma vaktuṃ na jānāti yathā'tyantajaḍo janaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as an utterly dull person does not know how to speak of <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: tathaivātyantabodhātmā brahma vaktuṃ na budhyate // NBs_22.8 //
children.translated_text: so too one of the nature of utter awakening does not think to speak of <s>Brahman</s>. [NBs 22.8]
Surely the fault of laziness would steal the glory even of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>);

children.text: yathā yathā'laso jñānī vardhate'sau tathā tathā // NBs_22.9 //
children.translated_text: [but] the more the wise man becomes 'lazy' [in worldly terms], the more he grows. [NBs 22.9]
The Ten Verses on <s>Nirvāṇa</s>

children.text: na śakyaṃ vaktumevedaṃ tathāpi kṛpayā tava /
children.translated_text: This cannot be spoken at all; yet, out of compassion for you,

children.text: kayā citkalayā vatsa nirvāṇadaśakaṃ bruve // NBs_23.1 //
children.translated_text: by some art, O child, I shall speak the ten verses on <s>nirvāṇa</s>. [NBs 23.1]

children.text: mohanidrā na tatrāsti tenāyaṃ jāgaro mahān /
children.translated_text: The sleep of delusion is not there — therefore this is a great waking;

children.text: bhāvādayo na bhāsante tenāyaṃ naiva jāgaraḥ // NBs_23.2 //
children.translated_text: [yet] states and the rest do not appear — therefore this is not waking at all. [NBs 23.2]
An unprecedented thing shines forth — therefore this is a supreme dream;

children.text: dṛśyaṃ na bhāsate tatra tena svapno na caiva saḥ // NBs_23.3 //
children.translated_text: [yet] the visible does not appear there — therefore it is not a dream either. [NBs 23.3]
Because of the absence of objects, it is deep sleep of the nature of bliss;

children.text: na jāḍyaṃ na tamastatra suṣuptirapi naiva sā // NBs_23.4 //
children.translated_text: [yet] there is no dullness, no darkness there — therefore it is not deep sleep either. [NBs 23.4]
Free from the three states, it is proclaimed as <s>turīya</s> (the fourth);
[yet] there is no knowledge of one, two, or three — what does <s>turīya</s> depend on? [NBs 23.5]
This is the true form of the individual soul — therefore it is called <s>jīva</s> (soul);

children.text: jīvaceṣṭā na tatrāsti tena nirjīvatā sphuṭā // NBs_23.6 //
children.translated_text: [yet] the activity of the soul is not there — therefore lifelessness is evident. [NBs 23.6]
Because of being of the nature of existence, consciousness, and bliss, if it is <s>Brahman</s> — yet even that may not apply;

children.text: yo veda sa tu na brūte yo na veda girā'sya kim // NBs_23.7 //
children.translated_text: he who knows does not speak — he who does not know, what can his words [accomplish]? [NBs 23.7]
Therefore <s>śruti</s> (scripture) declares the truth to be beyond speech and mind;
as experienced by the sages, just so it is — there is no doubt. [NBs 23.8]
This is the culmination of all sacred tradition; this is the culmination of all asceticism;
instruction too culminates in this; discrimination too culminates in this. [NBs 23.9]

children.text: śrotavyaṃ śrutivākyena sarvaṃ brahma tvayā śrutam /
children.translated_text: By the statement of <s>śruti</s>, 'all is <s>Brahman</s>' has been heard by you;

children.text: bhavitavyaṃ yadi brahma tarhi brahmaiva bhūyatām // NBs_23.10 //
children.translated_text: if one is to become <s>Brahman</s>, then let one become <s>Brahman</s> indeed! [NBs 23.10]
The Five Verses on the Lamp of Knowledge
It does not require a base or vessel, nor does it need oil;

children.text: na vartikāmāśrayate na dhatte kajjalaṃ manāk // NBs_24.1 //
children.translated_text: it does not depend on a wick, nor does it produce even a trace of soot. [NBs 24.1]

children.text: na tāpakarttā kasyāpi vāyunā na ca kampate /
children.translated_text: It causes no heat to anyone; it is not shaken by wind;

children.text: na vināśamavāpnoti tamaḥ sarvaṃ nihanti ca // NBs_24.2 //
children.translated_text: it does not undergo destruction; and it destroys all darkness. [NBs 24.2]
All things appear as one form by its light;

children.text: yadagre na prakāśeta cchāyā māyāsvarūpiṇī // NBs_24.3 //
children.translated_text: before it, shadow — which is of the nature of <s>māyā</s> — does not appear. [NBs 24.3]
That which is beyond the scope of the eyes, devoid of form and shape,
and unilluminable even by the mind — yet it is the illuminator of form and shape. [NBs 24.4]
Sometime, somewhere, O dear one, by some cause,
this lamp of knowledge is lit in the temple of the hearts of the good. [NBs 24.5]
The Sixteen Instructions
By means of reason alone, empty the mind-pot that is full of mental tendencies;

children.text: na kaścidbhavitā tāta brahmaṇā pūraṇe śramaḥ // NBs_25.1 //
children.translated_text: O dear one, there will be no effort at all in filling [it] with <s>Brahman</s>. [NBs 25.1]
Abandon worry, O great-minded one; enjoy the happiness of freedom from worry;

children.text: tvayā'rjitāmimāṃ cintāṃ vada ko'nyaḥ parityajet // NBs_25.2 //
children.translated_text: this worry that you have acquired — tell me, what other person would let it go? [NBs 25.2]
The thing to be contemplated by you is the remedy for the disease of worry;

children.text: athavā tāta cintā''khyaṃ rogameva parityaja // NBs_25.3 //
children.translated_text: or rather, O dear one, abandon the disease called worry itself. [NBs 25.3]

children.text: vardhitā vardhate cintā tyaktā naśyati sattvaram /
children.translated_text: Worry, when nurtured, grows; when abandoned, it quickly perishes;

children.text: īdṛśenāpi rogeṇa durdhiyo maraṇaṃ gatāḥ // NBs_25.4 //
children.translated_text: from such a disease, even the dull-witted have gone to death. [NBs 25.4]
Harsh, quarrelsome, demanding, barren, eternally inauspicious —

children.text: tyajyatāṃ kāmanā caṇḍī bhujyatāṃ muktisundarī // NBs_25.5 //
children.translated_text: Abandon the fierce woman called Desire; embrace the beautiful woman called Liberation. [NBs 25.5]

children.text: janaiḥ paṇḍita ityuktaḥ prāpnoṣi paramaṃ sukham /
children.translated_text: You are called a learned one by people, and you attain supreme happiness;

children.text: manasā karmaṇā vācā bhava paṇḍita eva tat // NBs_25.6 //
children.translated_text: by mind, action, and speech, be that learned one indeed. [NBs 25.6]
You are indeed of an ever-shining form, for your nature is consciousness;
this world is but a certain shining forth of your own shining-form. [NBs 25.7]

children.text: bhāsvato mama bhāmātramiti jñāte bhrame gate /
children.translated_text: When it is known — 'I am the luminous one; this [world] is merely my radiance' — and the delusion has departed,

children.text: kva dvitīyaṃ kva saṃsāraḥ kva māyā tatkṛtaṃ kimu // NBs_25.8 //
children.translated_text: where then is a second? Where is <s>saṃsāra</s>? Where is <s>māyā</s>? What has it produced? [NBs 25.8]
Knowership, agentship, experiencership, the perspectives of inert and conscious —
these are your own self-manifestations; become a jewel and observe [them]. [NBs 25.9]
Mutually unaware of each other — waking, dream, and deep sleep;

children.text: tvayā tisraḥ striyo bhuktāsturīyāṃ sundarīṃ bhaja // NBs_25.10 //
children.translated_text: you have enjoyed three women — now worship the beautiful fourth (<s>turīya</s>). [NBs 25.10]
Waking, dream, and deep sleep — again you observe these;

children.text: turīyaṃ tava dhāmaiva na tatkimiti paśyasi // NBs_25.11 //
children.translated_text: <s>turīya</s> is your own abode — why do you not see it as 'what is this?' [NBs 25.11]

children.text: mā dhāva sukhahetostvaṃ dhāvatāṃ na sukhaṃ sakhe /
children.translated_text: Do not run seeking happiness — there is no happiness for those who run, O friend;

children.text: sukharūpe nije rūpe sukhaṃ tiṣṭha sukhī bhava // NBs_25.12 //
children.translated_text: in your own form, which is the form of bliss, rest happily — be happy. [NBs 25.12]
Here are some verses:

children.text: varayogyā'si kalyāṇi na sthāsyasi varaṃ vinā /
children.translated_text: O auspicious one, you are worthy of a bridegroom — you shall not remain without one;
the bridegroom to be chosen should be one who is ageless and deathless. [NBs 25.13]

children.text: na śṛṇoṣi varaṃ yāvattāvatte kampate manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Until you hear of [such] a bridegroom, your mind trembles;
afterwards, O blessed one, with great celebration you shall choose your lord. [NBs 25.14]
Today, on my advice, enjoy yourself with the Supreme Person;

children.text: sakhi paścātsvataścittaṃ kuru yatrādhikaṃ sukham // NBs_25.15 //
children.translated_text: friend, afterwards direct your mind of its own accord to where there is greater happiness. [NBs 25.15]

children.text: yātaṃ dinaṃ na punareti navaṃ vayaste lajjāṃ vihāya bhaja taṃ ramaṇīyarūpam /
children.translated_text: The day that has passed does not return; your youth is new — abandon shame and embrace that one of delightful form;

children.text: bāle paraḥ puruṣa eṣa yadā sametaḥ svargeṇa kiṃ kimu tadā nṛsukhena vā te // NBs_25.16 //
children.translated_text: O young one, when this Supreme Person is attained, of what use is heaven to you then, or human happiness? [NBs 25.16]
Page 559
Twenty Investigations into <s>Brahman</s> (<s>Brahmacarcā</s>)
Worship (<s>arcā</s>) whose aim is higher [than ordinary worship] is called the investigation (<s>carcā</s>) of the Supreme Self itself;
therefore, for the awakening of the disciple, the investigation of <s>Brahman</s> is set forth. [NBs 26.1]
<s>Brahman</s> is the support of all beings, yet nothing is its support;

children.text: nirādhārasvarūpaṃ cennāsti brahma tadā kvacit // NBs_26.2 //
children.translated_text: if its nature is unsupported — then <s>Brahman</s> would not exist anywhere. [NBs 26.2]

children.text: adhiṣṭhānaṃ vinā kāryaṃ na tiṣṭhati kadācana /
children.translated_text: Without a substratum, an effect never subsists;

children.text: sarvādhiṣṭhānarūpaṃ hi kathaṃ brahma na kutracit // NBs_26.3 //
children.translated_text: if <s>Brahman</s> is the universal substratum, how can it be 'nowhere'? [NBs 26.3]
That <s>Brahman</s> is separate from everything — this cannot be said,
for if everything is of its nature, how can it be separate from everything? [NBs 26.4]
That <s>Brahman</s> is non-separate from everything — you should not say that either,
for as separate from everything, it has been experienced by the great sages. [NBs 26.5]
If you argue that this [world] should be called 'of the nature of the Self' —

children.text: anātmarūpaṃ kiṃ nvasti svātmarūpaṃ yatastvidam // NBs_26.6 //
children.translated_text: what then is not of the nature of the Self, since this [world] is indeed of one's own nature? [NBs 26.6]

children.text: jñānasya brahma viṣaya iti vaktuṃ na śakyate /
children.translated_text: That <s>Brahman</s> is the object of knowledge — this cannot be said,

children.text: jñānasvarūpaṃ tadbrahma jñānasya viṣayaḥ katham // NBs_26.7 //
children.translated_text: for <s>Brahman</s> is of the nature of knowledge itself — how can it be the object of knowledge? [NBs 26.7]
If you think, 'Let <s>Brahman</s> be of the nature of knowledge itself' —

children.text: jñeyameva na yatrāsti jñānatvaṃ tasya kīdṛśam // NBs_26.8 //
children.translated_text: where there is nothing to be known, what kind of 'knowledge-ness' does it have? [NBs 26.8]
If it is conceived that <s>Brahman</s> is of the nature of the knower —
in what is self-luminous by nature, how can there be dependence on [separate] knowledge? [NBs 26.9]
That this <s>Brahman</s> is of all forms — who could say so?
For it is always of one form alone, since it is said to be eternal. [NBs 26.10]
That this <s>Brahman</s> is of one form — this too cannot be said,

children.text: nirguṇaṃ tatparaṃ brahma syādekatvaṃ yato guṇaḥ // NBs_26.11 //
children.translated_text: for that supreme <s>Brahman</s> is without qualities, since oneness would itself be a quality. [NBs 26.11]
That supreme <s>Brahman</s> is without qualities — surely this is inappropriate,

children.text: anantenaiva gīyante hyanantā eva tadguṇāḥ // NBs_26.12 //
children.translated_text: for its infinite qualities are sung indeed by the infinite [scriptures]. [NBs 26.12]

children.text: brahma nāstīti ko brūyādbhātīdaṃ yasya sattvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Who would say '<s>Brahman</s> does not exist'? — for this [world] shines by virtue of its reality.

children.text: tarhyasti brahmetyapi no nātaḥ sattā pṛthagyataḥ // NBs_26.13 //
children.translated_text: But then, '<s>Brahman</s> exists' is also not [correct] — because existence is not separate [from it]. [NBs 26.13]
How could a wise person say that this <s>Brahman</s> is 'not of one's own nature'?
This <s>Brahman</s> is directly experienced as one's own nature. [NBs 26.14]
'This <s>Brahman</s> is of one's own nature' — even this is not quite accurate,

children.text: tatra ko nu svaśabdārtho yatsvarūpamidaṃ bhavet // NBs_26.15 //
children.translated_text: for what then is the meaning of the word 'own' that would [separately] constitute its nature? [NBs 26.15]
If 'own-ness' means that which distinguishes from another — then state it;

children.text: yatra svaparabhāvo na brahma kiṃ tatra nāsti hi // NBs_26.16 //
children.translated_text: where there is no sense of 'own' and 'other' — does <s>Brahman</s> not exist there? [NBs 26.16]

children.text: ahameva paraṃ brahma brahmāhamiti ca śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I am indeed the supreme <s>Brahman</s>' — and from the scripture 'I am <s>Brahman</s>';

children.text: kathaṃ bhavedahaṃ brahmāhantā yatra na vidyate // NBs_26.17 //
children.translated_text: how can I be <s>Brahman</s> where the 'I'-sense does not exist? [NBs 26.17]

children.text: tvameva tatparaṃ brahma tvaṃ brahmeti śrutirjagau /
children.translated_text: 'You are that supreme <s>Brahman</s>' — the scripture sang 'You are <s>Brahman</s>';

children.text: tvameva tatkathaṃ brahma tvaṃtā yatra na varttate // NBs_26.18 //
children.translated_text: how can you be that <s>Brahman</s> where the 'you'-sense does not obtain? [NBs 26.18]
To say 'that is <s>Brahman</s>' on the authority of scripture — 'that is <s>Brahman</s>' cannot be said,
for in what is utterly without separation, how can it be as if remote? [NBs 26.19]
When the sleep of delusion has perished, when the mind of the sage has dissolved,
what remains — that is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, beyond the reach of mind and speech. [NBs 26.20]
With this investigation, worthy of further investigation, let the wise

children.text: carcayantu paraṃ brahma tuṣyantu ca ramantu ca // NBs_26.21 //
children.translated_text: investigate the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, and may they be satisfied and delighted. [NBs 26.21]
Page 572
The Four [Stages of] Spontaneous Conduct (<s>Svecchācāra</s>)
O blessed virtuous one, listen with a concentrated mind;
the four [stages of] spontaneous conduct are the very essence of the ultimate truth. [NBs 27.1]
