Abandoning her own husband, the housewife herself carries on worldly affairs;
she dallies with another man — she is called 'the clever adulteress.' [NBs 27.2]
Separating the ego, the <s>turīya</s>-intellect, day by day,

children.text: patyā pareṇa ramate puṃścalī parasaṅginī // NBs_27.3 //
children.translated_text: dallies with the other husband — [she is] the wanton one, attached to the other. [NBs 27.3]
Afterwards, conquered by the woman, that [husband] too, unable to retaliate,

children.text: asyāḥ sambhogavelāyāṃ gṛhaṃ santyajya gacchati // NBs_27.4 //
children.translated_text: at the time of her enjoyment, abandons the house and departs. [NBs 27.4]

children.text: īdṛśe vyavahāre tu dāmpatyaṃ vada kīdṛśam /
children.translated_text: In such a relationship, tell — what kind of marriage [remains]?
Within a few days, spontaneous conduct begins. [NBs 27.5]

body.text: svānubhavānāṃ satyapi bādhitāhankāre samādhibhaṅgo nāstītyarthaḥ // NBs_27.6 //
body.translated_text: The meaning is: for the experiences of the Self, even though the ego has been sublated, there is no breaking of <s>samādhi</s>. [NBs 27.6]

children.translated_text: Page 577
Three Illustrations of the Non-obstructive Nature of the Ego
A child, seeing a snake painted on a wall, runs away;
some [other] child says, 'This is a painted snake.' [NBs 28.1]
From then on, that [first child], now wise, plays with it;
similarly, the deluded one, perceiving the ego within the Self, runs away. [NBs 28.2]
Therein the true <s>guru</s> declares, 'Only consciousness exists here, nothing else';

children.text: tataḥ prabhṛtyasau vidvāṃstenaiva saha khelati // NBs_28.3 //
children.translated_text: from then on, that [person], now wise, plays with it. [NBs 28.3]
Page 579
Two Pearls of Question and Answer
There the <s>vāsanā</s> (latent desire) of sense-objects says:
'One should not play with snakes; one should not contemplate the Self;

children.text: aho jīva mahāmūḍha maraṇaṃ te bhaviṣyati // NBs_29.1 //
children.translated_text: alas, O living being, O greatly deluded one, death shall befall you!' [NBs 29.1]
That living being replied:

children.text: ahinānena ye daṣṭā amaratvaṃ gatā hi te /
children.translated_text: 'Those who have been bitten by this snake have attained immortality;
its fang is made of nectar — therefore I play with this snake.' [NBs 29.2]
Page 581
Three Wonders of Question and Answer

children.text: yathāpūrvaṃ na khelanti yathāpūrvaṃ hasanti na /
children.translated_text: 'They do not play as before, they do not laugh as before' —

children.text: kaiścitkāmādayaḥ pṛṣṭāḥ bhavantaḥ kiṃ hataprabhāḥ // NBs_30.1 //
children.translated_text: when <s>kāma</s> (desire) and the other [passions] were asked: 'Are you of diminished power?' [NBs 30.1]
<s>Kāma</s> and the others said:

children.text: asmānpuṣṇāti yā nityaṃ sā'smākaṃ jananī mṛtā /
children.translated_text: 'Our mother who always nourished us has died;

children.text: sukhalubdhena pitrā naḥ kācidanyā kṛtā vadhūḥ // NBs_30.2 //
children.translated_text: our father, greedy for happiness, has married some other woman. [NBs 30.2]

children.text: asmāndviṣyati sā nityaṃ na puṣṇāti kadācana /
children.translated_text: She always hates us and never nourishes us;
within a few days, [we shall have to] leave the house.' [NBs 30.3]
Page 583
The Eight Verses on the Play of Suckling
The revered <s>Guru</s> says:

children.text: upamātā ca mātā ca bāla mātṛdvayaṃ hi te /
children.translated_text: 'O child, you have two mothers — a foster-mother and a real mother;
the breast-milk of the foster-mother is bitter, sour, sweet, and pungent, [NBs 31.1]
associated with old age and death, its essence being the varied tastes of duality;

children.text: nijamātā tava tu yā tanmāhātmyaṃ vadāmyaham // NBs_31.2 //
children.translated_text: but your real mother — I shall tell you of her greatness. [NBs 31.2]

children.text: saiva mātā pitā saiva jagatāmīśvarī ca sā /
children.translated_text: She alone is the mother, she alone the father, she the mistress of the worlds;

children.text: sā gatiḥ sā paraṃ tattvaṃ tatparaṃ nāsti kiñcana // NBs_31.3 //
children.translated_text: she is the goal, she is the supreme reality — beyond her there is nothing. [NBs 31.3]
Your foster-mother is of low birth; your [real] mother is of noble birth;

children.text: tāṃ kujātiṃ parityajya sujātiṃ mātaraṃ śraya // NBs_31.4 //
children.translated_text: abandoning that low-born one, take refuge in the noble-born mother. [NBs 31.4]
The breast-milk of your real mother rains the nectar of non-duality;
it destroys birth, disease, and old age — once drunk, it conquers death. [NBs 31.5]
Previously, in your deluded state, you did not know the difference between the two;
now, knowing the difference, drink from the breast of your real mother. [NBs 31.6]

children.text: tvayā stane parityakte sā vidīrya mriyeta cet /
children.translated_text: If, when you abandon her breast, she were to burst and die,
the association with the low-born would perish — that would be beneficial indeed. [NBs 31.7]
Dear one, the mixture of <s>māyā</s> and <s>Brahman</s> — why this confusion of castes?
Abandoning <s>māyā</s> alone, become of the nature of pure <s>Brahman</s>.' [NBs 31.8]
Page 591
The Four Wonders

children.text: andhaḥ paśyati sarvaṃ ca paṅguryāti purātpuram /
children.translated_text: The blind one sees everything; the lame one goes from city to city;

children.text: jaḍaḥ kāryāṇi kurute nīraso rasamaśnute // NBs_32.1 //
children.translated_text: the inert one accomplishes tasks; the tasteless one relishes flavor. [NBs 32.1]
The unconscious one determines the ultimate; the dispassionate one enjoys pleasures;
the one devoid of all touch attains the touch of <s>Brahman</s>. [NBs 32.2]
The all-consuming one carries no food in his belly;

children.text: mugdho bhunakti pāṇḍityaṃ siddhāntaṃ vakti maunavān // NBs_32.3 //
children.translated_text: the bewildered one enjoys erudition; the silent one speaks the established doctrine. [NBs 32.3]
The one without enmity attains victory; the desireless one attains the fullness of desire;
the sleeping one is awake in wisdom; even the dead one tastes immortality. [NBs 32.4]
Page 596

body.text:
turīyatulasīpatrapūjā
turīyatulasīpatrairviṣṇupūjā nirūpyate /
premapradhānabhāvena śṛṅgārarasarūpiṇī// NBs_33.1 //
body.translated_text: Worship with <s>Tulasī</s> Leaves of the Fourth State. The worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s> with <s>tulasī</s> leaves of the <s>turīya</s> (fourth state) is set forth, predominantly through the sentiment of love, in the form of the <s>śṛṅgāra rasa</s> (amorous sentiment). [NBs 33.1]

children.translated_text: Here are the words of the <s>Gopī</s>:

children.text: dṛṣṭyā mayā madhurayā kalito'dhunā'yaṃ yatkāminījanamanoharaṇo mukundaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'With my sweet gaze I have now perceived this <s>Mukunda</s>, who captivates the minds of amorous women; I contemplate him in my heart — there is no happiness in this house; let my dwelling be with him in that forest.' [NBs 33.2]

children.text: taṃ cintayāmi hṛdaye na sukhaṃ gṛhe'smiṃs tasminvane bhavatu tena sahaiva vāsaḥ // NBs_33.2 //
gopālikā'smi caturā na ca me manīṣā dehaśritā vividhagorasavāsanā me /
children.translated_text: 'I am a clever cowherd-girl; my intelligence is not body-bound; my tendencies are toward the various essences of the cow; pondering what should be done, I stood — and then, by force, <s>Mukunda</s> met me.' [NBs 33.3]

children.text: kimvā vidheyamiti cintayatī sthitā'haṃ tāvadbalānmilita eva mayā mukundaḥ // NBs_33.3 //
ekākinī bata gatā'smi vane niśīthe kuñje nilīya ramaṇasya raso gṛhītaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Alone I went to the forest at midnight; hiding in a bower, I partook of the beloved's essence; it is wondrous — I worship and do not perceive the cause there — [yet] all these companions of mine are of cheerful countenance.' [NBs 33.4]

children.text: citraṃ bhajāmi kalayāmi na tatra hetuṃ sarvāḥ prasannavadanā yadimā vayasyāḥ // NBs_33.4 //
kiṃ varṇayāmi purataḥ kila kasya varṇyaṃ kiṃ varṇitena sakhi varṇayituṃ na śakyam /
children.translated_text: 'What shall I describe? Before whom should what be described? What use is describing? O friend, it cannot be described; my limbs have melted along with my waist-cloth, my lip having been bitten by the lord of love in the ecstasy of passion.' [NBs 33.5]

children.text: aṅgāni me vigalitāni sahaiva nīvyā daṣṭe'dhare ratirase ratināyakena // NBs_33.5 //
nanvetadeva sukṛtaṃ phalitaṃ madīyaṃ yatkāminīṣu rasalaṃpaṭa eṣa kṛṣṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Surely it is my own merit that has borne fruit — that this <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is amorous among women; otherwise, for the Lord of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, there would be no reason for any conversation with us cowherd-women.' [NBs 33.6]

children.text: lakṣmīpateritarathā na bhavedakasmād asmāsu gopavanitāsu kathāprasaṅgaḥ // NBs_33.6 //

children.translated_text: The wearer of the forest-garland (<s>Vanamālī</s>), well-worshipped with <s>tulasī</s> leaves of <s>turīya</s>,
grants the most desired fruit that [grows] in this forest. [NBs 33.7]
Page 608
The Garland of Reasons, the Pearl-String
When the matter is established by the authority of scripture, what use are reasons? Still,
because it has the nature of novel composition, the ornament [of reasoning] is great. [NBs 34.1]
Birth is [said to be] the coming into being of the non-existent; but the sage who has attained direct realization

children.text: sadrūpatāmeva gatastena janma na vidyate // NBs_34.2 //
children.translated_text: has entered the state of the Real itself — therefore birth does not exist [for him]. [NBs 34.2]
The sage who has attained direct realization has obtained the immortal <s>Brahman</s>;

children.text: amṛtaṃ yena saṃprāptaṃ sa mṛtatvaṃ kathaṃ vrajet // NBs_34.3 //
children.translated_text: how can one who has attained the immortal go to a state of death? [NBs 34.3]
Death is the abandonment of the body; the sage who has attained direct realization

children.text: śarīraṃ tyaktavānpūrvaṃ mṛtasya maraṇaṃ kimu // NBs_34.4 //
children.translated_text: has already abandoned the body — what death can there be for the [already] dead? [NBs 34.4]
This sage who has attained direct realization, along with the ego-sense itself,
has abandoned doership — therefore he is not tainted by actions. [NBs 34.5]
The sage who has attained direct realization is inherently pure of self;

children.text: na ca puṇyaiḥ pavitro'sau tena puṇyairna lipyate // NBs_34.6 //
children.translated_text: he is not purified by merits — therefore he is not tainted by merits. [NBs 34.6]
This sage who has attained direct realization is of an absolutely pure nature;

children.text: tatkaroti pavitraṃ yattena pāpairna lipyate // NBs_34.7 //
children.translated_text: that which he does, he makes pure — therefore he is not tainted by sins. [NBs 34.7]
Because of being of the nature of innate bliss, the sage who has attained direct realization —

children.text: yena hṛṣyati tannāsti tasmādeṣa na hṛṣyati // NBs_34.8 //
children.translated_text: there is nothing that can make him rejoice; therefore he does not rejoice [at anything particular]. [NBs 34.8]
No one is capable of harming the sage who has attained direct realization;

children.text: apakartturabhāvena sa tu na dveṣṭi kaṃcana // NBs_34.9 //
children.translated_text: since there is no one who can harm him, he hates no one. [NBs 34.9]
What remains unattained for the sage who has attained direct realization?

children.text: hānirnāsti tato hetorna śocati kadācana // NBs_34.10 //
children.translated_text: Since there is no loss, he never grieves. [NBs 34.10]
The sage who has attained direct realization, in every way,

children.text: brahma sarvātmakaṃ prāpya na kāṅkṣati kimapyuta // NBs_34.11 //
children.translated_text: having attained <s>Brahman</s>, which is the Self of all, does not desire anything whatsoever. [NBs 34.11]
Indeed no one is stronger than the sage who has attained direct realization;

children.text: yasmādbibheti tannāsti tasmādeṣa bibheti na // NBs_34.12 //
children.translated_text: since there is nothing that he fears, he is fearless. [NBs 34.12]
Whatever is the supreme purpose of the sage who has attained direct realization,

children.text: tatsarvameva saṃsiddhaṃ na tasmātsa viṣīdati // NBs_34.13 //
children.translated_text: all of that is already accomplished — therefore he does not despair. [NBs 34.13]
Worthy of honor by <s>Brahmā</s> and the rest, the sage who has attained direct realization,

children.text: mānito yadi lokena sa tu mānaṃ na vindati // NBs_34.14 //
children.translated_text: even when honored by the world, does not feel honored. [NBs 34.14]
Worthy of honor even by the lords of the gods, the sage who has attained direct realization,

children.text: na mānito yadi janairapamānaṃ na vindati // NBs_34.15 //
children.translated_text: even when dishonored by people, does not feel dishonored. [NBs 34.15]
Neither benefit nor harm to the sage who has attained direct realization

children.text: śakyau na kenacitkartuṃ tulyo mitrāripakṣayoḥ // NBs_34.16 //
children.translated_text: can be done by anyone — he is equal toward the sides of friend and foe. [NBs 34.16]
Having transcended the states of merit and defect, the sage who has attained direct realization
has attained the supreme abode — for him, censure and praise are equal. [NBs 34.17]
There is no possessiveness toward home and the like for the sage who has attained direct realization;
therefore he is called 'homeless' — a sage whose home is wherever he is at evening. [NBs 34.18]
Having attained the previously unattained knowledge, the sage who has attained direct realization —

children.text: sa tu na kṣīyate tena niryogakṣema ātmavān // NBs_34.19 //
children.translated_text: that [knowledge] does not diminish; therefore he is self-possessed, beyond gain and protection. [NBs 34.19]
Although the sage who has attained direct realization is the same everywhere,

children.text: tathāpi tatstāvakasya mama stutiphalaṃ mahat // NBs_34.20 //
children.translated_text: still, for me, his devotee, the fruit of praising him is great. [NBs 34.20]
This garland of reasons, a necklace of diamonds, should be worn by the wise around the neck;
because it is of an unprecedented composition, what ornament could be greater? [NBs 34.21]
The Key to Liberation (<s>Kaivalyakuñcikā</s>)
O child, properly ascertain the Key to Liberation;

children.text: udghāṭaya kapāṭaṃ ca bodharatnaṃ kare kuru // NBs_35.1 //
children.translated_text: open the door and place the jewel of knowledge in your hand. [NBs 35.1]

children.text: dṛṣṭyā śrutyā'nubhūtyā vā yo yo bhāvaḥ parisphuret /
children.translated_text: Whatever entity arises — whether through seeing, hearing, or experience —
that entity should be immediately divided into five parts. [NBs 35.2]

children.text: asti bhāti priyaṃ rūpaṃ nāma cetyaṃśapañcakam /
children.translated_text: Existence (<s>asti</s>), consciousness (<s>bhāti</s>), dearness (<s>priyam</s>), form (<s>rūpa</s>), and name (<s>nāma</s>) — these are the five aspects;

children.text: ādyaṃ trayaṃ brahmarūpaṃ māyārūpaṃ tato dvayam // NBs_35.3 //
children.translated_text: the first three are of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>; the latter two are of the nature of <s>Māyā</s>. [NBs 35.3]

children.text: nāmarūpe tu naiva stastatra hetuṃ vadāmyaham /
children.translated_text: Name and form do not truly exist — I shall state the reason for this:

children.text: nāma tu vyavahārārthaṃ kalpitaṃ na tu vāstavam // NBs_35.4 //
children.translated_text: a name is conceived merely for conventional purposes; it is not real. [NBs 35.4]

children.text: ghaṭo na gho nāpi ca ṭastāvubhau yatkhamāśritau /
children.translated_text: A pot (<s>ghaṭa</s>) is neither the syllable 'gha' nor the syllable 'ṭa'; those two depend on space [as sound];
'gha' is guttural and 'ṭa' is cerebral — and these two never [occur] at the same time. [NBs 35.5]
Thus are all names; now examine form, O dear one:

children.text: ghaṭastu pṛthivīrūpaṃ sā jaḍā jalarūpiṇī // NBs_35.6 //
children.translated_text: the pot is of the form of earth; earth is inert, of the form of water. [NBs 35.6]

children.text: tejaso jalamutpannaṃ tadvāyoḥ sa ca khodbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Water is produced from fire; that from wind; and wind is born from space;
space and all [the elements] arise from ego-sense; and that is born from <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature). [NBs 35.7]
<s>Prakṛti</s>, whose nature is the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), is <s>Māyā</s>; and <s>Māyā</s>, being composed of <s>Māyā</s>, does not [truly] exist;

children.text: nāmarūpe tato na sto'thāstītyādi vicāraya // NBs_35.8 //
children.translated_text: therefore name and form do not exist. Now examine 'existence' (<s>asti</s>) and the rest. [NBs 35.8]
'Existence' (<s>asti</s>) is Being (<s>sat</s>); 'consciousness' (<s>bhāti</s>) is Consciousness (<s>cit</s>); 'dearness' (<s>priyam</s>) is characterized by Bliss (<s>ānanda</s>);
that which is of the nature of Being-Consciousness-Bliss (<s>saccidānanda</s>) — that <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute liberation) alone remains. [NBs 35.9]
<s>Samādhi</s> (absorption) should be practiced there — this [samādhi] is suffused with the meaning;

children.text: atha śabdānuviddhaṃ tu samādhiṃ kathayāmi te // NBs_35.10 //
children.translated_text: now I shall tell you the <s>samādhi</s> suffused with words. [NBs 35.10]
'I am indeed eternal, I am pure, I am of the nature of consciousness, without interruption,

children.text: sahajānandarūpo'smi na me māyā na me malaḥ // NBs_35.11 //
children.translated_text: I am of the nature of innate bliss — <s>Māyā</s> does not belong to me, nor does impurity.' [NBs 35.11]
'In this [world], which when absent [shows that] existence was bestowed by me in the form of consciousness —

children.text: upasaṃhṛtya sattāṃ tāṃ svasattāyāmahaṃ sthitaḥ // NBs_35.12 //
children.translated_text: having withdrawn that existence, I am established in my own being.' [NBs 35.12]
'I am not a modification through modification, nor <s>Prakṛti</s> through <s>Prakṛti</s>;

children.text: tathāpi jātaṃ mayi cettarhi jātamajātavat // NBs_35.13 //
children.translated_text: yet if something has arisen in me, then what has arisen is as if unarisen.' [NBs 35.13]
'O Self of the universe, withdraw!' — even as I say this,
this [world] is already withdrawn — it is seen but does not [truly] stand. [NBs 35.14]
Through the contemplation of the purport of the words and sentences of such <s>Upaniṣad</s> statements,
the <s>samādhi</s> called 'word-suffused' arises for the sage. [NBs 35.15]
The meaning-suffused [<s>samādhi</s>] has been described; then the word-suffused;
having duly practiced both, one should enter the [<s>samādhi</s>] free from both. [NBs 35.16]
Just as, having held two pieces of chalk, the syllable <s>OṂ</s> is written,
so too, having held the two [types of] <s>samādhi</s>, let the meaning of <s>OṂ</s> be inscribed. [NBs 35.17]

children.text: paṭoḥ praṇavalekheṣu te hi nāvaśyake yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as the two chalk-pieces are not necessary once the <s>OṂ</s> is written on the cloth,
so too the two [types of] <s>samādhi</s> [are not necessary] once the cloth [bears] the meaning of <s>OṂ</s>. [NBs 35.18]
Steadfastness in the <s>nirvikalpa samādhi</s> (thought-free absorption) is the goal of the <s>yogin</s> of knowledge;
this Key to Liberation is the cause of opening the door. [NBs 35.19]

children.text: rahasyaṃ hi rahasyānāṃ nidhīnāṃ paramo nidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: It is the secret of secrets, the supreme treasure among treasures,
the supreme reasoning among reasonings — this Key to Liberation. [NBs 35.20]
In the tradition of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and <s>Vyāsa</s>, through the path of <s>Śaṅkarācārya</s> —
and again by the <s>Śaṅkarācāryas</s>, full of the essence of compassion, [NBs 35.21]
it was transmitted to <s>Ānandabodha</s> and others, and held in succession by the wise;
it is to be especially understood — this Key to Liberation. [NBs 35.22]
The Praise of Intellect (<s>Buddhipraśaṃsā</s>)
Just as intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) is the root of all conventional activity,

children.text: tadvattu paramārthasya nidānaṃ buddhireva hi // NBs_36.1 //
children.translated_text: so too intellect alone is the basis of the supreme truth. [NBs 36.1]
What is known yet [appears] unknown — if not known through intellect, then

children.text: buddhyā buddhaṃ tu yadbuddhaṃ tannābuddhaṃ kadāpi ca // NBs_36.2 //
children.translated_text: what is truly known through intellect — that is never unknown. [NBs 36.2]

children.text: buddhyā na buddho yo bodho dvaitabodhabudhairapi /
children.translated_text: The knowledge that is not known by the intellect — even by those of dualistic knowledge, the wise [say]:

children.text: buddhyā buddhamimaṃ viddhi buddhisākṣitayā budhaiḥ // NBs_36.3 //
children.translated_text: 'Know this as known through the intellect' — by the wise, through the witnessing-nature of the intellect. [NBs 36.3]
What is unknown yet known, and what is known yet [appears] as if unknown —
knowing through the intellect that which is equal in being known and unknown, yet distinct from the unknown. [NBs 36.4]
The Trilogy of the Play of Color (<s>Raṅgalīlātrayī</s>)
The sky of the heart, colored with various colorings, has become variegated;

children.text: raṅge nirañjane kṣiptaṃ raṅgaṃ prāptaṃ nirañjanam // NBs_37.1 //
children.translated_text: cast into the stainless stage, it has attained the stage of the stainless. [NBs 37.1]
The sky of the heart, having now attained the stainless stage,

children.text: rañjitaṃ rañjanaiścitrairapi raṅgaṃ bibharti na // NBs_37.2 //
children.translated_text: even when colored with various colorings, no longer retains the coloring. [NBs 37.2]
O child, establish this twofold play of color in the mind;

children.text: raṅgaṃ parīkṣaya dhiyā sāñjanaṃ ca nirañjanam // NBs_37.3 //
children.translated_text: examine with the intellect the stage — both stained and stainless. [NBs 37.3]
The Quartet of Wonder of Moonlight and Moon (<s>Candrikācandracamatkāracatuṣṭayī</s>)

children.text: acandre candrikā nāsti na candraścandrikāṃ vinā /
children.translated_text: Without the moon there is no moonlight; without moonlight there is no moon;
how can the union of moonlight and moon be separated? [NBs 38.1]

children.text: vismṛtyā candrikā nāptā smṛtyā''pteva tu candrikā /
children.translated_text: Through forgetfulness, moonlight is not obtained; through remembrance, moonlight is obtained, as it were;
has the identity of moonlight and moon been prevented by anyone? [NBs 38.2]
You yourself have experienced the wonder of moonlight and moon;
O dear one, for the sake of showing an illustration, it has been made manifest again. [NBs 38.3]

children.text: tāvatī candrikā proktā yāvāneva hi candramāḥ /
children.translated_text: The moonlight is exactly as much as the moon itself;
this moon is beginningless and endless, and its moonlight is beginningless and endless. [NBs 38.4]
The Fivefold Wondrous Beheading (<s>Adbhutaśiraśchedapañcakam</s>)
Through the dispassion born of inquiry into the principles, the supreme [attainment] is the forgetting of the universe;
cutting the head of what is to be cut is better than cutting limb by limb. [NBs 39.1]
If, even when cutting limb by limb, the head itself is what must be cut,

children.text: prathamaṃ tacchiraśchindhi vṛthā kiṃ ceṣṭayā'nyayā // NBs_39.2 //
children.translated_text: then cut that head first — why the vain effort of anything else? [NBs 39.2]

children.text: dayāśīlā hi munayo muneḥ sā'pi dayālutā /
children.translated_text: Sages are indeed compassionate; and that compassion of the sage
is what severs the head of the mind without the pain of cutting limb by limb. [NBs 39.3]

children.text: sadyo mama śiraśchindhi māmityāha mano mama /
children.translated_text: 'Cut off my head at once!' — so says my mind to me —

children.text: mayā soḍhuṃ na śakyante pratyaṅgacchedadurdaśāḥ // NBs_39.4 //
children.translated_text: 'I cannot endure the miseries of having my limbs cut one by one.' [NBs 39.4]
The innumerable states born of the mind — how can they be cut off one by one?
Therefore this mind has been cut off completely by me, O sage. [NBs 39.5]
The Nectar of Questions from the Revered <s>Guru</s> to the Disciple Who Has Attained Direct Realization:
That which is eternally experienced, yet which had attained the state of being unexperienced —
the supreme state has been experienced through the touches of the essence of experience. [NBs 40.1]
Through the very marks of direct perception, which are distinct from outward-turned [mental] activity,
<s>Śiva</s> has been directly realized — with the marks of Being-Consciousness-Bliss. [NBs 40.2]
You rejoice, lulled to sleep like <s>Mukunda</s> (baby <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>)

children.text: lālitaḥ prāpito nidrāṃ mukunda iva modase // NBs_40.3 //
children.translated_text: by the sweet, gentle Vedāntic utterances sung like <s>Yaśodā</s>'s lullabies. [NBs 40.3]
Inwardly nourished by the delightful bites of fresh-butter-like marvels of self-knowledge,
you play like the child <s>Mukunda</s>. [NBs 40.4]
Having dissolved the visible into your own Self, having attained solitude,

children.text: kiṃ nṛtyasi nijānande mahādeva ivātmani // NBs_40.5 //
children.translated_text: do you dance in your own bliss like <s>Mahādeva</s> (the great God) in himself? [NBs 40.5]
At the evening-time called <s>samādhi</s>, seeing your own power, <s>Umā</s>,
who is tender and beautiful in all limbs — do you dance like <s>Maheśa</s> (the great Lord)? [NBs 40.6]
Having drunk the poison of the visible, having digested it in the Self,

children.text: mṛttyuñjayapadaṃ prāptaḥ kiṃ hṛṣyasi haro yathā // NBs_40.7 //
children.translated_text: having attained the state of the Conqueror of Death — do you rejoice like <s>Hara</s> (Śiva)? [NBs 40.7]
Just as one sees one's face by bringing it before a mirror,

children.text: akhaṇḍavṛttau ca tathā svarūpaṃ kiṃ vilokitam // NBs_40.8 //
children.translated_text: so too, in the unbroken <s>vṛtti</s> (mental modification) — have you beheld your own true nature? [NBs 40.8]
Seeing <s>Hari</s> within and without, seeing <s>Māyā</s> pervading the world,

children.text: vismayaṃ paramaṃ yāsi mārkaṇḍeya ivātmani // NBs_40.9 //
children.translated_text: you attain supreme wonder in yourself, like <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>. [NBs 40.9]
The Disciple's Reply:
O revered <s>Guru</s>, for us, through the compassion of the glorious ones

children.text: śrīmatāṃ kṛpayā nūnamasmākaṃ kimu durlabham // NBs_41.1 //
children.translated_text: whose minds are full of grace and who possess [spiritual] power — indeed, what is difficult to attain? [NBs 41.1]
The Quartet on Conduct (<s>Caryācatuṣṭayī</s>)

children.text: jātyā yadyapi gaurameva vadanaṃ rūpasya nāsti kṣatistatkiṃ kajjalakālimā mukhatale saṃlāpanīyo budhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: If the face is naturally fair and there is no blemish in beauty, why should the wise smear black collyrium on the face? If even through evil deeds there is no damage to the knower of <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: astu brahmavidaḥ kṛtairapi na tairduṣkarmabhiścetkṣatiḥ kiṃ kāmādikadarthitā varamaho niḥsaṅgasaukhyaṃ varam // NBs_42.1 //
children.translated_text: why the harassment of desire and the rest? Far better is the bliss of non-attachment — far better indeed! [NBs 42.1]

children.text: vidyaivādhigatā sadā'mṛtamayī vidyāvatā tatsukhaṃ stheyaṃ vartmani saṅgadoṣarahite saṅgaḥ punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ /
children.translated_text: The knowledge that has been attained is always nectar-like; the one who possesses knowledge has that bliss; one should abide on the path free from the fault of attachment — what kind of attachment [could there be]?

children.text: kiṃ bhūṣā'sya varā sthitiḥ stutimayī sā rājasiṃhāsane dvāri dvāri kapardikārthamaṭanaṃ kiṃ vā'sya rājño varam // NBs_42.2 //
children.translated_text: What [need for] ornaments? His excellent state is one of praise [itself] — sitting on that royal throne; rather than wandering from door to door for a cowrie's worth — what is better than being a king? [NBs 42.2]

children.text: śiṣṭācārapathaṃ vinā yadi bhavedātmaprabodho mahāṃstyājyastarhi tu sarvadaiva viduṣā varṇāśramāṇāṃ kramaḥ /
children.translated_text: If the great awakening of the Self should occur outside the path of righteous conduct, then the wise person should always abandon the order of <s>varṇas</s> (classes) and <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life); if the path of the knower is extraordinary, what [difference does it make] whether actions are performed or not performed?

children.text: vartma jñasya vilakṣaṇaṃ yadi kṛtātkiṃ cākṛtātkarmaṇaḥ saṃgṛhṇātu janāṃstadā munijanastenāpi nāsya kṣatiḥ // NBs_42.3 //
children.translated_text: Let him [then] embrace the people — even by that, there is no harm to him. [NBs 42.3]

children.text: datto'sāvṛṣabho jaḍaśca bharato maṅkiśca saṃvarttakaḥ karmabhraṣṭapathaṃ gatāḥ kathamamī cetpūrvapakṣastava /
children.translated_text: If you cite as your objection that <s>Datta</s> (Dattātreya), the dull <s>Bharata</s>, <s>Maṅki</s>, and <s>Saṃvarttaka</s> went on a path that deviated from prescribed action —

children.text: sādho jāgaritānpratīdamuditaṃ paśyanti śṛṇvanti ye nidrāndhā na vilokayanti na punaḥ śṛṇvanti vācyā na te // NBs_42.4 //
children.translated_text: O virtuous one, this is said regarding those who are awake — those who see and hear; the blind with sleep neither see nor hear — they are not to be addressed. [NBs 42.4]
The Eighty Waves of the River of Knowledge (<s>Jñānagaṅgātaraṅgonāśītikam</s>)
Now hear the eighty [verses] called "Waves of the River of Knowledge" (<s>Jñānagaṅgātaraṅga</s>).
By even one wave clinging [to the body], all sins are destroyed. [NBs 43.1]

children.text: vāṅmayaṃ khaṃ hi sarvatra vāco mūkasya durlabhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Space is indeed made of sound everywhere, yet speech is unattainable for the mute.

children.text: cinmayaṃ brahma sarvatra vidyāhīnasya durlabham // NBs_43.2 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, <s>Brahman</s> made of consciousness is everywhere, yet it is unattainable for one devoid of knowledge. [NBs 43.2]

children.text: prācīmatha pratīcīṃ vā yatra kvacana gacchatu /
children.translated_text: Whether one goes east or west or anywhere at all,

children.text: tamasā dṛśyate naiṣā brahmacidbhāskaro yathā // NBs_43.3 //
children.translated_text: darkness is not seen by the sun of <s>Brahman</s>-consciousness. [NBs 43.3]
Just as in the empty sphere of space there is the sphere of stars,
so in the empty sphere of <s>Brahman</s>-consciousness there is the sphere of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence). [NBs 43.4]
While in the nature of the waking state itself, the sage sees this world as dream-like.
As if in deep sleep yet in the form of consciousness — the sage's state of <s>turīya</s> (the fourth state) is wondrous. [NBs 43.5]

children.text: mumukṣā dambhamātraṃ te na te tīvrā mumukṣutā /
children.translated_text: Your desire for liberation is mere pretense; you do not have intense longing for liberation.

children.text: tīvrā yadi mumukṣā syānna vilambo bhavediyān // NBs_43.6 //
children.translated_text: If there were intense desire for liberation, there would not be this much delay. [NBs 43.6]

children.text: abhūtkuhūmayaṃ viśvaṃ pakṣaḥ sa malino gataḥ /
children.translated_text: The universe had become like a new-moon night; that dark fortnight has passed.

children.text: idānīṃ nirmalaḥ pakṣo jātaṃ rākāmayaṃ jagat // NBs_43.7 //
children.translated_text: Now the bright fortnight has come; the world has become like a full-moon [night]. [NBs 43.7]

children.text: na tiṣṭhati mano yatra goḥ śṛṅge sarṣapo yathā /
children.translated_text: Where the mind does not stay — like a mustard seed on a cow's horn —
those established in <s>samādhi</s>, like mountains, have attained stability right there. [NBs 43.8]
Like a flowing stream that is naturally uninterrupted,
far beyond the fourteen [types of worldly] cognitions is the sage's mental state. [NBs 43.9]
Having fallen from the state of the Supreme Self, he again attains the state of the Supreme Self,

children.text: yayā prāpnoti viśvātmā sā munermananasthitiḥ // NBs_43.10 //
children.translated_text: the Soul of the universe — that is the sage's mental state. [NBs 43.10]
The pure one, standing nearby, does not accept a reflection.

children.text: prapañcavañcane yuktiḥ sā munereva nāmuneḥ // NBs_43.11 //
children.translated_text: The skill of being undeceived by the phenomenal world belongs to the sage alone, not to the non-sage. [NBs 43.11]
"Let them depart!" — when told thus, these [mental states] depart in an instant.

children.text: yadājñayā manobhāvāḥ sa vaśī kasya nādbhutaḥ // NBs_43.12 //
children.translated_text: He by whose command the states of mind [obey] — that master, for whom is he not wondrous? [NBs 43.12]
Through the digestion of <s>kālakūṭa</s> poison, <s>Śambhu</s>'s (<s>Śiva's</s>) serpents became tame.
Similarly, through the killing of the mind, the activities of the sense-organs [become tame] for the sage. [NBs 43.13]
If the abandonment of ego (<s>ahantā</s>) and possessiveness (<s>mamatā</s>) cannot be accomplished,
then let the absence of ego and possessiveness be practiced everywhere. [NBs 43.14]
One who is beautiful in caste, stage of life, age, dress, learning, and conduct —

children.text: vinā vicāravairāgyaiḥ paśureva na saṃśayaḥ // NBs_43.15 //
children.translated_text: without inquiry and dispassion, is merely an animal, without doubt. [NBs 43.15]
He in whose mind sharp inquiry and dispassion are constantly present —
he is the learned one; what need has he of thinking about other means? [NBs 43.16]
A tree grows by watering the root; it dries up by drying the root;
it is reduced to ashes by the flames of fire — such is the nature of a tree. [NBs 43.17]
[<s>Saṃsāra</s>] grows by the watering of the mind; it dries up by the drying of the mind;
it is reduced to ashes by the flames of knowledge — such is the nature of worldly existence. [NBs 43.18]
The swan (<s>haṃsa</s>) situated on the far shore appears reflected as though in two.
Similarly, the seer of truth, standing on the bank, knows the self. [NBs 43.19]
Wondrous! In a short time, for one whose mind is roasted by knowledge,
like a roasted seed, the capacity to produce effects is gone. [NBs 43.20]

children.text: paṅgavastu kṛtā eva dṛgādyā na calanti yat /
children.translated_text: "I have already made the senses lame, so that the eye and the rest do not move;

children.text: andhānapi kariṣyāmi na paśyanti yathā jagat // NBs_43.21 //
children.translated_text: I shall also make them blind, so that they do not see the world." [NBs 43.21]

children.text: jānātu vā na jānātu brahma jīvasya jīvanam /
children.translated_text: Whether one knows it or not, <s>Brahman</s> is the life of the living being.

children.text: jānāti cetparo lābho na jānāti bhayaṃ mahat // NBs_43.22 //
children.translated_text: If one knows, it is the supreme gain; if one does not know, it is great danger. [NBs 43.22]
The nature of the cow of <s>Brahman</s> is different from the celestial wish-fulfilling cow.
The drinker of her milk immediately becomes one with her form. [NBs 43.23]

children.text: yadi yoge kṛtā buddhiḥ saptamīṃ gaccha bhūmikām /
children.translated_text: If the intellect is directed toward <s>yoga</s>, go to the seventh stage.
If drowned [in worldliness], go to the netherworld — such is the saying of the wise. [NBs 43.24]

children.text: madhyāhnabhāskaraṃ draṣṭuṃ sākṣādyadi tu na kṣamam /
children.translated_text: If one is unable to look directly at the midday sun,
one should see it through a cloth, or reflected in water. [NBs 43.25]
Similarly, if one is unable to [realize] the fierce sun of pure consciousness in its <s>nirvikalpa</s> (thought-free) [form],
one should see it through its all-pervasiveness, or as the inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>). [NBs 43.26]

children.text: lakṣaṃ śarāḥ prayoktavyāḥ sūkṣme lakṣye'pi dhanvinā /
children.translated_text: A hundred thousand arrows should be shot by the archer at the subtle target.
By chance, through divine conjunction, even one will hit. [NBs 43.27]
Let the activity of the mind always be directed toward the practice of meditation.
Sometime, by the grace of <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), the undivided form will be [realized]. [NBs 43.28]
Of <s>Hari's</s> ocean of sport, how [vast is it that he had] sixteen thousand women,
and innumerable women of various tastes were enjoyed by him.
Yet that very one was brought to a state of submission by <s>Bhāmā</s> (<s>Satyabhāmā</s>).
The lord of the <s>Yadus</s> was thoroughly mastered; therefore <s>Satyabhāmā</s> alone is truly blessed. [NBs 43.29]

body.translated_text: "A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is even better than <s>Brahman</s> itself" — thus he says by means of two [verses]:

children.text: varttate brahma sarvatra brāhmaṇo labhyate kvacit /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> exists everywhere, but a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (knower of <s>Brahman</s>) is found rarely.
Since <s>Brahman</s> is of moderate value, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> would be of great value. [NBs 43.30]
Attached to the pleasure of another's company — like women of yogins —

children.text: vihāya lokasiddhāntaṃ ramate svamate manaḥ // NBs_43.31 //
children.translated_text: abandoning established worldly doctrine, the mind delights in its own doctrine. [NBs 43.31]
By blocking the holes for water, the lake appears full.
By blocking the holes of mental modifications, knowledge is full — what is surprising? [NBs 43.32]
Rootless, without parts, dried up, and wretched is the desire for enjoyment.

children.text: tayā tirohitaḥ svāmī tṛṇeneva mahāgiriḥ // NBs_43.33 //
children.translated_text: Yet by it the Lord is concealed — like a great mountain by a blade of grass. [NBs 43.33]

children.text: na deśakālau na vayo na yuktirna vidagdhatā /
children.translated_text: Neither place, nor time, nor age, nor reasoning, nor cleverness —
whenever there is the abandonment of desire (<s>vāsanā</s>), that very moment is your liberation. [NBs 43.34]
When the field is purified by means, and pure seed is planted —

children.text: kiṃ citraṃ dhānyasampattau sa devo yadi varṣati // NBs_43.35 //
children.translated_text: what is surprising about an abundant harvest, if the god [of rain] showers? [NBs 43.35]
For one who has inquired into the statements [of the Vedas] and desires the supreme truth,
the weightiest knowledge is non-knowledge; non-knowledge is the supreme knowledge. [NBs 43.36]
You expound the words of <s>Vedānta</s>, you defeat the dualists —

children.text: nāntarviśasi tanmanye tatrāsti maraṇaṃ tava // NBs_43.37 //
children.translated_text: yet you do not enter within; I think that therein lies your death. [NBs 43.37]
When asked by a friend about his welfare, remembering his former condition,

children.text: idānīṃ kuśalaṃ jātamiti hṛṣyati yogavit // NBs_43.38 //
children.translated_text: the knower of <s>yoga</s> rejoices: "Now welfare has arisen!" [NBs 43.38]
The mere ritualist is like an empty copper vessel coated with gold;
but the wise one is like a supreme golden vessel filled with jewels. [NBs 43.39]
Though both are alike in being trees, the difference between the two is such:
the wise one is like a sugarcane stalk; the ignorant one is like a mere stick of wood. [NBs 43.40]
"My husband delights only in the expansive vision, not in anything else;

children.text: yena dṛṣṭirviśālā syātsa mantro mama dīyatām // NBs_43.41 //
children.translated_text: give me that <s>mantra</s> by which the vision becomes expansive." [NBs 43.41]
Knowing "this one is to be worshipped," [the foolish woman] worshipped him, put him to sleep in her house,

children.text: na bhukto mūḍhayā svāmī kaścitpuruṣa ityayam // NBs_43.42 //
children.translated_text: but did not enjoy the master; the foolish woman [thought:] "this is merely some man." [NBs 43.42]
Having spent the night on the bed in attire fit for enjoyment,

children.text: priyasya bhogamaprāpya prātaḥ krandati kāminī // NBs_43.43 //
children.translated_text: the lover-woman weeps in the morning, not having obtained the enjoyment of her beloved. [NBs 43.43]
A woman painted on a canvas, wondrous in the wealth of her beauty,
is looked at only until the real beautiful woman arrives. [NBs 43.44]

children.text: cintāmaṇiṃ karādbhraṣṭaṃ mā śucaḥ prāha me guruḥ /
children.translated_text: "Do not grieve for the wish-fulfilling jewel that has slipped from your hand," my guru said.
"In just a few days, it will be found again." [NBs 43.45]
As long as I harbor doubt about seeing the face of <s>Mukunda</s>,

children.text: āśvāsayati māṃ tāvatparamā devatā manaḥ // NBs_43.46 //
children.translated_text: the supreme deity, the mind, reassures me. [NBs 43.46]
The beauty of ten million <s>Kandarpas</s> (Love-gods) — this is truly said of <s>Janārdana</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>).
<s>Kandarpa</s> and all his ilk fled in his radiance. [NBs 43.47]
Tears were shed by <s>Rādhā</s>, separated and hoping for reunion.

children.text: tatraiva māyayā guptaḥ prāptaḥ prakaṭatāṃ hariḥ // NBs_43.48 //
children.translated_text: Right there, concealed by <s>māyā</s>, <s>Hari</s> appeared. [NBs 43.48]
Some bees wander about for fragrance, and others long for honey.

children.text: na bhramanti na kāṅkṣanti madhumattā madhuvratāḥ // NBs_43.49 //
children.translated_text: Those intoxicated with honey neither wander nor long. [NBs 43.49]
The wood-carrier earns wealth with difficulty at twilight.
The gem-appraiser, seated comfortably, [earns] abundant wealth. [NBs 43.50]

children.text: narttakī svāṅgabhaṅgena dhanaṃ prāpnoti vā na vā /
children.translated_text: A dancing-girl, through bodily contortions, may or may not earn wealth.

children.text: kulāṅganā kaṭākṣeṇa svaṃ vaśīkurute patim // NBs_43.51 //
children.translated_text: A woman of good family, with a sidelong glance, brings her own husband under her control. [NBs 43.51]
This radiance of your intellect tells me that liberation is near.

children.text: nūnaṃ nirvāṇasamaye dīpo dedīpyate bhṛśam // NBs_43.52 //
children.translated_text: Surely, at the time of extinction, the lamp blazes most brightly. [NBs 43.52]

children.text: eke khananti vasudhāṃ tathā vikrayiṇaḥ pare /
children.translated_text: Some dig the earth, and others are sellers.

children.text: gharṣayantyapare ratnaṃ bhogaṃ gṛhnāti bhāgyavān // NBs_43.53 //
children.translated_text: Others polish the gem — the fortunate one takes the enjoyment. [NBs 43.53]
Some are satisfied with buttermilk, and others with curds and milk.

children.text: tattvajñā naiva tuṣyanti navanītaghṛtaṃ vinā // NBs_43.54 //
children.translated_text: The knowers of truth are never satisfied without butter and ghee. [NBs 43.54]

children.text: yatra kvāpi svapāmīti jātā nidrālutā mama /
children.translated_text: "I shall sleep anywhere" — such drowsiness has come upon me.

children.text: vistīrṇaṃ śayanaṃ prāptaṃ komalaṃ brahma nirmalam // NBs_43.55 //
children.translated_text: I have obtained a vast, soft, pure bed — <s>Brahman</s>. [NBs 43.55]
The visible, rubbed away by knowledge, has assumed the form of consciousness.

children.text: yatra yatraiva paśyāmi svaṃ rūpaṃ tatra dṛśyate // NBs_43.56 //
children.translated_text: Wherever I look, my own form is seen there. [NBs 43.56]
Because a python has swallowed even one person, people praise the python.

children.text: māṃ na stuvanti kiṃ yena gīrṇā brahmāṇḍakoṭayaḥ // NBs_43.57 //
children.translated_text: Why do they not praise me, by whom billions of universes have been swallowed? [NBs 43.57]

children.text: mayyasūyā na karttavyā bahu jalpāmi yadyapi /
children.translated_text: Let no envy be directed toward me, even though I speak much.
I say only "I am <s>Brahman</s>" — the <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) does not fault me. [NBs 43.58]
<s>Samādhi</s> is my throne; the <s>Vedāntas</s> are my bards.
The enemy named Delusion has been slain; my kingdom is without thorns. [NBs 43.59]
I have seen that which is called <s>Cidambara</s> (the space of consciousness) — a vast expanse.
This inert space is empty, utterly small in comparison. [NBs 43.60]
Food is dear to the hungry, wealth is dear to the poor,

children.text: tṛṣitasya jalaṃ tviṣṭaṃ caitanyaṃ mama vallabham // NBs_43.61 //
children.translated_text: water is dear to the thirsty — consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>) is my beloved. [NBs 43.61]
Through contact with the alchemical elixir, copper has gone beyond copper-ness.
Similarly, our ego has gone to the state of non-ego. [NBs 43.62]
Formerly, ego was the cause of my suffering.
The enemy is now seen dead — [it has become] the cause of supreme bliss. [NBs 43.63]

children.text: bhogepsūnāṃ sabhāmadhye bhoktā kānto yathā yuvā /
children.translated_text: Just as among those desirous of enjoyment, a young, handsome lover shines in the assembly,

children.text: mumukṣuṇāṃ tathā madhye rājate paramārthavit // NBs_43.64 //
children.translated_text: so among seekers of liberation, the knower of the supreme truth shines. [NBs 43.64]
Just as a lover-woman, though engaged in household duties, [is like one who] has already enjoyed her lover —
so the knower of <s>yoga</s> delights the mind with the mind itself. [NBs 43.65]

children.text: munimānanditaṃ dṛṣṭvā grāmīṇo vakti taṃ muhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing the sage delighted, the villager repeatedly says to him:

children.text: tvayā yastu nidhiḥ prāptastaṃ pradarśaya māmapi // NBs_43.66 //
children.translated_text: "Show me too the treasure that you have found!" [NBs 43.66]

children.text: vañcakairviṣayaistāta vada ke ke na vañcitāḥ /
children.translated_text: O dear one, tell me — who has not been deceived by the deceitful sense-objects?
Surely even these [sense-objects] have been deceived by the gurus, who are tigers among men. [NBs 43.67]
Let the dull people pour a thousand pots of water upon the head.
The knower of the self should cling to silence alone, like a <s>Śiva-liṅga</s>. [NBs 43.68]
Gurus with inquiry are [good] gurus; dispassionate ones are the best among gurus.

children.text: vicāre'pi viraktā ye gurūṇāṃ guravo hi te // NBs_43.69 //
children.translated_text: Those who are dispassionate even toward inquiry — they are the gurus of gurus. [NBs 43.69]
Even one who merely seeks to know abandons the hard-to-abandon sense-objects, though deluded.

children.text: vidāṃ tadrāgadoṣasya tyāge kimiva duṣkaram // NBs_43.70 //
children.translated_text: For the wise who know the fault of attachment, what difficulty can there be in renunciation? [NBs 43.70]
Worldly talk may arise even for those who have attained knowledge —

children.text: jāgare samanuprāpte yathā svapnakathā nṛṇām // NBs_43.71 //
children.translated_text: just as talk of dreams [may arise] for people when they have come to the waking state. [NBs 43.71]
When the visible is forgotten through delusion, deep sleep is experienced.
When the visible is forgotten through knowledge, <s>turīya</s> (the fourth state) remains. [NBs 43.72]

children.text: dṛśyaṃ cetsyādravirna syāttama ekaṃ tadā kila /
children.translated_text: If there were the visible but no sun, then there would be darkness alone.
If there were the sun, there would be the world — then there would be practical activity. [NBs 43.73]
If there is the sun but no world, then there would be light alone.

children.text: iti lokasthitiḥ putra paramārthagatiṃ śṛṇu // NBs_43.74 //
children.translated_text: Such is the state of the world, O son; hear the state of the supreme truth. [NBs 43.74]

children.text: nityo hi ravirasmākaṃ tasya nāśo na vidyate /
children.translated_text: For us, the sun is eternal; its destruction does not exist.
Even when all has become darkness, the witness of darkness is ever-imperishable. [NBs 43.75]
For the sage established in <s>samādhi</s>, the sun exists but the world does not.

children.text: anena hetunā sādho jyotirekaṃ tadā kila // NBs_43.76 //
children.translated_text: for this reason, O virtuous one, then there is light alone. [NBs 43.76]
When the sun exists, the world exists — for the observer of transactions;

children.text: ravirnāsti jagannāsti tama ekaṃ tadā kila // NBs_43.77 //
children.translated_text: when the sun does not exist, the world does not exist — then there is darkness alone. [NBs 43.77]
When the illuminable has departed, O son, what would the light illuminate?
Even with the destruction of illuminability, the nature of illumination is unbroken. [NBs 43.78]

children.text: āyātu yātu vā bhānoḥ prakāśyaṃ nijahetubhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Let the illuminable of the sun come or go by its own causes;

children.text: na mama svaprakāśasya kiñcidāyāti gacchati // NBs_43.79 //
children.translated_text: for me, who am self-luminous, nothing comes and nothing goes. [NBs 43.79]
The glory of the mind.

children.text: kiṃ baddhamasi muktaṃ vā manaḥ pṛccha mahāmune /
children.translated_text: Ask the mind, O great sage: 'Are you bound or free?'
If it says 'bound,' then you are undoubtedly bound. [NBs 44.1]
If it says 'somewhat free,' then you are somewhat free, due to delusion;

children.text: yadi muktamiti brūyāttarhi mukto'si mohataḥ // NBs_44.2 //
children.translated_text: if it says 'free,' then you are free from delusion. [NBs 44.2]

children.text: baddhena manasā baddho mukto muktena cetasā /
children.translated_text: Bound by a bound mind, freed by a freed mind;

children.text: na baddho na ca mukto'yamiti vedāntanirṇayaḥ // NBs_44.3 //
children.translated_text: this [Self] is neither bound nor free — this is the conclusion of <s>Vedānta</s>. [NBs 44.3]

children.text: sphuranti mahimāno ye yatra yatra jagattraye /
children.translated_text: Whatever glories manifest wherever in the three worlds,

children.text: te sarve manaso dharmā mano hi mahimā''śrayam // NBs_44.4 //
children.translated_text: all those are properties of the mind; the mind indeed is the abode of glory. [NBs 44.4]

children.text: aṇimā mahimā caiva laghimā garimā tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Aṇimā</s> (minuteness), <s>mahimā</s> (greatness), <s>laghimā</s> (lightness), <s>garimā</s> (heaviness),

children.text: prāptiḥ prākāmyamīśitvaṃ vaśitvaṃ manaso guṇāḥ // NBs_44.5 //
children.translated_text: <s>prāpti</s> (attainment), <s>prākāmya</s> (irresistible will), <s>īśitva</s> (lordship), and <s>vaśitva</s> (mastery) — these are qualities of the mind. [NBs 44.5]

children.text: mano dhanurmano maurvī mana eva dhanurdharaḥ /
children.translated_text: The mind is the bow, the mind is the bowstring, the mind itself is the archer;

children.text: mano lakṣyaṃ mano vedho mano viddhaṃ vimuktaye // NBs_44.6 //
children.translated_text: the mind is the target, the mind is the piercing, the mind is what is pierced — for liberation. [NBs 44.6]
The mind alone is the cause of bondage and liberation for human beings;

children.text: ito'dhikaṃ tu kiṃ vācyamadvaye tu sthitaṃ na tat // NBs_44.7 //
children.translated_text: what more can be said beyond this? But when established in non-duality, it is not that [i.e., it transcends even this]. [NBs 44.7]
The slaying of the animal [of ignorance] by the goddess <s>Cit-Caṇḍī</s>.

children.text: cittāhaṃkṛtibuddhimānasamayairyuktaṃ caturbhiḥ padaiśchittvā'ntaḥkaraṇaṃ paśuṃ paraśunā bodhena tīkṣṇena yaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who, with the sharp axe of knowledge, cuts the animal of the inner instrument — endowed with its four feet of <s>citta</s> (thought), <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), and <s>manas</s> (mind) —

children.text: ciccaṇḍīcaraṇāmbujārcanamanuprāptaḥ prasādaṃ paraṃ kiñcitraṃ caraṇe luṭhanti rabhasāttasyākhilāḥ siddhayaḥ // NBs_45.1 //
children.translated_text: and having worshipped the lotus-feet of <s>Cit-Caṇḍī</s> (the goddess of consciousness), has attained supreme grace — it is no wonder that all <s>siddhi</s>s (powers) roll eagerly at his feet. [NBs 45.1]
Eighteen [verses] on liberation while living (<s>jīvanmukti</s>).
Having freed the self from the self, which was bound by mental construct (<s>saṃkalpa</s>), through [the dissolution of] mental construct,

children.text: ātmanā''tmani santuṣṭaḥ svātmārāmaḥ svayaṃ hariḥ // NBs_46.1 //
children.translated_text: content in the self by the self, delighting in the self, he is <s>Hari</s> [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] himself. [NBs 46.1]
One's own nature alone is <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute oneness); <s>saṃsāra</s> is pure foolishness;

children.text: aticitrā gatiḥ putra jīvanmuktasya yā sthitiḥ // NBs_46.2 //
children.translated_text: most wondrous, O son, is the state of the <s>jīvanmukta</s> (one liberated while living). [NBs 46.2]
Birth was taken as play for the attainment of the joy of <s>jīvanmukti</s>,

children.text: ātmanā nityamuktena na tu saṃsārakāmyayā // NBs_46.3 //
children.translated_text: by the self that is eternally free — not out of desire for <s>saṃsāra</s>. [NBs 46.3]
If this deceptive drama called <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) did not exist,
how would the Self of all obtain the great festival of <s>jīvanmukti</s>? [NBs 46.4]

children.text: advaitaṃ na sadehe'sti videhe dvaitamasti na /
children.translated_text: Non-duality does not exist in the embodied [state]; duality does not exist in the disembodied [state];
the great festival of duality-and-non-duality belongs to the <s>jīvanmukta</s>, not to any other. [NBs 46.5]

children.text: sadehe na videhatvaṃ videhe na sadehatā /
children.translated_text: In the embodied [state], there is no disembodiment; in the disembodied [state], there is no embodiment;
embodiment and disembodiment both operate in the <s>jīvanmukta</s>. [NBs 46.6]

children.text: sadehasya videhatvaṃ yadi na syāttadā vada /
children.translated_text: If the disembodied state of an embodied being were not possible, then tell —

children.text: janakasya sadehasya kathaṃ proktā videhatā // NBs_46.7 //
children.translated_text: how was the disembodied state (<s>videhatā</s>) proclaimed for <s>Janaka</s>, who was embodied? [NBs 46.7]

children.text: videhasya sadehatvaṃ yadi na syāttadā vada /
children.translated_text: If the embodied state of a disembodied being were not possible, then tell —

children.text: janakasya videhasya kathaṃ proktā sadehatā // NBs_46.8 //
children.translated_text: how was the embodied state proclaimed for <s>Janaka</s>, who was [also called] <s>Videha</s>? [NBs 46.8]
Liberation is certain in the scriptures; <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living) is well-established;
without attaining the state of being liberated while living, there is no liberation in the disembodied state. [NBs 46.9]

children.text: jñānaṃ vinā na kaivalyaṃ na mṛto jñānavānbhavet /
children.translated_text: Without knowledge, there is no <s>kaivalya</s>; a dead person cannot become a knower;
the attainment of knowledge occurs while living — that <s>jīvanmukti</s> is imperishable. [NBs 46.10]
If [one objects:] the happiness of <s>jīvanmukti</s> is for a short time — what use? — then listen:

children.text: brahmaloke virājante kathaṃ te sanakādayaḥ // NBs_46.11 //
children.translated_text: How do <s>Sanaka</s> and others shine in the world of <s>Brahman</s>? [NBs 46.11]
Therefore, this is a play of <s>Īśvara</s>, having the form of <s>Īśvara</s> himself;
<s>jīvanmukti</s>, the perpetuator of the tradition, is [a stepping stone to] the great liberation. [NBs 46.12]
In which the sages such as <s>Nārada</s> and others play unceasingly;
that which has been experienced by the knowers themselves — that <s>jīvanmukti</s> is imperishable. [NBs 46.13]
Those who, abandoning pastimes that distract the mind,

children.text: sthitā nirvāṇaniṣṭhāyāṃ ta eva sanakādayaḥ // NBs_46.14 //
children.translated_text: are established in the state of <s>nirvāṇa</s> (extinction) — they are indeed <s>Sanaka</s> and others. [NBs 46.14]
Those who, inwardly full of knowledge, appear in the world as though engaged in worldly affairs,

children.text: ye sthitā nijaniṣṭhāyāṃ ta eva janakādayaḥ // NBs_46.15 //
children.translated_text: who are established in their own firm state — they are indeed <s>Janaka</s> and others. [NBs 46.15]

children.text: gṛhaṃ vāstu vanaṃ vā'stu yeṣāṃ niṣṭhā na vartate /
children.translated_text: Whether in the home or in the forest — those whose firm establishment does not exist

children.text: sanakādiṣu naivaite na ca te janakādiṣu // NBs_46.16 //
children.translated_text: are neither among the <s>Sanaka</s>s nor among the <s>Janaka</s>s. [NBs 46.16]
The true teachers are indeed inwardly substantial, of few words, and givers of nectar;

children.text: mandraṃ mandraṃ hi garjanti prāvṛṣeṇyāḥ payodharāḥ // NBs_46.17 //
children.translated_text: the rainy-season clouds thunder softly, softly. [NBs 46.17]
This should always be studied and always contemplated —
these fourteen [verses] on <s>jīvanmukti</s>, for the attainment of the state of liberation while living. [NBs 46.18]
The roar of the elephant of the knower (<s>jñānī</s>).

children.text: āyānti tatra vilasanti vasanti ca draguḍḍīya yānti ca kulāni vihaṅgamānām/
children.translated_text: Flocks of birds come there, play, dwell, and suddenly flying up, depart —

children.text: bhāvāstathā mayi samā viṣamā vicitrā devālayāgramiva kevalamasmi nityaḥ // NBs_47.1 //
children.translated_text: similarly, various conditions, even and uneven, [arise] in me; I am merely like the pinnacle of a temple — eternal, alone. [NBs 47.1]

children.text: unmajjya majjati jaganmayi daivayogāduccāvacā na gaṇitā api te taraṅgāḥ /
children.translated_text: The world rises and sinks in me by the force of destiny; those waves, high and low, are uncounted;

children.text: niṣṭhāṃ gataḥ svamahimanyacalapratiṣṭhe tiṣṭhāmi sāgara iva svarasādapāraḥ // NBs_47.2 //
children.translated_text: I stand established in my own greatness, immovably founded — like the ocean, fathomless in its own nature. [NBs 47.2]

children.text: janmādayo vanacarāḥ pravahantu kāmaṃ gharṣantu kumbhamabhito mayi vṛttināgāḥ /
children.translated_text: Let the wild beasts of birth and the like roam freely; let the elephant-<s>vṛtti</s>s (mental modifications) rub against the pot [of the body] all around me;

children.text: asminyuge parayuge ca yugāntare vā tiṣṭhāmi niścalatayā girirājatulyaḥ // NBs_47.3 //
children.translated_text: in this age, in the next age, or in the interval between ages — I stand immovable, like the king of mountains. [NBs 47.3]

children.text: nīcairnipātitavimohamahīdharasya vindhyasya mūrdhani padaṃ vinidhāya samyak /
children.translated_text: Having firmly placed my foot upon the head of <s>Vindhya</s>, the mountain of delusion brought low,

children.text: iṣṭāṃ diśaṃ pratigataḥ punarāgato na svacchandameva viharāmi tadasmyagastyaḥ // NBs_47.4 //
children.translated_text: having gone to the desired direction and not returned — I roam freely; I am that <s>Agastya</s>. [NBs 47.4]

children.text: dṛṣṭo mayā'dya vigaladvadanaprasādaḥ kaścittṛtīyapadataḥ patitaḥ pṛthivyām /
children.translated_text: Today I have seen someone, his face-grace fading, fallen from the third station to the earth;

children.text: tanme matiḥ samudiyāya parāvarajñā svargastu hanta narakādapi durvipākaḥ // NBs_47.5 //
children.translated_text: thereby my understanding has arisen, knowing the higher and the lower — alas, heaven is indeed of worse consequence than hell! [NBs 47.5]

children.text: āruhya tuṅgapadavīṃ patitādanāryānnārūḍha eva hi varaṃ prakṛtau sthito yaḥ /
children.translated_text: From one who has climbed to a high station and fallen, the ignoble — better indeed is he who, never having climbed, remains in his natural state;

children.text: aṅgāni haṃta kila tasya na cūrṇitāni khedo na cetasi na vā parihāsapīḍā // NBs_47.6 //
children.translated_text: for his limbs are not crushed, there is no sorrow in his mind, nor the affliction of ridicule. [NBs 47.6]

children.text: nāḍīṃ praviśya yadi jīvati bhītabhītaḥ prānte ca khādati mṛtiścirajīvanaṃ kim /
children.translated_text: If, entering a vein [of the body], one lives on, frightened and afraid, and at the end is eaten by death — what kind of long life is that?

children.text: dehasvabhāvarahitaḥ paramātmabhāve tiṣṭhanmṛtiṃ jayati ceccirajīvanaṃ tat // NBs_47.7 //
children.translated_text: But one who, free from the nature of the body, stands in the state of the Supreme Self, conquers death — that indeed is long life. [NBs 47.7]

children.text: ālokitāni ca matāni munīśvarāṇāmālokitāśca bahavo bahusiddhamārgāḥ /
children.translated_text: The doctrines of the lords of sages have been examined; many paths established by many [masters] have been surveyed;

children.text: adyāpi taṃ malinabhāvamapāsya dūraṃ siddhistu kiṃ na yadi sidhyati nityasiddhaḥ // NBs_47.8 //
children.translated_text: even now, having cast off that impure state far away — is it not attainment if the eternally attained [Self] is realized? [NBs 47.8]

children.text: aṅgaṃ prasārya patitaḥ khalu citsvarūpe nidrālutāṃ gata iti pravinaṣṭaceṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having stretched out the limbs and fallen into the nature of consciousness, gone to drowsiness as it were, all activities ceased —

children.text: vindhyasya yojanaśatāyatikā śileva naiva hrasāmi na ca vṛddhimupaimi pūrṇaḥ // NBs_47.9 //
children.translated_text: like a rock a hundred <s>yojana</s>s long of the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain — I neither diminish nor increase; I am full. [NBs 47.9]

children.text: parilasati pitā me sarvalokasya rājā dhṛtimatibalaheturyauvanaṃ me navīnam /
children.translated_text: My father, the king of all worlds, shines forth; fortitude, intellect, and strength are [my] cause; my youth is fresh;

children.text: iyamapi ca subuddhiḥ kācidūḍhā varāṅgī sukhamadhikamataḥ kiṃ matparo nāsti dhanyaḥ // NBs_47.10 //
children.translated_text: and this excellent intelligence, like a beautiful bride, has been wed — what greater happiness? Who is more blessed than I? [NBs 47.10]
With the contemplation of the state of equanimity, possessing infinite contentment, having inwardly released the thread of craving for momentary drops of pleasure,

children.text: nijasukhanidhividyārājasiṃhāsanasthā vayamiha kalayāmaḥ kālamālambya deham // NBs_47.11 //
children.translated_text: seated on the royal throne of the knowledge of our own treasure of happiness — we pass our time here, holding onto the body. [NBs 47.11]

children.text: kati kati na hi jīvā devarājādayo'mī padapatanahatāśāḥ saṃsṛtau saṃsaranti /
children.translated_text: How many, how many beings — <s>Devarāja</s> [<s>Indra</s>] and others — with hopes dashed by falls from their stations, transmigrate in <s>saṃsāra</s>!

children.text: gurupadamavalaṃbya brahmavidyātaristhā adhigataparapārāste vayaṃ dhanyadhanyāḥ // NBs_47.12 //
children.translated_text: Having taken refuge at the feet of the <s>Guru</s>, standing in the boat of the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, having reached the further shore — we are the blessed of the blessed! [NBs 47.12]

children.text: vyoma vyomacarairna liptamapi yattatsarvadā nīrasaṃ kṣīrābdhiḥ saraso'pi vṛddhimadhikāṃ labdhvā punarmuñcati /
children.translated_text: The sky is not tainted even by sky-dwellers [birds]; though always juiceless, the milk-ocean, though full of flavor, having gained excessive growth, releases it again;

children.text: hemādrirjanako mudāmapi mudāṃ naivāśrayo nīraso na kṣīṇo na ca naiva modarahito'haṃ tattulā nāsti me // NBs_47.13 //
children.translated_text: the golden mountain, <s>Janaka</s> (progenitor) of joys, is not an abode of joys — [it is] juiceless. I am neither diminished, nor am I without delight — there is nothing comparable to me. [NBs 47.13]

children.text: sāyaṃ prātaranekaraṅgamapi tannānekaraṅgāśrayaṃ yāntyāyānti payāṃsi tatra na payorekhā'pi dṛṣṭā kvacit /
children.translated_text: Morning and evening, though many colors [arise], that [sky] is not the abode of many colors; waters come and go, yet not even a line of water is seen there;

children.text: sajñānena mayā vigāhya tadaho dṛṣṭaṃ nabho nirmalam nīlaṃ nīlamiti prathaiva nabhaso mithyā nabhonīlimā // NBs_47.14 //
children.translated_text: having dived in with knowledge, that pure sky has been seen — alas! The widespread notion 'the sky is blue, blue' is false — the blueness of the sky is false! [NBs 47.14]

children.text: rūpye rūpyamatiḥ kṛtā kṛtadhiyā raṅge punardurdhiyā satyaṃ dvāvapi saṃsthitau nijadhiyā sve niścaye niścale /
children.translated_text: On silver, the notion 'silver' was formed by a wise person; on a stage, again by a foolish one [on nacre]; truly both were established in their own conviction, unwavering;

children.text: ekasyaiva daridratā vyapagatā tasthau dvitīyastathā sañjāte krayavikrayavyayavidhau vyakto viśeṣastayoḥ // NBs_47.15 //
children.translated_text: the poverty of only one was removed; the second remained as before — when purchase, sale, and expenditure occurred, the distinction between them became manifest. [NBs 47.15]

children.text: nimnā nūnamudanvataḥ sthitiriyaṃ kallolinī cetkṛtā vikṣiptena kutaścidāgatavatā vindhyāṭavīvāyunā /
children.translated_text: The state of the ocean is indeed low; if the waves were caused by a wild <s>Vindhya</s>-forest wind that came from somewhere,

children.text: tatkiṃ nāyamapāṃ nidhiḥ kimathavā sthānādasau cālitaḥ kintu pratyuta tādṛśo'pi mahimā vikhyāpito vāridheḥ // NBs_47.16 //
children.translated_text: then what — is this not the reservoir of waters? Or has it been moved from its place? Rather, such very greatness of the ocean has been proclaimed. [NBs 47.16]

children.text: mādhuryaṃ ca payastvamāśritavatā tucche dadhitvāmlate rūpe saṃprati bibhratā tu payasā sarvaṃ yaśo hāritam /
children.translated_text: The sweetness and the milk — when one who has taken to curd assumes sourness of form, then by that milk all reputation is destroyed;

children.text: graiveyatvamathāṅgadatvamatha ca kṣudratvamakṣudratāṃ paryāyairbhajataḥ svabhāmajahato hemnastu nāsti kṣatiḥ // NBs_47.17 //
children.translated_text: but for gold, which assumes by turns the form of necklace, armlet, and then smallness or greatness — without abandoning its own nature — there is no loss. [NBs 47.17]

children.text: na hi na hi caturāste yairna buddhaṃ viśuddhaṃ na hi na hi kṛtinaste ye na pāraṃ prayātāḥ /
children.translated_text: They are indeed not clever who have not known the pure awakened [state]; they are indeed not accomplished who have not gone to the further shore;

children.text: na hi na hi tu kulīnā yairna tattvaṃ viviktaṃ na hi na hi munayaste yairdhṛtā lobhavārtā // NBs_47.18 //
children.translated_text: they are indeed not of noble lineage who have not discriminated the truth; they are indeed not sages who have held on to the news of greed. [NBs 47.18]

children.text: he'haṃkṛte tava na kṛtyamihāsti kiñcillīnā bhava svamahimanyacalapratiṣṭhe /
children.translated_text: O ego! You have nothing to do here; be dissolved in your own greatness, immovably established;

children.text: cetastvamehi paramaṃ svasukhābdhimantaḥ soḍhuṃ na śaknuma imāstava duṣṭavṛttīḥ // NBs_47.19 //
children.translated_text: O mind, enter within the ocean of your own bliss — we cannot endure these wicked tendencies of yours! [NBs 47.19]

children.text: āyānti naiva suta tatra manovikārā āyānti cediha vicāraya joṣamāsyam /
children.translated_text: Mental modifications do not arise there, O son; but if they do arise, examine [them] here — sit in silence;

children.text: tvaṃ cāpi mandamiha sañcara muñca mohaṃ so'hampade sukhanidhau yadi te manīṣā // NBs_47.20 //
children.translated_text: you too, move gently here; abandon delusion — if your aspiration is for the treasure of bliss in the 'I am That' (<s>so'ham</s>) state. [NBs 47.20]

children.text: tīvraṃ tamaḥ samaya eṣa niśīthanāmā deśo'pi caurabahulaḥ śithilā ca bhittiḥ /
children.translated_text: The darkness is intense; this time is called midnight; the place is full of thieves; the wall is weak;

children.text: itthaṃ sthite nijadhanaṃ prati sāvadhāno jāgartti cedgṛhapatirviphalā hi caurāḥ // NBs_47.21 //
children.translated_text: when things stand thus, if the householder remains vigilant regarding his own wealth, then the thieves are thwarted indeed. [NBs 47.21]
By kings wielding sharp weapons, nobly, a hunt should be undertaken to pacify the wicked beast;

children.text: duṣṭo mṛgo na nihato nihatāstadanye vyarthasya tatkṣitipatervada kaḥ prabhāvaḥ // NBs_47.22 //
children.translated_text: if the wicked beast is not killed but others are killed instead — tell, what is the prowess of that futile king? [NBs 47.22]

children.text: iṣṭe naṣṭe naśvare tyaktabhogaḥ sañjātālaṃpratyayo vītarāgaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the desired is lost, in the perishable, having abandoned enjoyment, having attained the conviction 'enough,' free from attachment,

children.text: tāṃ tāṃ kakṣāṃ svairamabhyeti sūkṣmāṃ yāṃ yāmante sādhakāḥ sādhayanti // NBs_47.23 //
children.translated_text: he freely reaches those subtle stages, one by one, that practitioners achieve in the end. [NBs 47.23]

children.text: hṛdi yadi savicārāstarhi samyakpracārā gatimanugatibhājaḥ kevalaṃ duḥkhabhājaḥ /
children.translated_text: If reflections exist in the heart, then [let there be] right conduct; those who merely follow the course without [true] discrimination are recipients of suffering alone;

children.text: parikalaya yadandhairnīyamānā ivāndhā yugapadapi sametā andhakūpe patanti // NBs_47.24 //
children.translated_text: consider: just as when the blind are led by the blind, all together they fall into the blind well. [NBs 47.24]

children.text: ekaḥ prāha paṭheti māṃ taditaraḥ prāhāṭa dūrāṭavīmanyaḥ prāha samedhayāgnimaparaḥ prāhārkamālokaya /
children.translated_text: One says 'read me'; another says 'go to the distant forest'; yet another says 'kindle the fire'; another says 'gaze at the sun';

children.text: sviṣṭepsuṃ prati māṃ vaco gurujanairuktaṃ tvamevāsi tatsviṣṭāptermama ghūrṇite'pi nayane andhā na paśyantyamī // NBs_47.25 //
children.translated_text: to me who desires the well-offered [oblation], the word spoken by the elders is: 'You yourself are That' — even when my eyes are dazzled by the attainment of that well-offered [goal], these blind ones do not see. [NBs 47.25]

children.text: yeṣāṃ vajradṛḍhaṃ kapolamathavā jihvā vitastyāyatā khyāttyarthaṃ kalahāya pustakapiśācānāṃ kathā tiṣṭhatu /
children.translated_text: Those whose cheeks are hard as diamond, or whose tongues are a span long — let the talk of those book-demons, [arguing] for fame and quarrel, be set aside.

children.text: māṃ pṛcchācchamate kathaṃ vilasati dhyānaṃ kathaṃ dhāraṇā ko bhāvaḥ svarasena kena vidhinā cetaḥ pare līyate // NBs_47.26 //
children.translated_text: Ask me: How does tranquility shine forth? How does meditation [arise]? How does concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>) [function]? What is the [inner] disposition? By what inclination and by what method does the mind dissolve into the Supreme? [NBs 47.26]

children.text: jihve devi gṛhāṇa maunamadhunā bhūyastvayā jalpitaṃ pratyagvastuni niṣṭhitā yadi matistatkiṃ pralāpāstava /
children.translated_text: O tongue, O goddess! Adopt silence now — enough of your prattling! If the mind is established in the inner reality, then what use are your babbles?

children.text: svacchandoparamāmṛtābdhilaharīlāvaṇyalagne hṛdi prāyaḥ karkaśatāṃ gatā'si kuṭile tasmānna me rocase // NBs_47.27 //
children.translated_text: O crooked one, your heart is attached to the beauty of the waves of the nectar-ocean of spontaneous cessation — yet you have mostly become harsh. Therefore you do not please me. [NBs 47.27]

children.text: sampūrṇaṃ jagadeva nandanavanaṃ sarve'pi kalpadrumā gāṅgaṃ vāri samastavārinicayāḥ puṇyāḥ samastāḥ kriyāḥ /
children.translated_text: The entire world is itself the pleasure-garden (<s>Nandanavana</s>); all [trees] are wish-fulfilling trees (<s>kalpadrumaḥ</s>); all collections of water are the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>; all actions are meritorious;

children.text: vācaḥ prākṛtasaṃskṛtāḥ śrutigiro vārāṇasī medinī sarvaiva sthitirasya muktipadavī dṛṣṭe pare brahmaṇi // NBs_47.28 //
children.translated_text: all words — whether <s>Prākṛta</s> or <s>Saṃskṛta</s> — are the words of the <s>Vedas</s>; the entire earth is <s>Vārāṇasī</s>; every condition is itself the path to liberation — when the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> is seen. [NBs 47.28]

children.text: otaṃ protamidaṃ vicitramakhilaṃ yasmiñjagadvarttate yatrodeti vilīyate punaridaṃ toye taraṅgādivat /
children.translated_text: That in which this entire variegated universe is woven warp and weft, where it arises and dissolves again,

children.text: tacceto mayi līyate pratidinaṃ mayyeva tajjāyate mahyaṃ tarhi vadantu he layavidaḥ so'haṃ tu līye kva nu // NBs_47.29 //
children.translated_text: like waves in water — that [Supreme] dissolves into me every day, and from me alone it is born. Tell me then, O you who know dissolution — where do I dissolve? [NBs 47.29]

children.text: bālā śvaśrūjananiyamitā dehalīdattadṛṣṭirdīrghaṃ cakṣuḥ kirati vadane yauvanālaṃkṛtasya /
children.translated_text: A young bride, restrained by her mother-in-law, fixing her gaze at the threshold, casts long glances at the face of a youth adorned with his prime;

children.text: yuktasyaivaṃ na calati tato bhrūtaṭe dattadṛṣṭeścetovṛttiḥ sphurati puruṣe mokṣalakṣmīnivāse // NBs_47.30 //
children.translated_text: even so, for one who is [thus] engaged, the activity of the mind does not waver — with gaze fixed at the eyebrow-ridge, [the mind's] activity shines forth in the <s>Puruṣa</s> who is the abode of the wealth of liberation. [NBs 47.30]

children.text: paryantai rahitasya yasya mahatī gambhīratā tādṛśī magnā yatra vibhānti no agaṇitā brahmāṇḍamṛtpiṇḍikāḥ /
children.translated_text: That which has no limits, whose greatness is such, and whose depth is so profound — in which innumerable cosmic eggs (<s>brahmāṇḍas</s>) appear as mere lumps of clay, sunken [within it];

children.text: yādṛktasya cidarṇavasya suraso yādṛksvarūpaṃ mahattatkasmai kathayāmi kasya viṣayaḥ ko vā'sya vaktā bhavet // NBs_47.31 //
children.translated_text: such is the delightful flavor of that ocean of consciousness, such is its great essential nature — to whom shall I describe it? Whose object [of knowledge] is it? Who could be its speaker? [NBs 47.31]

children.text: ākhyāsyāmi ramāvarasya purato gaurīvarasyāthavā śabdabrahmamayīvarasya puratastvaasya kasyāpi na /
children.translated_text: Shall I tell it before the Lord of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), or before the Lord of <s>Gaurī</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), or before the Lord whose form is <s>Śabdabrahman</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>)? Not before any of these.

children.text: prahlādapravaṇaṃ prakāśaparamaṃ saṃveditaṃ saṃvidā śānte cetasi yatkutūhalamaye nirjihmamujjṛmbhitam // NBs_47.32 //
children.translated_text: That which is full of bliss, supremely luminous, experienced by pure awareness, that which has blossomed forth straightforwardly in the tranquil mind filled with wonder — [that I cannot speak]. [NBs 47.32]

children.text: tṛṣṇābhirgalitaṃ kṣamābhiruditaṃ prajñābhirunmīlitaṃ mohairastamitaṃ bhramaiḥ pracalitaṃ dvaṃdvaiśca dūraṃ gatam /
children.translated_text: Drained away by cravings, risen through patience, opened by insights, set by delusions, shaken by confusions, gone far by dualities,

children.text: bodhairullasitaṃ sukhairvilasitaṃ saṃmīlitaṃ saṃśayaiḥ svaṃ dhāma sphuritaṃ yadaiva muninā nirmāyamālokitam // NBs_47.33 //
children.translated_text: illuminated by awakenings, made radiant by joys, closed by doubts — one's own abode has shone forth when the sage has gazed upon it free from illusion. [NBs 47.33]

children.text: pūrvaṃ nāma kimantaraṃ samabhavadyannedamālokitaṃ kiṃ vā kāraṇamasti jātamadhunā yenedamālokyate /
children.translated_text: What was there before, when this [reality] was not seen? Or what cause has now arisen by which this is seen?

children.text: itthaṃ vismayavanmano hi viduṣāṃ vijñānanidrāghane tatrānandavane munīndrasadane līnaṃ parabrahmaṇi // NBs_47.34 //
children.translated_text: Thus the mind of the wise, filled with wonder, in the dense sleep of knowledge, in that forest of bliss, in the abode of the supreme sage, is absorbed in the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>. [NBs 47.34]

children.text: śuddhe bodhe sphurati paritaḥ kṣālitā vāsanāṅkāḥ kṣīṇaṃ cittaṃ viratiruditā karmapāśā viśīrṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: In pure awareness, the stains of latent impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>) are washed away all around; the mind is destroyed; cessation has arisen; the bonds of <s>karma</s> are shattered;

children.text: bhagno bhedaḥ sukhamadhigataṃ kalpanā dūramuktā dṛṣṭe tattve karabadaravannāsti karttavyaśeṣaḥ // NBs_47.35 //
children.translated_text: difference is broken; bliss is attained; conceptual construction is cast far away — when reality is seen, like a fruit in the palm of the hand, nothing remains to be done. [NBs 47.35]
The <s>Narahari Ṣaṭkam</s> (Six Verses on <s>Narahari</s>)

children.text: nāmnaiva no naraharerhi vidīryate'sau duṣṭo hiraṇyakaśipurnitarāṃ baliṣṭhaḥ /
children.translated_text: That mighty and most terrible <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> is not torn apart by the mere name of <s>Narahari</s>;

children.text: tasmāttvayā nṛharirūpadhareṇa citta moho hiraṇyakaśipustu vidāraṇīyaḥ // NBs_48.1 //
children.translated_text: therefore, O mind, by you — who have assumed the form of <s>Nṛhari</s> (the Man-Lion) — the <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> of delusion must be torn asunder! [NBs 48.1]

children.text: indrasya rājyamapi sampratilabhya lubdhastṛṣṇāmayo nijaripurna jagāma tṛptim /
children.translated_text: Even upon obtaining the kingdom of <s>Indra</s>, that greedy one full of craving, his own enemy, did not attain satisfaction;

children.text: asyādhunā pralaya eva hitaṃ mameti prajñātmanā nṛhariṇā pralayaṃ praṇītaḥ // NBs_48.2 //
children.translated_text: 'Now, his destruction alone is beneficial for me' — thinking thus, the wisdom-souled <s>Nṛhari</s> brought about his destruction. [NBs 48.2]

children.text: vakṣo hiraṇyakaśipoḥ kila vajrasāraṃ śastrāṇi tatra sakalānyapi kuṇṭhitāni /
children.translated_text: The chest of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> was indeed hard as adamant; all weapons were blunted against it;

children.text: tādṛkpunastava nakhairnṛhare vidīrṇamatyadbhuto bhavata eṣa nakhaprabhāvaḥ // NBs_48.3 //
children.translated_text: yet, O <s>Nṛhari</s>, that very [chest] was torn apart by your nails — exceedingly wondrous is this power of your nails! [NBs 48.3]
The inner vision — the heart, [the enemy] stationed at the tip of the heart — <s>Nṛhari</s>, radiant with light, leading that enemy of darkness to its end;

children.text: kaṣṭaṃ samastamapi naṣṭadaśāṃ prayātaṃ prahlāda eva paramaṃ mahimānamāpa // NBs_48.4 //
children.translated_text: alas, all else has gone to a state of destruction — <s>Prahlāda</s> alone has attained the supreme greatness. [NBs 48.4]

children.text: nāntastu nāpi ca bahirna divā na rātrau nārdreṇa śuṣkavapuṣā ca na māryate yaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who cannot be killed — neither inside nor outside, neither by day nor by night, neither by something moist nor by a dry body;

children.text: nāyaṃ nareṇa na mṛgeṇa nipātanīyastādṛgripuṃ naraharirhatavānvicitram // NBs_48.5 //
children.translated_text: he who is not to be slain by man or by beast — such an enemy was slain by <s>Narahari</s>. Wondrous! [NBs 48.5]

children.text: sarvatraiva sadā sthito narahariryatsthāvare jaṅgame daivādvyaktimupāgataḥ punarasau pāṣāṇapiṇḍe'pi yat /
children.translated_text: Since <s>Narahari</s> is always present everywhere — in the immovable and the movable — and since, by divine providence, he became manifest even in a pillar of stone,

children.text: nāstitvaṃ gamito hiraṇyakaśipustādṛkprapañcāśrayaḥ tatsarvaṃ kila kautukaṃ nijajanaprahlādahetoḥ kṛtam // NBs_48.6 //
