children.translated_text: and since <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, the very support of the phenomenal world, was brought to non-existence — all this marvel was done for the sake of his own devotee <s>Prahlāda</s>. [NBs 48.6]
Having conquered the six enemies of the senses, if one sings in the heart this set of six [verses on <s>Narahari</s>],
this <s>Narahari Ṣaṭkam</s> wards off the six modifications [of existence]. [NBs 48.7]
<s>Unmattapralāpaśatakam</s> (The Hundred Ravings of a Madman)
Savoring the nectar of pure awakening, I rave like a madman;
let the intellects of the good ones extract the hidden meaning of these ravings. [NBs 49.1]
Desire (<s>kāma</s>), anger (<s>krodha</s>), greed (<s>lobha</s>), delusion (<s>moha</s>), pride (<s>mada</s>), and envy (<s>matsara</s>) —
how these are the [guiding] stars for crossing <s>saṃsāra</s>, hear now that explanation. [NBs 49.2]
Those who are lustful for the charm of union with the beautiful lady of inner repose,
who are clever in the play of solitude — such 'lustful ones' are on the path to liberation. [NBs 49.3]
That anger (<s>krodha</s>) by whose force the <s>yogin</s>, who is himself <s>Narahari</s>, tore open

children.text: vakṣo vidārayāñcakre sa krodho muktisādhanam // NBs_49.4 //
children.translated_text: the chest of the demon of delusion (<s>moha</s>) — that anger is the means to liberation. [NBs 49.4]
He whose frown-knit face is unbearable to look upon by desire, greed, and the other [afflictions] —

children.text: kāmalobhādayo bhāvāḥ sa dveṣī keśavapriyaḥ // NBs_49.5 //
children.translated_text: that 'hater' is dear to <s>Keśava</s>. [NBs 49.5]
Those who have attachment (<s>rāga</s>) to the eternal and aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>) to the perishable —

children.text: rāgadveṣavatāṃ tāta muktiḥ karatale sthitā // NBs_49.6 //
children.translated_text: for those who have [such] passion and hatred, O dear one, liberation rests in the palm of the hand. [NBs 49.6]
The sage who, by giving away the glass gem of the mind, buys the wish-fulfilling gem (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>) of knowledge —

children.text: krīṇāti yena lobhena sa lobho muktisādhanam // NBs_49.7 //
children.translated_text: the greed (<s>lobha</s>) by which [he does this] — that greed is the means to liberation. [NBs 49.7]
That [enchantment] by which, their hearts [filled] with love, [people] forget the duties of <s>varṇa</s> (class) and <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life), the body, enjoyments, wealth, and the like —

children.text: vismaranti citaḥ premṇā sa mohaḥ paramaṃ padam // NBs_49.8 //
children.translated_text: that delusion (<s>moha</s>) is the supreme state. [NBs 49.8]
'There is nothing higher than me; I alone am the Great Lord;
I alone am the highest' — such pride (<s>mada</s>) is considered to be the granter of liberation. [NBs 49.8*]
He who, by the force of the excellence of knowledge, cannot tolerate the excellence of the visible [world] —

children.text: sa tu samvatsaraśataṃ jyeṣṭho nirmatsarānmuneḥ // NBs_49.9 //
children.translated_text: that [envious one] is, for a hundred years, senior to the sage who is free from envy. [NBs 49.9]
He who does not tolerate for a moment any external manifestation, who is 'impatient' —
the virtues of the 'patient' ones are tied to the big toe of his left foot. [NBs 49.10]
Desire and the other [afflictions] are great scoundrels, by whom the three worlds have been swindled;

children.text: tāndhūrttayati yo yuktyā sa dhūrto dhūrjaṭipriyaḥ // NBs_49.11 //
children.translated_text: he who cleverly swindles them — that 'scoundrel' is dear to <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (<s>Śiva</s>). [NBs 49.11]
He who outwardly pampers greed and the rest, while inwardly cutting their roots —
appearing as one thing on the outside, being another within — that 'hypocrite' attains liberation. [NBs 49.12]
He who, in all things that [appear] virtuous, always whispers to the inner self about [their] fault —

children.text: karṇe japati yo nityaṃ piśuno'sau vimuktibhāk // NBs_49.13 //
children.translated_text: that 'slanderer' is the one who partakes of liberation. [NBs 49.13]
He in whose heart there is always the censure of the 'other' [i.e., of all that is non-self] —

children.text: parāṃ gatiṃ gato dṛṣṭaḥ sa mayā muniśekharaḥ // NBs_49.14 //
children.translated_text: I have seen that 'defamer' — that crest-jewel among sages — to have reached the supreme goal. [NBs 49.14]
For those whose minds are convinced that 'all this world is indeed false' —

children.text: sa mithyāvādināṃ loko durlabhaḥ satyavādinaḥ // NBs_49.15 //
children.translated_text: the world of those 'speakers of falsehood' is difficult to attain even for 'speakers of truth.' [NBs 49.15]
He who [says] 'I do nothing whatsoever' — who is devoid of [conventional] good conduct —

children.text: ācāriṇo na gacchanti tasyānācāriṇo gatim // NBs_49.16 //
children.translated_text: the practitioners of [conventional] good conduct cannot reach the destination of that 'one of bad conduct.' [NBs 49.16]

children.text: pūrvaṃ yāni ca mitrāṇi vicārādīni tānyapi /
children.translated_text: Having abandoned even those former friends — deliberation and the like —

children.text: vihāya tatparaṃ yāto mitradrohī sa mucyate // NBs_49.17 //
children.translated_text: he who has gone beyond to that [Supreme] — that 'betrayer of friends' is liberated. [NBs 49.17]
He who, by <s>māyā</s> (illusion), created the universe consisting of the five elements —

children.text: sa eva hi mayā dṛṣṭo māyāvī muktibhājanam // NBs_49.18 //
children.translated_text: that very 'sorcerer' I have seen to be the vessel of liberation. [NBs 49.18]

children.text: svecchayaiva kṛtaṃ viśvaṃ svecchayaiva nihanti yaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who by his own will created the universe and by his own will destroys it —
that 'ingrate' — more worshippable than the grateful — attains <s>mokṣa</s>. [NBs 49.19]
Wonderful! He who regards the <s>jīva</s> itself as the <s>Ātman</s>, as <s>Īśvara</s> —
that 'arrogant one' reaches the destination that is unattainable for those without ego. [NBs 49.20]
Seeing faults in [all apparent] virtues, censuring the world entirely,
those who are devoted to self-praise — they go always to the abode of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>. [NBs 49.21]
Even after knowing the pure <s>Ātman</s>, he acts like a worldly person [saying:] 'I do not act' —
that 'hypocrite' (<s>dambhakṛt</s>) is dear to <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>). [NBs 49.22]
With the sharp sword of awakening, he who slays those of evil mind [characterized by] delusion and egoism —
that 'killer' destroys sin accumulated over hundreds of previous births. [NBs 49.23]
'I am <s>Hari</s> who has [absorbed] egoism; I am <s>Brahman</s> itself; I am <s>Śiva</s>' —

children.text: iti viśvāsya hantāraḥ puṇyā viśvastaghātakāḥ // NBs_49.24 //
children.translated_text: those who thus slay [the egoism of] the universe — those meritorious 'slayers of the trusting' [are truly holy]. [NBs 49.24]
Liberated from injunctions and prohibitions, carefree, wandering by his own will —
he who is excluded from the row of ritualists — he is the purifier of our row. [NBs 49.25]

children.text: ninditāvabhinirmuktābhyuditau yau tu tau hi naḥ /
children.translated_text: Those two — the 'condemned' and the 'liberated one who has risen' — they alone are pure for us;
the one free from [conventional] <s>karma</s> and the one who has risen [above it] — they are always [truly] pure. [NBs 49.26]
The sage who, having bolted the door, like [one eating] broken sweetmeats,

children.text: ekākī miṣṭamaśnāti sa yāti paramāṃ gatim // NBs_49.27 //
children.translated_text: eats the delicious [bliss] all alone — he reaches the supreme goal. [NBs 49.27]
He who confined the groups of the knowledge-senses and action-senses in his own dwelling,

children.text: paṅktīkṛtya hato yena so'smākaṃ paṅktipāvanaḥ // NBs_49.28 //
children.translated_text: lined them up, and slew them — he is the purifier of our row. [NBs 49.28]
Behold — those who endure the destruction of the self for the sake of the destruction of <s>saṃsāra</s>;

children.text: saṃsāradveṣiṇāṃ teṣāṃ muktiḥ śāstreṣu varṇitā // NBs_49.29 //
children.translated_text: the liberation of those haters of <s>saṃsāra</s> is proclaimed in the scriptures. [NBs 49.29]
'I' and 'mine' — all of this was gambled away in the dice-game of awakening;
he by whom [this was done] is declared to be a partaker of liberation in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Śruti</s>. [NBs 49.30]
He who has no compassion for the wretched deer of the senses —
he alone is exceedingly dear to <s>Devakī's</s> son, the friend of the afflicted. [NBs 49.31]
The king who, devoted to the enjoyment of the self (<s>ātmabhoga</s>), does not look after [his] city —

children.text: lipyate na sa pāpena pramāṇaṃ muṇḍakaśrutiḥ // NBs_49.32 //
children.translated_text: he is not tainted by sin; the authority is the <s>Muṇḍaka Śruti</s>. [NBs 49.32]
He by whom the wealth-bearing mind was slain with the noose of knowledge and dispassion —

children.text: yaḥ syādevaṃvidhaḥ pāśī tasya kāśī pade pade // NBs_49.33 //
children.translated_text: for one who is such a 'noose-bearer' (<s>pāśin</s>), <s>Kāśī</s> (the abode of liberation) is at every step. [NBs 49.33]
Between the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the <s>Yamunā</s> (the two nostrils), the young ascetic widow (<s>bālaraṇḍā</s>) [= the <s>kuṇḍalinī</s>],

children.text: balātkāreṇa yo bhuṅkte sa raṇḍāvyasanī śuciḥ // NBs_49.34 //
children.translated_text: he who forcefully enjoys her — that 'violator of widows' is [truly] pure. [NBs 49.34]
He by whom the dense forest of duality was burned by the wildfire of awakening —

children.text: atipuṇyāṃ gatiṃ yāti sa hi dāvāgnidāyakaḥ // NBs_49.35 //
children.translated_text: he, the 'arsonist,' attains a supremely meritorious destination. [NBs 49.35]

children.text: gṛhe sthitānāmapi yo gavāṃ grāsaṃ dadāti na /
children.translated_text: He who does not give grass even to cows staying at home [i.e., the senses dwelling in the body],
but cultivates the nourishment of the self alone — he is freed from all sins. [NBs 49.36]
By one who does not know <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, all essences (<s>rasas</s>) have been sold;

children.text: granthau baddhaṃ bodhadhanaṃ sa dhanyo rasavikrayī // NBs_49.37 //
children.translated_text: the wealth of awakening has been tied up in a book — that wealthy 'seller of essences' [is blessed]. [NBs 49.37]
He by whom, through the inner ruler (<s>antaryāmin</s>) as the self, the mixing of classes (<s>varṇasaṅkara</s>) was produced —

children.text: svayaṃ śaṅkara evāsau varṇito varṇasaṅkarī // NBs_49.38 //
children.translated_text: he himself is <s>Śaṅkara</s> — that 'producer of class-mixing' is celebrated. [NBs 49.38]
He who, having studied the <s>Vedas</s>, and having understood their meaning by his own reflection,

children.text: plāvitāḥ saha vedāntairvedaplāvī sa mucyate // NBs_49.39 //
children.translated_text: set them afloat along with the <s>Vedānta</s> — that 'flooder of the <s>Vedas</s>' is liberated. [NBs 49.39]
Everything has been offered to <s>Śiva</s> and has become the remnant of <s>Śiva's</s> offering (<s>nirmālya</s>);
the one of pure soul who eats that — he is the 'eater of <s>Śiva's</s> remnants.' [NBs 49.40]
He who, having taken the vow of <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), enjoys all the leading ladies of the city [i.e., the sense-objects transmuted by knowledge] —

children.text: lipyate na sa pāpena citraṃ vedāntadarśanam // NBs_49.41 //
children.translated_text: he is not stained by sin; wondrous is the vision of <s>Vedānta</s>! [NBs 49.41]
Of <s>yogins</s>, <s>avadhūtas</s>, <s>Śuka</s> and the like — from their mouths, what has fallen,
having tasted even a little of that 'leftover' — the 'eater of leftovers' is liberated. [NBs 49.42]
He alone who knows <s>Brahman</s> — of that <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, by his own understanding,

children.text: vṛttilopaḥ kṛto yena sa dhanyo vṛttilopakṛt // NBs_49.43 //
children.translated_text: he by whom livelihood was cut off — that blessed 'destroyer of livelihood' [is liberated]. [NBs 49.43]
The sage who eats food obtained by chance — [even if] cooked with eggplant or <s>kalañja</s> (garlic) and the like —
<s>Hari</s> is very near to him. [NBs 49.44]
The knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> taught by <s>Varuṇa</s> to <s>Bhṛgu</s> is the <s>Vāruṇī</s> (liquor of Varuṇa);
for those intoxicated by tasting the essence of that <s>Vāruṇī</s>, the supreme state is the highest goal. [NBs 49.45]

children.text: parāgvṛttiṃ parityajya yā pratyaksā tu vāruṇī /
children.translated_text: Abandoning outward-directed mental activity, the inner-directed <s>Vāruṇī</s> —

children.text: tadabhyāsaratānāṃ ca na dūre paramaṃ padam // NBs_49.46 //
children.translated_text: for those devoted to its practice, the supreme state is not far. [NBs 49.46]
Those whose mind has stumbled upon seeing the beautiful beloved of consciousness, the inner ruler, the sense-organ [itself as] the lord of the senses —

children.text: mānasaṃ skhalitaṃ yeṣāṃ te muktā ajitendriyāḥ // NBs_49.47 //
children.translated_text: they are liberated, though of unmastered senses. [NBs 49.47]
Having ascended the ground of <s>yoga</s>, [and then] falling into the deep ocean of <s>Brahman</s>,
afterwards, absorbed — the one who ascended and fell is pure. [NBs 49.48]
I have bathed in the river named 'Destruction of <s>Karma</s>,' which is the consciousness-knowledge;
from the touch of the waters of the destruction of <s>karma</s>, the bondage of <s>karma</s> ceases. [NBs 49.49]
In <s>Aṅga</s>, <s>Vaṅga</s>, <s>Kaliṅga</s>, in <s>Saurāṣṭra</s> and <s>Magadha</s> —
I am complete everywhere, free from all conditioning (<s>saṃskāra</s>). [NBs 49.50]
He who abandons his own house and delights in the supreme temple —

children.text: sa gṛhastho gatiṃ gacchetparāmiti vidāṃ matam // NBs_49.51 //
children.translated_text: that householder attains the supreme goal — this is the view of the wise. [NBs 49.51]
He by whom merit has been abandoned out of greed for the self's bliss —

children.text: sa eva sukṛtī śeṣaḥ sukṛtyapi hi duṣkṛtī // NBs_49.52 //
children.translated_text: he alone is truly meritorious; the rest, though meritorious, are actually sinful. [NBs 49.52]
Ignorance is itself true knowledge; non-discrimination is discrimination;

children.text: sarvātmakatvaṃ kaivalyaṃ yeṣāṃ te siddhasattamāḥ // NBs_49.53 //
children.translated_text: the being-all-things is liberation (<s>kaivalya</s>) — for those [who realize this], they are the best among the perfected ones. [NBs 49.53]
Those who, through heedlessness of knowledge, destroy that mind —
their liberation, accomplished in reverse, is declared by <s>Śaṅkara</s>. [NBs 49.54]
I have proclaimed my own <s>dharmas</s> in the form of reciting <s>Vedānta</s>;
through the proclamation of one's own <s>dharma</s> alone, the state of union (<s>sāyujya</s>) has been attained. [NBs 49.55]
The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who has two wives should abandon the first devoted wife

children.text: parasyā guṇalobhena sa yāti paramāṃ gatim // NBs_49.56 //
children.translated_text: out of desire for the qualities of the other — he goes to the supreme state. [NBs 49.56]
Commentary on this:
Engagement (<s>pravṛtti</s>) and withdrawal (<s>nivṛtti</s>) are the two wives taught by the <s>Veda</s>;
the first is devoted to action (<s>karmaniṣṭhā</s>); the second is devoted to <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmaniṣṭhā</s>). [NBs 49.57]
'Harsh' (<s>karkaśā</s>) and 'Tasteful' (<s>rasikā</s>) are their respective other names;
the 'harsh' one belongs to the <s>karmakāṇḍa</s> (ritual portion); the 'tasteful' one speaks of <s>Brahman</s>. [NBs 49.58]

children.text: karkaśā rasikā ceti yadyapi dve pativrate /
children.translated_text: Though both the 'harsh' and the 'tasteful' are devoted wives,

children.text: rasikā svapatiṃ bhuṅkte karkaśā kaṣṭabhāginī // NBs_49.59 //
children.translated_text: the 'tasteful' one enjoys her husband, while the 'harsh' one is the one who bears hardship. [NBs 49.59]
The one devoted to action is like a maid, always engaged in household duties;
the one devoted to knowledge is a great queen, seated on the royal throne. [NBs 49.60]
For the sake of the husband, day and night, let her do the housework;

children.text: patiṃ nāliṅgya nidrāti kathaṃ saubhāgyabhāginī // NBs_49.61 //
children.translated_text: [but] she who does not embrace her husband before sleeping — how can she be a fortunate wife? [NBs 49.61]
The 'harsh' one, the speaker of action, does not know the way of essence (<s>rasa</s>);

children.text: pativratā svabhāvena bharttāraṃ stauti kevalam // NBs_49.62 //
children.translated_text: devoted by nature, she merely praises her husband. [NBs 49.62]
But the 'tasteful' one, devoted to knowledge, with the marks of refined culture,
delights her husband and plays while embracing him. [NBs 49.63]

children.text: āsane śayane yāne bhojane sā tadanvitā /
children.translated_text: In sitting, in sleeping, in traveling, in eating, she accompanies him;

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ na tiṣṭhati svāmī tāṃ vinā rasalālasaḥ // NBs_49.64 //
children.translated_text: the lord, desirous of essence, does not remain even a moment without her. [NBs 49.64]
He who knows by skill the great difference between these two —

children.text: sa kathaṃ tatra mūḍhāyāṃ rameta kimu tatsukham // NBs_49.65 //
children.translated_text: how would he delight in that dull one? And what happiness is that? [NBs 49.65]
But whoever is a great fool, a lowly one, following the ways of animals,

children.text: karkaśāyāṃ ramate rasikāṃ ca na vindati // NBs_49.66 //
children.translated_text: delights in the 'harsh' one and does not find the 'tasteful' one. [NBs 49.66]
He obtains suffering from her, quarrels daily,

children.text: bhūyastāmeva bhajate daurbhāgyaṃ tasya tādṛśam // NBs_49.67 //
children.translated_text: yet worships her again and again — such is his ill-fortune. [NBs 49.67]
In this scriptural allegory of the two wives, the subject is thus established:

children.text: nivṛttivanitāṃ tyaktvā pravṛtto narakaṃ vrajet // NBs_49.68 //
children.translated_text: abandoning the woman of withdrawal (<s>nivṛtti</s>) and taking up engagement (<s>pravṛtti</s>), one goes to hell. [NBs 49.68]
Abandoning the woman of engagement (<s>pravṛtti</s>) and taking up withdrawal (<s>nivṛtti</s>), one attains liberation;
though this scriptural meaning is difficult, the authority is from the words of <s>Vyāsa</s>. [NBs 49.69]

body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the commentary on the scripture of engagement and withdrawal.

children.translated_text: Now another [verse]:
If 'The one <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the great element' spoken by <s>Vyāsa</s> should be grasped,

children.text: tanmahābhūtasañcāre na dūre paramaṃ padam // NBs_49.70 //
children.translated_text: then in the movement of that great element, the supreme state is not far. [NBs 49.70]
This <s>mantra</s> of the <s>Ḍākinī-siddhi</s>, consisting of the syllables 'I am <s>Brahman</s>',
by mere contemplation of which, one immediately attains identity with that. [NBs 49.71]
Through the grace of the <s>guru</s> and the scripture, having attained the supreme state,

children.text: mamaivedaṃ mayā prāptamiti prāha sa uttamaḥ // NBs_49.72 //
children.translated_text: he, the best, says: 'This is mine indeed; I have attained it by myself.' [NBs 49.72]
Yet that which has not been truly attained even by the knowledges

children.text: na kiñcidapi samprāptaṃ tasya prāptirmahīyasī // NBs_49.73 //
children.translated_text: accumulated over hundreds of births — the attainment of that is the greatest. [NBs 49.73]
The nearness of the remote, the vastness of the minute,

children.text: parasya nijarūpatvaṃ yatpratyeti pramā hi sā // NBs_49.74 //
children.translated_text: the own-nature-ness of the other — the cognition that ascertains this is indeed valid knowledge (<s>pramā</s>). [NBs 49.74]

children.text: yaddṛśyate tattu mithyā tatsatyaṃ yanna dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: What is seen is unreal; what is not seen is real —
this indeed is the authoritative view of the great <s>Upaniṣads</s>. [NBs 49.75]

children.text: vicitrā yasya racanā samastā bhāti nīrasā /
children.translated_text: He whose entire, variegated creation appears tasteless —
he, like one who is living-dead, is praised in the <s>Śruti</s> as a <s>jīvanmukta</s> (one liberated while living). [NBs 49.76]
Just as a lamp in an empty room illuminates by itself —

children.text: tasya vyarthaprakāśasya sārthakaṃ janma varṇitam // NBs_49.77 //
children.translated_text: the birth of that one whose illumination [appears] purposeless [to the world] is described as meaningful. [NBs 49.77]
He who does not perceive even the slightest difference between entities and the Self —
this lamp of non-knowledge is our lamp of knowledge. [NBs 49.78]
I am awake in the night; I sleep through the entire day;

children.text: na ca rogā prabādhante mā jarāmaraṇādayaḥ // NBs_49.79 //
children.translated_text: diseases do not afflict me, nor do old age, death, and the rest. [NBs 49.79]
The discrimination of high, low, and middle is the fruit of intellects;
for him who is devoid of these, the state of king among the learned was proclaimed by <s>Hari</s>. [NBs 49.80]
He by whom both merit and demerit have been abandoned through mere dullness —

children.text: buddhiyuktaḥ sa eveti pārthaṃ prāha janārdanaḥ // NBs_49.81 //
children.translated_text: 'He alone is endowed with wisdom' — so <s>Janārdana</s> told <s>Arjuna</s> (<s>Pārtha</s>). [NBs 49.81]
He who has no purpose in what is done or not done, who has no refuge anywhere —
the Charioteer of <s>Pārtha</s> says: 'He is [seemingly] worthless, [yet] a partaker of pure liberation.' [NBs 49.82]

children.text: dharmādharmau na jānāti na jānāti śubhāśubhe /
children.translated_text: He knows neither <s>dharma</s> nor <s>adharma</s>, he knows neither the auspicious nor the inauspicious,

children.text: sukhaduḥkhe na jānāti sa jñānīti mataṃ hareḥ // NBs_49.83 //
children.translated_text: he knows neither pleasure nor pain — he is a knower: this is the view of <s>Hari</s>. [NBs 49.83]
Everywhere it is described that liberation comes through contemplation alone;

children.text: asmākaṃ tu mate svasminna kiñcidapi cintayet // NBs_49.84 //
children.translated_text: but in our view, one should not contemplate anything whatsoever about one's own self. [NBs 49.84]
Contemplation is the view of all scriptures; my view is different —

children.text: na kiñciccintanādeva svayaṃ tattvaṃ prakāśate // NBs_49.85 //
children.translated_text: through not contemplating anything at all, the truth shines forth of itself. [NBs 49.85]
When the truth has shone forth of itself, at that very moment one becomes identical with it;

children.text: eko'pi na guṇo yasmindvau trayo vā kutaḥ kila /
children.translated_text: not even one quality exists in him — how then two or three?

children.text: guṇāngāyati govindo nistraiguṇyasya tasya hi // NBs_49.86 //
children.translated_text: <s>Govinda</s> sings of qualities for that one who is beyond the three <s>guṇas</s>. [NBs 49.86]
He who has no qualification whatsoever in any action —

children.text: mukhyo'dhikārī kaivalye sa gīto nandasūnunā // NBs_49.87 //
children.translated_text: he is the primary qualified person for <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation): so it is sung by the Son of <s>Nanda</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>). [NBs 49.87]
He who, while seeing, hearing, touching, and smelling, denies direct perception —

children.text: naiva kiñcitkaromīti tamāryaṃ prāha keśavaḥ // NBs_49.88 //
children.translated_text: 'I do not do anything at all' — <s>Keśava</s> calls him noble. [NBs 49.88]
Those who, though knowing the true path, teach the deluded [a wrong path],
and praise the path of the deluded — <s>Mādhava</s> called them 'saintly.' [NBs 49.89]
That path upon entering which, even if one falls, in the next birth
[one continues] — that very path of the <s>yogins</s> was praised by the Charioteer of <s>Pārtha</s>. [NBs 49.90]
For <s>haṭha-yogins</s>, the restraint of all voluntary activity grants attainment;
for us, the <s>jñāna-yogins</s> (yogins of knowledge), voluntary activity is itself <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation). [NBs 49.91]

children.text: hatvā'pi ya imāllokānna hanti na nibadhyate /
children.translated_text: 'Even having slain all these people, he does not slay and is not bound' —

children.text: asmākaṃ tu mate tasya saṅgatiḥ śāntisādhanam // NBs_49.92 //
children.translated_text: in our view, association with such a person is the means to peace. [NBs 49.92]

children.text: jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyurdhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca /
children.translated_text: 'For the born, death is certain; for the dead, birth is certain' —
the remedy for this unavoidable [cycle] is my teaching. [NBs 49.93]
He whose fire of knowledge reduces all actions to ashes —

children.text: na tasya karmabhraṣṭasya karmaṭhairlabhyate padam // NBs_49.94 //
children.translated_text: the state of that one, fallen from action, cannot be attained by the ritualists. [NBs 49.94]
He who, though a [seemingly] worthless person, has gone forth from everything out of desire [for the Self] —

children.text: sa eva puruṣārthīti jagāda puruṣottamaḥ // NBs_49.95 //
children.translated_text: 'He alone is the seeker of the supreme human goal' — so said the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>). [NBs 49.95]
I have studied the <s>Viṣṇu-gītā</s>; the conclusion that emerged there is:
he who abandons all <s>dharmas</s> is freed from all sins. [NBs 49.96]
This babble, though connected, is about the subject of non-attachment;
when meditated upon again and again, it would grant the saintly ones complete non-attachment. [NBs 49.97]
In the inquiry into the imperceptible, this century [of verses], which proceeds by the censurable path of desire and the like,
manifestly has the nature of a madman's babble. [NBs 49.98]
O child, do not disregard this because of its nature as a madman's babble;
surely its inner meaning is difficult to understand for those attached to sense-objects. [NBs 49.99]

body.text: ityunmattapralāpo'yaṃ nāmnā prokto mayā tava // NBs_49.100 //
body.translated_text: Thus this 'Madman's Babble' has been proclaimed by me to you by name. [NBs 49.100]

children.translated_text: Surely by one of exclusive devotion, with a constantly one-pointed mind,
this 'Madman's Babble' should be investigated by one of accomplished intellect. [NBs 49.101]
Those of great intellect who are 'mad' with the state of the mind-transcending (<s>manonmanī</s>) —
this babble is their treasure, to be installed in the temple of the heart. [NBs 49.102]
The Century of <s>Śiva</s>-Worship (<s>Śivapūjāśatakam</s>)
The action that consists of <s>Śiva</s>-worship is capable of uprooting all action;
the intention (<s>saṅkalpa</s>) of <s>Śiva</s>-worship removes the suffering of all intentions. [NBs 50.1]
The initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) of the five-syllabled [mantra] of <s>Śiva</s>, consisting of the Word-<s>Brahman</s>, is beneficial;
one who is proficient in the Word-<s>Brahman</s> attains the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. [NBs 50.2]
The three lines of <s>vibhūti</s> (sacred ash) are faith, devotion, and dispassion;
they should be worn on one's body by the devotees of <s>Śambhu</s>, for the purpose of attaining the qualification for worship. [NBs 50.3]
The ornaments of <s>Rudra</s> — the <s>mudrās</s> and <s>rudrākṣa</s> rosaries — should be worn;

children.text: devo bhūtvā yajeddevamitīyaṃ śāśvatī śrutiḥ // NBs_50.4 //
children.translated_text: 'Having become God, one should worship God' — this is the eternal <s>Śruti</s> (scripture). [NBs 50.4]
Now the order of worship:
In that [<s>Māyā</s>] in which forms — <s>Brahmā</s> and the rest, moving and unmoving — are conceived,
a <s>Śivaliṅga</s> made of that very clay is worshipped by the devotees of <s>Śiva</s>. [NBs 50.5]

children.text: tatra prathamaṃ harāya nama iti mṛttikāgrahaṇam |
children.translated_text: First, 'Salutation to <s>Hara</s>' — the taking up of clay:
The clay from whose potsherds crores of cosmic eggs (<s>brahmāṇḍas</s>) are heard of in truth —

children.text: harāya nama ityeva grāhyā sā mṛttikā budhaiḥ // NBs_50.6 //
children.translated_text: that clay should be taken up by the wise with [the mantra] 'Salutation to <s>Hara</s>.' [NBs 50.6]
'Salutation to <s>Maheśvara</s>' — the shaping of the <s>liṅga</s>:
The unbroken, all-encompassing mental modification (<s>akhaṇḍākāravṛtti</s>) that is described in <s>Vedānta</s> —

children.text: namo maheśvarāyeti liṅgasaṅghaṭṭanaṃ hi tat // NBs_50.7 //
children.translated_text: 'Salutation to <s>Maheśvara</s>' — that indeed is the shaping of the <s>liṅga</s>. [NBs 50.7]
'Salutation to the Trident-bearer' — the installation:
Having abandoned the impossibility [of realization] and likewise the contemplation of the opposite,

children.text: śulapāṇiḥ pratiṣṭhāpyaḥ pīṭhe niṣṭhāmaye budhaiḥ // NBs_50.8 //
children.translated_text: the Trident-bearer should be installed by the wise on the pedestal made of firm conviction. [NBs 50.8]
'Salutation to the Bearer of <s>Pināka</s>' — the invocation:
Though the God is all-pervading, Your devotion is the invocation;
'I invoke You with devotion' — thus the Bearer of <s>Pināka</s> is to be invoked. [NBs 50.9]

body.text:
atha dhyānam |
dhyāyennityaṃ maheśaṃ rajatagirinibhaṃ cārucandrāvataṃsaṃ ratnākalpojjvalāṅgaṃ paraśumṛgavarābhītihastaṃ prasannam /
padmāsīnaṃ samantātstutamamaragaṇairvyāghrakṛttiṃ vasānaṃ viśvādyaṃ viśvavandyaṃ nikhilabhayaharaṃ pañcavaktraṃ trinetram// NBs_50.10 //
body.translated_text: Now the meditation: One should always meditate on <s>Maheśa</s> (the great Lord) — resembling a silver mountain, with the beautiful crescent moon as his crest-ornament, his body brilliant with jeweled ornaments, holding an axe, a deer, the boon-granting and fear-dispelling [hands], gracious, seated in the lotus-posture, praised on all sides by hosts of gods, wearing a tiger-skin, the origin of the universe, worshipped by the universe, the remover of all fear, five-faced, three-eyed. [NBs 50.10]

children.translated_text: Now the commentary on this:
Commentary on the first three words 'one should meditate' and so forth:

children.text: anitye nityaṃ virasā nitye nityaṃ dhṛtavratāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those of firm vow, [finding the] non-eternal tasteless [and the] eternal [delightful], always meditate —
those who discriminate between the eternal and the non-eternal always meditate on <s>Maheśa</s>. [NBs 50.11]
Now the commentary on 'resembling a silver mountain':

children.text: rajatasya giriḥ śaṃbhuḥ śāmbhavānāṃ paraṃ dhanam /
children.translated_text: The mountain of silver is <s>Śambhu</s> — the supreme wealth of the devotees of <s>Śambhu</s>;

children.text: dhanena tena pūrṇānāṃ daridratvaṃ na vidyate // NBs_50.12 //
children.translated_text: for those who are full of that wealth, there is no poverty. [NBs 50.12]
Now the commentary on 'with the beautiful crescent moon as crest-ornament':

children.text: śuddhātmā śītalā kāntā sūkṣmā bodhakalā parā /
children.translated_text: The pure Self, cool, beautiful, subtle, the supreme digit of knowledge —

children.text: vakrāyate durāpeyaṃ candracūḍo vibharti tām // NBs_50.13 //
children.translated_text: though it appears curved and difficult to attain, the Moon-crested one bears it. [NBs 50.13]
Now, the explanation of "whose limbs shine with jeweled ornaments":
Certain jewels of knowledge, which are themselves the <s>yoga</s>-initiation,
are worn by <s>Śaṅkara</s> — hence his limbs shine with jeweled ornaments. [NBs 50.14]
Now, the explanation of "axe in hand":
By which the forest of delusion is cut down and never sprouts again —

children.text: sa bodhaḥ paraśustīkṣṇo haste rudrasya varttate // NBs_50.15 //
children.translated_text: that sharp axe, which is knowledge, is in the hand of <s>Rudra</s>. [NBs 50.15]
Now, the explanation of "deer in hand":

children.text: dhartuṃ na śakyate dhīrairyo dhṛto'pi palāyate /
children.translated_text: That which cannot be held by even the steadfast, and even when held, runs away —

children.text: līlayaiva dhṛto haste śambhunā sa manomṛgaḥ // NBs_50.16 //
children.translated_text: that deer, the mind, is held in hand by <s>Śambhu</s> with ease. [NBs 50.16]
Now, the explanation of the truth of "boon-granting hand":

children.text: varārthibhirvareṇyāya vṛto yaistu varaḥ sa tam /
children.translated_text: That which is chosen by seekers of boons as the most excellent [boon-giver],

children.text: varaṃ dadāti hastena varadastena śaṃkaraḥ // NBs_50.17 //
children.translated_text: grants the boon with his hand — therefore <s>Śaṅkara</s> is the boon-granter. [NBs 50.17]
Now, the explanation of the truth of "fear-removing hand":
Even <s>Brahmā</s> fears death; death indeed is the great fear.
Therefore, freedom from death and fearlessness are in the hand of <s>Mṛtyuñjaya</s> (the Conqueror of Death). [NBs 50.18]
Now, the explanation of "benevolent":
Having attained even a single <s>siddhi</s> (perfection), some become internally pleased.

children.text: nidhānaṃ sarvasiddhīnāṃ prasannaḥ sarvadā haraḥ // NBs_50.19 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hara</s>, who is the treasure-house of all <s>siddhis</s>, is always benevolent. [NBs 50.19]
Now, the explanation of "seated in lotus-posture":
Since <s>Sadāśiva</s> is seated in the lotus-hearts of the virtuous,

children.text: ata eva hi vedeṣu padmāsīna itīritaḥ // NBs_50.20 //
children.translated_text: therefore he is called "seated in lotus-posture" (<s>padmāsīna</s>) in the <s>Vedas</s>. [NBs 50.20]
Now, the explanation of "praised on all sides by the hosts of gods":
Humans praise the gods; the gods [praise] the lords of the gods;
the god of gods, <s>Mahādeva</s>, is praised by the lords of the gods. [NBs 50.21]
Now, the explanation of "wearing a tiger-skin":
By <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the hunter, the tiger of delusion was slain.

children.text: kaṭau kṛttisvarūpeṇa paśya tasya nidarśanam // NBs_50.22 //
children.translated_text: See its evidence — [the tiger-skin] in the form of a hide at his waist. [NBs 50.22]
Now, the explanation of "the first of the universe, worshipped by the universe":
He is the creator of the universe, of universal form, the destroyer of the universe, the protector of the universe,
the first of the universe, worshipped by the universe — <s>Viśveśa</s>, the lord of <s>Girijā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>). [NBs 50.23]
Now, the explanation of "remover of all fear":
The <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) says "fear" — "from the second, indeed, fear arises."

children.text: haro harati bhaktānāṃ muktido nikhilaṃ bhayam // NBs_50.24 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hara</s>, the granter of liberation, removes all fear of his devotees. [NBs 50.24]
Now, the explanation of "five-faced":
His devotees meditate [on him] everywhere; he faces all of them.

children.text: unmukho vimukhānāṃ yastasya sā pañcavaktratā // NBs_50.25 //
children.translated_text: He who faces even those who turn away — that is his five-facedness. [NBs 50.25]
Now, the explanation of "three-eyed":

children.text: karmopāstī ubhe netre jñānaṃ netraṃ tṛtīyakam /
children.translated_text: Ritual action (<s>karma</s>) and meditation (<s>upāsti</s>) are the two eyes; knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) is the third eye.

children.text: lalāṭe rājate yasya trinetrastena śaṅkaraḥ // NBs_50.26 //
children.translated_text: That which shines on the forehead — by that, <s>Śaṅkara</s> is three-eyed. [NBs 50.26]

body.translated_text: Thus ends the meditation [section].

children.translated_text: Now, the examination of the accessories.
First, the examination of "resembling pure crystal":
In the pure one, all this is reflected;
resembling pure crystal, free from attachment — that is this Lord. [NBs 50.27]
Now, the examination of "camphor-white":
By whose fragrance (i.e., the fragrance of desirelessness), all evil desires have departed,
naturally cool — that is the camphor-whiteness of <s>Śiva</s>. [NBs 50.28]
Now, the examination of "sky-clad" (<s>digambara</s>):
<s>Hara</s> himself is of the nature of uncovered knowledge.

children.text: svairaṃ carati saṃsāre tena prokto digambaraḥ // NBs_50.29 //
children.translated_text: He moves freely in <s>saṃsāra</s> — therefore he is called sky-clad. [NBs 50.29]
Now, the examination of the smearing with ashes:
The fire of knowledge reduces all <s>karmas</s> to ashes.
With that very ash, <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) smears his body. [NBs 50.30]
In ash, there is no distinction among differentiated things — it shines [uniformly].
By its very own nature, ash is dear to <s>Bharga</s> (<s>Śiva</s>). [NBs 50.31]
Now, the examination of "crescent-crowned":

children.text: naśyantyasya kalāḥ sarvāḥ sā kalā naiva naśyati /
children.translated_text: All the digits [of the moon] perish, but that one digit never perishes

children.text: yā'rpitā śaṅkare bhaktyā candracūḍastayā haraḥ // NBs_50.32 //
children.translated_text: which is offered to <s>Śaṅkara</s> with devotion — by that, <s>Hara</s> is crescent-crowned. [NBs 50.32]
Now, the examination of the matted locks:
<s>Hara</s> is the ancient banyan tree, the resting place of the greatest sages.
The three [systems] known as <s>Vedānta</s>, <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, and <s>Yoga</s> are remembered as his three matted locks. [NBs 50.33]
Now, the examination of being the bearer of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>:

children.text: brahmalokā ca yā gaṅgā suṣumṇā śītaladravā /
children.translated_text: The <s>Gaṅgā</s> from the world of <s>Brahmā</s> — the cool-flowing <s>Suṣumnā</s> [channel] —

children.text: mastake rājate yasya tena gaṅgādharo haraḥ // NBs_50.34 //
children.translated_text: shines on the head of him by whom <s>Hara</s> is the bearer of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. [NBs 50.34]
Now, the examination of three-eyedness:
The one that nourishes is <s>Soma</s> (moon); the one that destroys darkness is <s>Sūrya</s> (sun); the one that burns faults with knowledge is <s>Agni</s> (fire).
Having <s>Soma</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, and <s>Agni</s> as eyes — by that, <s>Śaṅkara</s> is three-eyed. [NBs 50.35]
Now, the examination of being blue-throated:
In the throat, the shadows of the many swallowed cosmic spaces —
[their reflections] in [his body] that resembles crystal — that is the cause of his blue-throatedness. [NBs 50.36]
The dark space of the cosmic body situated in the throat region

children.text: kaṇṭhadeśe sthitaṃ vyoma nīlakaṇṭhastato haraḥ // NBs_50.37 //
children.translated_text: of the lord of <s>Pārvatī</s> — therefore <s>Hara</s> is blue-throated. [NBs 50.37]
By <s>Śaṅkara</s>, who is cloud-white, the water of poison was compassionately
held in the throat — therefore his throat is beautiful like a fresh rain-cloud. [NBs 50.38]
Resembling pure crystal, he stands on Mount <s>Mandara</s>.
The shadow of the sapphire mountain — that is the cause of his blue-throatedness. [NBs 50.39]
<s>Rāma</s> is his supreme devotee; <s>Śaṅkara</s> is affectionate toward his devotees.
The gem of <s>Rāma</s> is worn at the throat — that is the cause of his blue-throatedness. [NBs 50.40]
Now, the examination of being adorned with serpents:
Yogins who subsist on air and who sleep in mountain-caves —
held in his own form by him — therefore <s>Hara</s> is adorned with serpents. [NBs 50.41]
A certain <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> power was brought under control by <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Through <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>, the serpents have become the ornaments of his body. [NBs 50.42]
<s>Ananta</s> and <s>Vāsuki</s> have become the ear-ornaments of <s>Śambhu</s>.
By their preeminence, others too are known by the name "serpent-ornaments." [NBs 50.43]
Now, the examination of the trident:
With the three sharp points called peace (<s>śānti</s>), dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), and knowledge (<s>bodha</s>),
the three-eyed one destroys the three-citied [demon] of the three <s>guṇas</s> with the trident. [NBs 50.44]
Now, the examination of the <s>ḍamaru</s> (hand-drum):
Under the pretext of the "ṭaṇ-ṭaṅ" sound, for the sake of the liberation of <s>Śaiva</s> devotees,

children.text: neti neti muhuḥ prāha ḍamaruḥ śāmbhavo hi saḥ // NBs_50.45 //
children.translated_text: it repeatedly declares "not this, not this" (<s>neti neti</s>) — that <s>ḍamaru</s> is indeed <s>Śambhu's</s>. [NBs 50.45]
Now, the examination of the garland of skulls:
In wearing the garland of skulls of infinite dead cosmic-eggs,
only <s>Śiva</s> is capable, because of his beginningless and endless nature. [NBs 50.46]
Now, the examination of the bull-mount:
That [stage of <s>samādhi</s>] upon which <s>Brahmā</s> and the rest have not mounted — <s>Śaṅkara</s> mounts it:
the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>dharmamegha</s> (cloud of dharma) — therefore he has the bull as his vehicle. [NBs 50.47]
Now, the examination of <s>Kailāsa</s>:
<s>Rudra</s> shines in <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute isolation/liberation), and his devotees too, always.
Through the play of that <s>kaivalya</s>, <s>Kailāsa</s> is the abode of <s>Śambhu</s>. [NBs 50.48]
Now, the examination of <s>Mandara</s>:
That by which this ocean of existence was churned for the sake of the jewel of liberation —

children.text: sa bodho mandaro nāma mandiraṃ śaṅkarasya tat // NBs_50.49 //
children.translated_text: that knowledge, named <s>Mandara</s>, is the abode of <s>Śaṅkara</s>. [NBs 50.49]
Now, the examination of the cremation ground:
Where this one, the <s>Bhairava</s> of dissolution, constantly plays —

children.text: tatra śmaśāne saṃsāre śivaḥ sarvatra dṛśyate // NBs_50.50 //
children.translated_text: in that cremation ground, which is <s>saṃsāra</s>, <s>Śiva</s> is seen everywhere. [NBs 50.50]
Now, the examination of the <s>gaṇas</s> (attendants):
<s>Śambhu</s> is the ocean of bliss; his <s>śakti</s> (power) is called the flowing [water].
Like drops of the ocean, those particles of his bliss are the <s>gaṇas</s>. [NBs 50.51]
The Lord is distinct from the world in his own form, nature, and marks.
That his <s>gaṇas</s> too are distinct from the world — what is surprising about that? [NBs 50.52]
Now, the examination of the <s>yoginī</s>-host:
Whatever mental modification of yogins, through the practice of <s>yoga</s>,

children.text: sā samīpaṃ gatā śambhoḥ saivāyaṃ yoginīgaṇaḥ // NBs_50.53 //
children.translated_text: has approached <s>Śambhu</s> — that itself is this host of <s>yoginīs</s>. [NBs 50.53]
The companions of <s>Śaṅkara</s> — the <s>yoginīs</s>, <s>Bhairavas</s>, and the rest —
are the <s>jīvanmuktas</s> (liberated while living), called by the ignorant "ghosts, spirits, and ghouls." [NBs 50.54]
Now, the examination of <s>Kālabhairava</s>:
Time (<s>Kāla</s>), which has projected the net of the world, is his doorkeeper.

children.text: kālādbibheti yadviśvaṃ sa gaṇaḥ kālabhairavaḥ // NBs_50.55 //
children.translated_text: The universe fears time — that <s>gaṇa</s> is <s>Kālabhairava</s>. [NBs 50.55]
Now, the examination of <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> (the staff-bearer):
Through the punishment of the mind alone, one becomes a <s>gaṇa</s> named <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s>.

children.text: tādṛśā eva devasya gaṇatvamupayānti hi // NBs_50.56 //
children.translated_text: Indeed, such ones attain the status of <s>gaṇas</s> of the Lord. [NBs 50.56]
Now, the examination of the <s>kṣetrapālas</s> (field-guardians):
The Supreme Self is <s>Śambhu</s> himself; his portions are the <s>kṣetrapālas</s>.
Through the distinction of part and whole, <s>Hara</s> is surrounded by <s>kṣetrapālas</s>. [NBs 50.57]
Now, the examination of <s>Nandi</s>-<s>gaṇa</s>:
That upon which the Supreme Lord appears in resplendent form —

children.text: sa bodhaḥ śuddhabhāvātmā gīyate nandikeśvaraḥ // NBs_50.58 //
children.translated_text: that knowledge, of the nature of pure being, is celebrated as <s>Nandikeśvara</s>. [NBs 50.58]
Now, the examination of <s>Bhṛṅgi</s>:
The devotee who, through the wasp-and-caterpillar process, has attained the same form [as the Lord] —

children.text: sa eva khaṇḍaparaśorbhṛṅgināmā gaṇaḥ kila // NBs_50.59 //
children.translated_text: he is indeed the <s>gaṇa</s> named <s>Bhṛṅgi</s> of the <s>Khaṇḍaparaśu</s> (axe-wielding one, <s>Śiva</s>). [NBs 50.59]
Now, the examination of <s>Mahākāla</s>:

children.text: kālena bhakṣitaṃ viśvaṃ kālo bodhena bhakṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The universe was devoured by Time; Time was devoured by Knowledge.

children.text: bodhātmā kālakālo'yaṃ mahākālo paro gaṇaḥ // NBs_50.60 //
children.translated_text: This one, whose nature is knowledge, the death of Death — this supreme <s>gaṇa</s> is <s>Mahākāla</s>. [NBs 50.60]
Now, the examination of <s>Skanda</s>:
He by whom, with the army of knowledge, the routing (<s>skandana</s>) of delusion was accomplished —

children.text: sa buddhimānmahāsenaḥ skando nāma śivātmajaḥ // NBs_50.61 //
children.translated_text: that intelligent one, <s>Mahāsena</s> (the great general), named <s>Skanda</s>, is the son of <s>Śiva</s>. [NBs 50.61]
Now, the examination of <s>Gaṇeśa</s>:
The other son, the destroyer of hosts of obstacles, skilled in all knowledge,
with a belly swollen with bliss, is verily the bestower of <s>siddhis</s> — <s>Gaṇeśvara</s>. [NBs 50.62]
Now, the examination of <s>Śivarātri</s>:

children.text: yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgartti saṃyamī /
children.translated_text: "That which is night for all beings — in that, the self-controlled one is awake."
He who is awake on <s>Śivarātri</s> — <s>Śiva</s> is pleased with him. [NBs 50.63]
The five organs of action and the five organs of knowledge,
mind, ego, and <s>citta</s> — three — and <s>buddhi</s> is the fourteenth. [NBs 50.64]
This is declared by <s>Śaivas</s> as the fourteenth [day] of <s>Śivarātri</s>.
Through fasting there, the wise one should become a restrainer of mental modifications. [NBs 50.65]
Performed first by the devotees of <s>Śiva</s>, it is supremely dear to <s>Śiva</s>.
This <s>Śivarātri</s>, O son, bestows union with <s>Śiva</s>. [NBs 50.66]

children.text: niśītha eva madhyāhno rātrireva dinaṃ vibhoḥ /
children.translated_text: Midnight itself is midday; night itself is the day of the Lord.

children.text: na yatra kiñcitkāśeta sa prakāśastu śāmbhavaḥ // NBs_50.67 //
children.translated_text: Where nothing shines [i.e., the external world] — that radiance is <s>Śambhu's</s>. [NBs 50.67]
Now, the examination of <s>Śiva's</s> cosmic dance (<s>tāṇḍava</s>):
By whose blissful dissolution, <s>Nārada</s> and the others were delighted —
know that bliss-sport as <s>Śambhu's</s> <s>tāṇḍava</s>. [NBs 50.68]
Now, the examination of being the slayer of <s>Smara</s> (Love):

children.text: hṛte smare hṛtā eva ṣaḍapyete smarādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: When <s>Smara</s> (desire) is slain, these six too — beginning with <s>Smara</s> — are slain.
Because of the slaying of desire and the rest, the Lord, <s>Hara</s>, is the slayer of <s>Smara</s>. [NBs 50.69]
Now, the examination of <s>Gaurī</s>:
She is by nature contrary [to the world], beyond the reach of mind and speech.

children.text: vāmāṅgī vāmadevasya vāme gaurī virājate // NBs_50.70 //
children.translated_text: As the left-body of <s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Gaurī</s> shines on the left. [NBs 50.70]
She is the foremost among those who discourse on <s>Brahman</s> — <s>Bhavānī</s>, the speaker of <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: yā kaṭākṣeṇa sarvatra śivākhyaṃ brahma vīkṣate // NBs_50.71 //
children.translated_text: who, with a sidelong glance, beholds <s>Brahman</s> called <s>Śiva</s> everywhere. [NBs 50.71]

children.text: mama priyo mama svāmī mamā''ttmā me gṛheśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: "My beloved, my lord, my self, the master of my home" —

children.text: iti yasyāḥ śive bhāvaḥ sā dhanyā śailakanyakā // NBs_50.72 //
children.translated_text: she whose devotion to <s>Śiva</s> is of this nature, that blessed daughter of the mountain. [NBs 50.72]

children.text: sa īkṣitaḥ sa āśliṣṭaḥ sa bhuktaḥ sa ca pūjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: He is gazed upon, he is embraced, he is enjoyed, he is worshipped;

children.text: sa eva hṛdaye dhyātaḥ pārvatyā parameśvaraḥ // NBs_50.73 //
children.translated_text: he alone is meditated upon in the heart by <s>Pārvatī</s> — the Supreme Lord. [NBs 50.73]
<s>Pārvatī</s> worships <s>Śiva</s> with devotion and wifely fidelity (<s>pātivratya</s>).

children.text: ataḥ saubhāgyametasyā loke vede ca gīyate // NBs_50.74 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, her good fortune is celebrated in the world and in the <s>Vedas</s>. [NBs 50.74]
This <s>yoga</s> of the lords of <s>yoga</s>, by which the Great Lord is enjoyed —

children.text: tena yogena sampannā bhavānī divyayoginī // NBs_50.75 //
children.translated_text: endowed with that <s>yoga</s>, <s>Bhavānī</s> is the divine <s>yoginī</s>. [NBs 50.75]
The Supreme Lord constantly dances before <s>Pārvatī</s>.

children.text: yadantastādṛśaṃ prema tadagre kiṃ na nṛtyatu // NBs_50.76 //
children.translated_text: When such love exists within, why should he not dance before her? [NBs 50.76]
Endowed with the unity of self, yet appearing as two distinct selves,
I bow to <s>Bhavānī</s> and <s>Śaṅkara</s>, like a knower of <s>Brahman</s> and <s>Brahman</s> [itself]. [NBs 50.77]
<s>Pārvatī</s> is worthy of praise in two ways.

children.text: yadasyāḥ śaṅkare prema yadasyāṃ prema śāṅkaram // NBs_50.78 //
children.translated_text: Such is the love she has for <s>Śaṅkara</s>, and such is <s>Śaṅkara</s>'s love for her. [NBs 50.78]
<s>Pārvatī</s> is to be worshipped even more than <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
for she increases the bliss of him who is himself the very form of bliss. [NBs 50.79]
<s>Pārvatī</s> is verily the form of the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — there is no doubt in this.
For the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, has abundant love for her. [NBs 50.80]

children.text: mandārāstaravo vaneṣu parikhātoyaṃ sudhāsāgaro dvārepyaṣṭavibhūtayo nidhigaṇairantaḥpure pārvatī /
children.translated_text: <s>Mandāra</s> trees in the groves, the ocean of nectar as a moat, the eight powers (<s>aṣṭa-vibhūti</s>) at the gate, <s>Pārvatī</s> in the inner chamber with hosts of treasures,

children.text: śūlaṃ śastravaraṃ vṛṣaḥ priyasakhā nāraḥ kapālaḥ kare graiveyaṃ garalaṃ bhujeṣu bhujagā bhasmāṅgarāge ruciḥ // NBs_50.81 //
children.translated_text: the trident as the best of weapons, the bull as a dear companion, a human skull in the hand, a garland of poison around the neck, serpents on the arms, and a fondness for ashes as bodily adornment. [NBs 50.81]

Conquering the radiance of a hundred moons and suns, resplendent with the crescent moon as a crest-jewel, wearing matted locks from which the <s>Gaṅgā</s> is born, three-eyed, pure as the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: vāme bhūdharakanyakā sahacarī bhūtyā sadā'; laṃkṛtā svānandā śitikaṇṭhinī purabhido mūrttiḥ puraḥ sphūrjati // NBs_50.82 //
children.translated_text: with the daughter of the mountain as companion on the left, ever adorned with glory, self-blissful, the blue-throated one — the form of the destroyer of the cities shines forth! [NBs 50.82]

body.translated_text: Thus ends the meditation with its accessories.

children.translated_text: "Salutations to <s>Paśupati</s>" — this is the bathing.
The residual impression of the bound soul (<s>paśutva-vāsanā</s>) is to be abandoned by the stream of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> of knowledge,

children.text: pavitrayā śītalayā snāpyaḥ paśupatiḥ śivaḥ // NBs_50.83 //
children.translated_text: which is purifying and cooling — <s>Paśupati</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, is to be bathed [in it]. [NBs 50.83]
"Salutations to <s>Śiva</s>" — this is the worship.

children.text: śivo devaḥ śivo jīvaḥ śivādanyanna vidyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s> is God, <s>Śiva</s> is the individual soul; nothing other than <s>Śiva</s> exists.

children.text: evaṃ śive prakarttavyaṃ bhaktyā candanalepanam // NBs_50.84 //
children.translated_text: Thus, sandal-paste is to be applied to <s>Śiva</s> with devotion. [NBs 50.84]
Now, the unbroken rice grains (<s>akṣata</s>):
The devotee who worships becomes unimpaired (<s>akṣata</s>), and the deity himself is unimpaired.
Therefore, <s>Śiva</s> is to be worshipped with unbroken (<s>akṣata</s>) devotion and with unbroken rice grains. [NBs 50.85]
Now, the consideration of the <s>arka</s> flower:
The <s>arka</s> plant is named <s>Pāśupata</s>, and the Lord is fond of <s>Pāśupata</s>.

children.text: ataḥ pāśupatārkasya puṣpaṃ paśupateḥ priyam // NBs_50.86 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the flower of the <s>Pāśupata arka</s> is dear to <s>Paśupati</s>. [NBs 50.86]
A certain tree with pungent leaves, offered to <s>Girīśa</s> (Lord of the mountain) by a devotee,
being an illuminator and destroyer of darkness, attained the status of <s>arka</s> (sun-plant). [NBs 50.87]
The flower of this pungent-leaved [plant], offered by a devotee of <s>Śambhu</s>,

children.text: śambhunā svīkṛtaṃ tena sā jātā śivamallikā // NBs_50.88 //
children.translated_text: was accepted by <s>Śambhu</s>, and thereby it became the <s>Śiva-mallikā</s> (jasmine of Śiva). [NBs 50.88]
Now, the determination regarding the <s>dhattūra</s> plant:
By the grace of <s>Īśvara</s>, the world shines in a wondrous way.
Because of its qualities similar to his own, <s>dhattūra</s> is dear to <s>Śiva</s>. [NBs 50.89]
Through <s>unmanī</s> (transcendence of mind), he himself is intoxicated and intoxicates the devotees of <s>Śambhu</s>.

children.text: ata eva priyaṃ śambhoḥ puṣpamunmattasambhavam // NBs_50.90 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the flower born of the intoxicating [plant] is dear to <s>Śambhu</s>. [NBs 50.90]
The deception of this trickster — [yet] the all-pervading one is not tainted [by it].

children.text: ataḥ kitavadhūrttasya kaitavaṃ kusumaṃ priyam // NBs_50.91 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the deceptive flower of the rogue-plant is dear [to him]. [NBs 50.91]
<s>Kāma</s> and the other [passions] are great rogues who have deluded the three worlds.

children.text: tāndhūrtayati yo yuktyā sa dhūrto dhūrjaṭipriyaḥ // NBs_50.92 //
children.translated_text: He who outwits them through skillful means — that rogue is dear to <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (Śiva). [NBs 50.92]
The <s>dhūrta</s>-leaf offered to <s>Śaṅkara</s> bestows merit equal to gold.

children.text: anena hetunā jāto dhattūraḥ kanakāhvayaḥ // NBs_50.93 //
children.translated_text: For this reason, <s>dhattūra</s> has come to be called <s>Kanaka</s> (gold). [NBs 50.93]
Now, the determination regarding the <s>kaṇṭakārikā</s> (thorny nightshade):
If a devotee offers the activity of the mind to <s>Śaṅkara</s> with devotion,
even though thorny by nature, it becomes <s>akaṇṭakārikā</s> (thornless). [NBs 50.94]
Now, the consideration of the <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple):
The great sage <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>, by his nature of devotion to <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: tannāmnaiva priyaṃ śambhoḥ patraṃ śāṇḍilyasambhavam // NBs_50.95 //
children.translated_text: [established that] the leaf born of <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>'s [tree], bearing his very name, is dear to <s>Śambhu</s>. [NBs 50.95]
<s>Mahādeva</s>, whose form is the universe, is himself characterized as an actor (<s>śailūṣa</s>).

children.text: ataḥ śailūṣapatrāṇāṃ pūjayā sa prasīdati // NBs_50.96 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, he is pleased by the worship of <s>śailūṣa</s>-leaves (bilva). [NBs 50.96]
The fruit of human birth is the offering of <s>bilva</s> leaves to <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: ato nirūpito vṛkṣo bilvaḥ śrīphalasaṃjñayā // NBs_50.97 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>bilva</s> tree is designated by the name <s>Śrīphala</s> (auspicious fruit). [NBs 50.97]
Incense, lamp, food-offering, fruit, betel, and <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee) —

children.text: śivāya nama ityeva sarvamevāsya pūjanam // NBs_50.98 //
children.translated_text: "Salutations to <s>Śiva</s>" alone constitutes all of his worship. [NBs 50.98]
Among the branches of knowledge, the <s>Śruti</s> (Veda) is supreme; among the <s>Śrutis</s>, the <s>Rudraikādaśinī</s> (Rudra hymns).

children.text: tatra pañcākṣarī śreṣṭhā sā japyā śivatuṣṭaye // NBs_50.99 //
children.translated_text: Among those, the five-syllabled <s>mantra</s> (<s>Pañcākṣarī</s>) is the best — it should be recited for the satisfaction of <s>Śiva</s>. [NBs 50.99]
The seer, the seeing, and the seen — possessing this triad of leaves,

children.text: śive samarpyā cidrūpe prathamā bilvapatrikā // NBs_50.100 //
children.translated_text: the first <s>bilva</s>-leaf is to be offered to <s>Śiva</s>, who is of the form of consciousness. [NBs 50.100]
The doer, the deed, and the instrument — possessing this triad of leaves,

children.text: śive samarpyā cidrūpe dvitīyā bilvapatrikā // NBs_50.101 //
children.translated_text: the second <s>bilva</s>-leaf is to be offered to <s>Śiva</s>, who is of the form of consciousness. [NBs 50.101]
The enjoyer, the eating, and the enjoyed — consisting of this triad of leaves,

children.text: śive samarpyā cidrūpe tṛtīyā bilvapatrikā // NBs_50.102 //
children.translated_text: the third <s>bilva</s>-leaf is to be offered to <s>Śiva</s>, who is of the form of consciousness. [NBs 50.102]
<s>Bhūḥ</s> (earth), <s>Bhuvaḥ</s> (atmosphere), and <s>Svaḥ</s> (heaven) — consisting of this triad of leaves,

children.text: śive samarpyā cidrūpe caturthī bilvapatrikā // NBs_50.103 //
children.translated_text: the fourth <s>bilva</s>-leaf is to be offered to <s>Śiva</s>, who is of the form of consciousness. [NBs 50.103]
Waking, dream, and deep sleep — possessing this triad of leaves,

children.text: śive samarpyā cidrūpe pañcamī bilvapatrikā // NBs_50.104 //
children.translated_text: the fifth <s>bilva</s>-leaf is to be offered to <s>Śiva</s>, who is of the form of consciousness. [NBs 50.104]
The gross, the subtle, and that called causal — possessing this triad of leaves,

children.text: śive samarpyā cidrūpe ṣaṣṭhikā bilvapatrikā // NBs_50.105 //
children.translated_text: the sixth <s>bilva</s>-leaf is to be offered to <s>Śiva</s>, who is of the form of consciousness. [NBs 50.105]
Ignorance, worldly existence, and the individual soul — possessing this triad of leaves,

children.text: śive samarpyā cidrūpe saptamī bilvapatrikā // NBs_50.106 //
children.translated_text: the seventh <s>bilva</s>-leaf is to be offered to <s>Śiva</s>, who is of the form of consciousness. [NBs 50.106]
Creation, sustenance, and destruction — possessing this triad of leaves,

children.text: śive samarpyā cidrūpe hyaṣṭamī bilvapatrikā // NBs_50.107 //
children.translated_text: the eighth <s>bilva</s>-leaf is to be offered to <s>Śiva</s>, who is of the form of consciousness. [NBs 50.107]
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Rudra</s> — possessing this triad of leaves,

children.text: śive samarpyā cidrūpe navamī bilvapatrikā // NBs_50.108 //
children.translated_text: the ninth <s>bilva</s>-leaf is to be offered to <s>Śiva</s>, who is of the form of consciousness. [NBs 50.108]
<s>Tamas</s> (darkness), <s>Rajas</s> (passion), and <s>Sattva</s> (purity) — possessing this triad of leaves,

children.text: śive samarpyā cidrūpe daśamī bilvapatrikā // NBs_50.109 //
children.translated_text: the tenth <s>bilva</s>-leaf is to be offered to <s>Śiva</s>, who is of the form of consciousness. [NBs 50.109]
"Thou-ness," "I-ness," and "this-ness" — possessing this triad of leaves,

children.text: śive samarpyā cidrūpe rudrākhyā bilvapatrikā // NBs_50.110 //
children.translated_text: the <s>bilva</s>-leaf called <s>Rudra</s> (the eleventh) is to be offered to <s>Śiva</s>, who is of the form of consciousness. [NBs 50.110]
These eleven <s>bilva</s>-leaves pertaining to <s>Śambhu</s> have been described.

children.text: etābhirarcitaḥ śambhuḥ sadyo muktiṃ prayacchati // NBs_50.111 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śambhu</s>, worshipped with these, grants immediate liberation. [NBs 50.111]
Now, the worship of the eight forms (<s>aṣṭamūrti-pūjā</s>):

children.text: śarvo bhavo rudra ugro bhīmaḥ paśupatistathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Śarva</s>, <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Ugra</s>, <s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Paśupati</s>,
<s>Mahādeva</s>, and <s>Īśāna</s> — thus is the worship of the [eight] forms. [NBs 50.112]
The eight forms of <s>Prakṛti</s> are indeed the eight afflictions of the embodied being.
Clearly, through [worship of] the eight forms, the eight-formed one (<s>Aṣṭamūrti</s>) removes them. [NBs 50.113]
Now, the determination regarding circumambulation (<s>pradakṣiṇa</s>):
<s>Mahādeva</s> is limitless; even in a hundred <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: na syātpradakṣiṇaṃ tena śivasyārdhaṃ pradakṣiṇam // NBs_50.114 //
children.translated_text: a full circumambulation would not be possible — therefore, half a circumambulation for <s>Śiva</s>. [NBs 50.114]
Now, the consideration of the bell and musical instruments:

children.text: yathā svarūpaṃ devasya tathā vaktuṃ na śakyate /
children.translated_text: Just as the true nature of God cannot be expressed,

children.text: stutirvā gallavādyaṃ vā tena śambhordvayaṃ samam // NBs_50.115 //
children.translated_text: so praise or musical instruments — both are equal for <s>Śambhu</s>. [NBs 50.115]
Now, the consideration of salutation (<s>namaskāra</s>):
With a feeling overflowing with love, having fallen upon the ground like a staff,
<s>Mahādeva</s> should be saluted, for thereby the ego melts away. [NBs 50.116]
Now, the seeking of forgiveness:
Having attained a human birth, yet not having worshipped <s>Maheśvara</s>,
a great offense has been committed — one should repeatedly say, "Forgive me!" [NBs 50.117]
Now, the determination regarding the dismissal:
The dismissal of knower-ship, doer-ship, enjoyer-ship, individual-soul-ship, and so forth —
in this worship of <s>Śiva</s>, this alone constitutes the dismissal (<s>visarjana</s>). [NBs 50.118]
The four aims of human life (<s>puruṣārtha-catuṣṭayī</s>) come under the command [of this worship].

children.text: yato'syāḥ śivapūjāyā mahimā kena varṇyatām // NBs_50.119 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, who can describe the greatness of this worship of <s>Śiva</s>? [NBs 50.119]

children.text: tattvato yaḥ śivaṃ veda sa veda śivapūjanam /
children.translated_text: He who knows <s>Śiva</s> in truth — he knows the worship of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: kastattvataḥ śivaṃ veda ko veda śivapūjanam // NBs_50.120 //
children.translated_text: But who truly knows <s>Śiva</s>? Who [truly] knows the worship of <s>Śiva</s>? [NBs 50.120]
Praise of the <s>Bodhasāra</s>

children.text: ādau gurustavo yatra prānte ca śivapūjanam /
children.translated_text: That in which the praise of the <s>Guru</s> is at the beginning and the worship of <s>Śiva</s> at the end,

children.text: madhye mukundasmaraṇaṃ bodhasāraḥ sa uttamaḥ // NBs_51.1 //
children.translated_text: with the remembrance of <s>Mukunda</s> in the middle — that <s>Bodhasāra</s> is supreme. [NBs 51.1]
Having accomplished meaning, easily understood, endowed with many special qualities —

children.text: granthastvetāddṛśastāta na bhūto na bhaviṣyati // NBs_51.2 //
children.translated_text: O son, a treatise like this has never been before, nor shall it ever be. [NBs 51.2]

children.text: na stomi na ca nindāmi kathayāmi yathāsthitam /
children.translated_text: I neither praise nor blame; I state things as they are.
In each and every verse here, a definitive conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>) is declared. [NBs 51.3]
Just as the entirety of the macrocosm (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>) is reflected in each microcosm (<s>piṇḍa</s>),

children.text: tathā siddhāntasarvasvaṃ śloke śloke nirūpitam // NBs_51.4 //
children.translated_text: so the entirety of the established doctrine is reflected in each verse. [NBs 51.4]
A spade for uprooting ignorance, a fire for the forest of ignorance,
a tiger against the deer of ignorance, a lion against the elephant of ignorance. [NBs 51.5]
Poison for the serpent of ignorance, a blade for the throat of ignorance,
water for the salt of ignorance, a deluge for the ocean of ignorance. [NBs 51.6]
A thunderbolt for the mountain of ignorance, a <s>Śaṅkara</s> for the demon <s>Andhaka</s> of ignorance,
a <s>Govinda</s> for the <s>Kaṃsa</s> of ignorance, a fierce <s>Caṇḍikā</s> for the <s>Caṇḍa</s> of ignorance. [NBs 51.7]
A cooling moon for the burning of ignorance, a blazing sun for the darkness of ignorance —
such indeed is this <s>Bodhasāra</s>, an awakening from the dream of ignorance. [NBs 51.8]
Devotion to the <s>Bodhasāra</s>
The <s>Bodhasāra</s> is my <s>Guru</s>, for it bestows knowledge upon me.

children.text: śiṣyo me bodhasāro'yaṃ yamuddiśya vadāmyaham // NBs_52.1 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhasāra</s> is my disciple, for it is to this that I address my teachings. [NBs 52.1]

children.text: svāmī me bodhasāro'yaṃ māṃ pālayati yaḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhasāra</s> is my master, for it always protects me.

children.text: sevako bodhasāro me mama sevāṃ karoti yaḥ // NBs_52.2 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhasāra</s> is my servant, for it performs service to me. [NBs 52.2]
The <s>Bodhasāra</s> is my well-wisher, for it knows everything about me.

children.text: sakhā me bodhasāro'yaṃ yasmindṛṣṭe sukhaṃ mama // NBs_52.3 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhasāra</s> is my friend, for upon seeing it, I am happy. [NBs 52.3]
The <s>Bodhasāra</s> is my home, for it is where I truly dwell.

children.text: ārāmo bodhasāro me vihāro yatra māmakaḥ // NBs_52.4 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhasāra</s> is my garden, where my recreation takes place. [NBs 52.4]
The <s>Bodhasāra</s> is my beloved, embracing whom I fall asleep.

children.text: mano me bodhasāro'yaṃ mananaṃ yena jāyate // NBs_52.5 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhasāra</s> is my mind, for through it reflection arises. [NBs 52.5]
The <s>Bodhasāra</s> is my intellect, through which the supreme is understood.

children.text: cittaṃ me bodhasāro'yaṃ yena cetāmi tatpade // NBs_52.6 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhasāra</s> is my thought (<s>citta</s>), through which I become aware of that [supreme] state. [NBs 52.6]
The <s>Bodhasāra</s> is my ego — indeed, I am the <s>Bodhasāra</s> itself.

children.text: śarīraṃ bodhasāro me mamatā yatra bhūyasī // NBs_52.7 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhasāra</s> is my body, for which I have the greatest affection. [NBs 52.7]

children.text: prāṇo me bodhasāro'yaṃ mamatā yatra bhūyasī /
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhasāra</s> is my vital breath, for which I have the greatest affection.

children.text: jīvo me bodhasāro'yaṃ yena jīvāmyahaṃ sadā // NBs_52.8 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhasāra</s> is my life-force, for it is through it that I always live. [NBs 52.8]

children.text: īśvaro bodhasāro me yato muktiprado mama /
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhasāra</s> is my <s>Īśvara</s> (Lord), for it grants me liberation.

children.text: bodhasāraḥ paraṃ brahma bodhasārātparaṃ nahi // NBs_52.9 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhasāra</s> is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>; there is nothing beyond the <s>Bodhasāra</s>. [NBs 52.9]
For establishing authority:

children.text: upaniṣadi vane ye puṣpitā mantravṛkṣāḥ surabhikusumameṣāmekamekaṃ vivicya /
children.translated_text: In the forest of the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, there are flowering trees of <s>mantras</s>. Selecting each one of their fragrant blossoms,
for the attainment of the essence of equal flavor, <s>Narahari</s>, the wise one, has worshipped the <s>liṅga</s> of knowledge (<s>bodha-liṅga</s>) with these verbal flowers alone. [1]
Beneficial to the wise, following the tradition, a treasury of supreme bliss, the cause of freedom from delusion —

children.text: naraharivihito'yaṃ bodhavṛkṣasya toyaṃ kumativanakuṭhāraḥ paṭhyatāṃ bodhasāraḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: this <s>Bodhasāra</s>, composed by <s>Narahari</s>, is the water for the tree of knowledge, an axe for the forest of wrong understanding — let it be studied! [2]
For those initiated by <s>Gurus</s>, everything indeed is an offering to <s>Īśvara</s>.
But this <s>Bodhasāra</s> is the very self of the supreme Lord. [3]
